James Trafford has already been sold to Leeds, while Omar Marmoush, Rico Lewis and Savinho are others who spent much of Pep Guardiola’s final season on the periphery and could be sold.

Sports.title: Arsenal open talks with Bayer Leverkusen over deal for Jarell Quansah
Sports.content:
Arsenal have opened talks with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they intensify efforts to bring in cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber.

The England defender, who left Liverpool last summer for an initial £30m and was part of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad, has been identified as an ideal replacement for the France and Netherlands defenders, who will miss the start of the new season due to injury. While Quansah’s preferred position is in central defence, he was also deployed at right-back by Tuchel at the World Cup and was sent off in the last-16 victory over Mexico.

It is understood that Leverkusen are reluctant to sell the Warrington-born 23-year-old, who signed a five-year deal when he left Anfield last July, and would want at least €50m (£43m). Arsenal – who saw a bid of £30m for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected earlier in the window – are not thought to want to pay that much but now could test the German club’s resolve by submitting a similar offer. Liverpool had a €70m buyback option on Quansah but that has now expired.

Arsenal are still believed to be interested in Konsa, who also filled in at right-back for England during the World Cup but is better known as a central defender. Villa value the 28-year-old at £60m.

Mikel Arteta said this week that Saliba’s back injury would take “some time to heal” and he was unsure about when he would be available again. Arsenal also have concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that forced him to miss most of the run‑in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said after Arsenal’s friendly defeat by Borussia ­Dortmund last Sunday. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.”

Arsenal would still like to sign a new attacker before the end of the window and could allow Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to depart in order to free up more funds. ­Galatasaray have offered £38m for Martinelli, although the Brazil ­forward has turned down a move to Turkey. Napoli have shown an ­interest in Jesus.

Ethan Nwaneri could also be sold, with Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund among those who have been linked with the 19-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The future of Myles Lewis-Skelly is unclear after he was offered to Chelsea and Manchester United this week. Arteta refused to address the rumours after he scored in the friendly against Como – managed by Cesc Fábregas – on Wednesday.

“I’m not going to talk about speculation,” he said. “If there is speculation about our players, it’s a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Rangers and the paradox of a painful exit that boosts their trophy chances
Sports.content:
AND NOW FOR SOME PERSPECTIVE

All new managers want to hit the ground running. But landing with a dull thud has never been a barrier to future glory, certainly not at Ibrox. Take Graeme Souness, whose start as Rangers’ player-manager put the ‘pish’ in ‘inauspicious’. On his league debut, away to Hibs, he was sent off in the first half after a revenge attack on the wrong mullet. Rangers lost 2-1 and were beaten in the third game as well. Graeme out! Rangers won the League Cup and finished the season as champions for the first time in nine years.

Dick Advocaat had a similarly awkward start in 1998. In his first game, played at Tranmere’s Prenton Park, Rangers went 3-0 down to Shelbourne in the first leg of their Big Vase tie. They went through comfortably in the end but lost the first league game a few days later. Dic- Advocaat out! Rangers had to settle for a domestic treble that season. Different times, when toys were played with for more than a few seconds before being launched from the pram with maximum force, followed a few seconds later by a handful of freshly sourced excreta. In 2026, alas, hot air and horse pucky are an acceptable substitute for reasonable discourse. And so, after failing to win any of his first four games as Rangers manager, Derek McInnes is “out of his depth” and a “dead man walking”.

Que Sera, Sera? Eff that! Turns out the future is ours to see after four games, two of them in a competition Rangers had no chance of winning anyway. Football Daily hasn’t a clue if McInnes is up to the Brobdingnagian challenge of managing Rangers, one that most tea-timely newsletters don’t really understand. But we do know that a culture of self-fulfilling poppycock, where ostentatious negativity is football’s version of the fatberg and many people would rather be right than happy, is a stain on our daily bread.

That said, what a roflcopter of a start! Given the events of last season, it was never going to be an equanimity-cultivating experience for a new Rangers manager to see Russell Martin’s start and lower it. Rangers have one point from two league games and are out of Bigger Vase after the most costly 1-1 draw against Polish opposition on British soil since Brian Clough called somebody a clown. Paradoxically, the aggregate defeat to Jagiellonia Bialystok – and subsequent drop into Tin Pot – has increased Rangers’ chances of winning a trophy under McInnes. Time will tell whether those chances have increased from 0.0000001% to 0.0000002%, from 9% to 9.4% or from some other figure to some other figure. Right now, the supercomputers know, and the bairns in the prams certainly don’t.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 10: Fulham
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 15th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 11th

Prospects

Marco Silva cutting the cord after five years by the river came as little surprise. If his time at Craven Cottage was successful in re-establishing Fulham as a Premier League club, he rarely concealed his ambitions to manage in European competition. He was frequently explicit in his disappointment that the club’s ownership did not meet him halfway by funding a stronger squad. Silva’s powers of rebadging and replenishing talent will be missed now that he has decamped to Benfica. Under him, Fulham played entertaining football, a collection of ugly ducklings showing their renewed worth for a club that, despite falling short of European qualification, looked upwards rather than downwards at the relegation battle. They were often a pleasure to watch, and ornery opposition for all-comers.

Álvaro Arbeloa is a very different type of appointment, with far less experience than his predecessor in frontline coaching terms, even if he arrives with Real Madrid on his CV. His arrival, though, has opened up a working relationship with the Spanish aristos, Gonzalo García and César Palacios arriving to work with a coach who helped them through the ranks in Madrid. By little coincidence, all three share the same agency as their representatives. There have been links with Endrick and Thiago Pitarch, two further young Real jewels, leading to a sense of Fulham becoming some form of Madrileño nursery, a Santiago Bernabéu on Thames. Should that play out, it would represent another sea change.

Silva preferred to work with hard-bitten pros. A couple of his leading men, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, have departed. The latter played the best football of his career last season but, like his manager, got a better offer elsewhere, from Leeds. Fulham’s latest approach is to source young players and polish them up. Can they have the same successes as mid-tier peers such as Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth, where the approach is far more data-driven? Will supporters be looking upwards rather than downwards? A previously enigmatic club just got more enigmatic.

Off-field picture

In May, the club were runners-up at the football business awards, for stadium experience, as the Riverside Stand’s opulent hospitality completed its first full season in service. Fulham need the Riverside to deliver as a revenue stream, as financial results for the 2024-25 season showed a pre-tax loss for the year at £44.5m, and that was lowered by the sale of João Palhinha in July 2024. There has been no such windfall since. The Khan family ownership continues to back the club, its overall investment estimated at about £900m, with staff costs at 117% of turnover. Therein lies the reasoning behind Silva not receiving the backing he desired.

Owner-fan relationship

The most expensive season ticket at Craven Cottage comes in at £3,084 for access to the Riverside’s facilities, the highest in the Premier League. Shahid Khan and his son Tony, the vice-chair and director of football operations, are unpopular among committed supporters for price rises and pandering to tourism. Khan’s boat Kismet was named superyacht of the year in 2025, its main salon inspired by the Palace of Versailles, and can be chartered for more than $3m per week. Though the balance sheets confirm Khan’s outlay in funding a continued Premier League status, fans would prefer he recognised not everyone lives the high life.

The manager

Where Silva had an unremarkable playing career, Arbeloa featured among the elite, a World Cup and Champions League winner. He also had the ear of Florentino Pérez, the perennial Real Madrid president asking him to replace Xabi Alonso mid-season in the 2025-26 campaign. That did not pan out and he took his first job away from Madrid, where he was a well-regarded youth coach, in south-west London. Khan Sr’s comment that Arbeloa “believes in giving young players a chance” is pertinent for Fulham’s change in direction. Crucially, as befitting traditions at Craven Cottage, the new man from Salamanca believes in open, attacking football, offering some continuity from Silva’s reign.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García surges forward during Fulham’s Costa del Sol Trophy match against Málaga. Photograph: Joaquin Corchero/AFP7/Shutterstock

Gonzalo García’s reputation was made by his performances at last summer’s Club World Cup, where he won the tournament’s Golden Boot. Comparisons were made to Raúl, a considerable accolade at the Bernabéu. Goals followed in the Champions League against Juventus and Borussia Dortmund but García eventually lost out to the star system of Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé. His reputation in Spain is as a hard worker off the ball, necessary for a Premier League player. Last season, Rodrigo Muniz’s injuries meant the old soldier Jiménez shouldered the burden at centre-forward. García is younger and fresher but the hype surrounding his arrival gives him much to live up to.

Stat attack

Fulham had the oldest side in the Premier League last season, which may help explain why they had arguably the least intense press. Marco Silva’s side recorded the fewest high turnovers, which occur when a team recovers the ball to start a new open-play possession sequence in the final 40 metres of the pitch. Real Madrid are hardly known for being a high-pressing side but they comfortably outperformed Fulham on this metric. It will be fascinating to see how Arbeloa approaches this.

Set for a breakthrough

Jonah Kusi-Asare’s arrival last summer from Bayern Munich is further mining of a super-club’s youth department. Bayern inserted a buy-back clause for a player they picked up from AIK. The Sweden Under-21s player has been compared to Alexander Isak, and made seven substitute appearances last season – without scoring – before an initial loan became a permanent move. At 6ft 5in he offers a different profile of striker to García. Hayden Mullins, the former under-21 coach now Newport manager, saw the best of Kusi-Asare last season, the 18-year-old scoring five goals in six matches.

World Cup impact

García made his debut for Spain in a pre-World Cup friendly against Iraq but failed to make the eventual champions’ tournament squad. Antonee Robinson had a fine tournament for the USA until the co-hosts perished in the last 16 at the hands of a Belgium team featuring Timothy Castagne. Luc de Fougerolles, yet to play a Premier League game for Fulham, showed off teenage defensive talents in Canada’s run to the knockouts. To complete a successful quintet – saving the best till last? – Sander Berge had a fine tournament as Norway also reached the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: Tony Mowbray demands answers from PGMOL over late decision after storming down tunnel in disgust
Sports.content:
Tony Mowbray demands answers from PGMOL over late decision after storming down tunnel in disgust

Blackburn manager Tony Mowbray will speak to the PGMOL after Wolves snatched a 2-2 draw thanks to a controversial late penalty.

The 62-year-old was left furious as his side were denied an opening three points on Friday night by Raul Jimenez's last-gasp spot-kick.



5 A late penalty from Jimenez stole three points from Blackburn on Friday Credit: Getty

Jimenez scored on his return to Molineux in the third minute of stoppage time to claim a point for the relegated side against Blackburn.

Marshall Munetsi had put Wolves in front after 18 minutes, but goals from Sean McLoughlin and Andri Gudjohnsen turned things around for the visitors, who have been tipped for relegation this season.

They then managed to hold on to their lead for the entire second half, looking set to shock the former Premier League outfit.



However, in the dying seconds of the match, a cross struck Ryan Alebiosu, and the ball bounced back off his arm.

Referee Farai Hallam pointed to the penalty spot, with replays showing that Alebiosu was right on the edge of the box.



The Blackburn full-back's body was outside the area, but his arm seemed to have been inside, according to the officials.

The decision left manager Mowbray raging on the touchline, while Jimenez then went on to bring the game level.



Moments later, the full-time whistle blew and the points were shared, but Mowbray remained angry and stormed down the tunnel.

How did Mowbray react at full time?

During talkSPORT's commentary of the game, presenter Adrian Durham explained: "Tony Mowbray couldn't stop shaking his head after that penalty was given.

"He's shaking hands with the opposition's dugout and then gone straight down the tunnel.

5 Alebiosu blocked a cross with his arm and Wolves were awarded a penalty Credit: Sky Sports



5 The referee believed that the full-back's arm was inside the box Credit: Sky Sports

"[He] told one of his staff to take the players over to the fans away to our left. They've moved the away ends away to our left here, and he's gone straight down the tunnel to the dressing room.

"Tony Mowbray can't believe how that game has finished up."

What has Mowbray said about the penalty?

The Blackburn boss seemed to have calmed down by the time he spoke to the media post-match, but he still wasn't happy.

In fact, he admitted to talkSPORT that he will be going to speak to the PGMOL's Select Group 2 Manager, Kevin Friend, who oversees refereeing in the Championship, to question the decision.



“We’re obviously disappointed," Mowbray told talkSPORT. "Having watched the still back, when it hits his hand it looks as if it’s outside the box, the still I’ve just looked at.

"And I think we'll go and see Kevin Friend, who is here tonight, who is the assessor. We'll go and sit with the referee and see what he thought.

5 Mowbray was left furious by the decision to award a penalty for Wolves in added time Credit: Getty

5 The Blackburn boss wanted his players to get the win he believed they deserved Credit: Getty



“If it’s in the 93rd minute, you have to be 100 per cent sure. These lads train and work every day, this is their lives, this is what they do for a living and you have to get it right I think.

"And the still I've seen looks to me outside the box and yet there you go. He made the call, we have to live with it.

"At 2-2, would we have taken that before the game? I generally thought we could come here and win, but they are a decent side, a good side who play positional football."

Mowbray added: "I'm pleased for our supporters who made the trip today and that they saw a team fighting for the victory.



"And unfortunately it was taken away from us right at the death, but we put the point in the bag and we move on."

Blackburn have to settle for just the one point to start the season, but there were certainly some encouraging signs.

Next up for Rovers are Middlesbrough at Ewood Park next week, while Wolves travel to take on Preston North End.

Sports.title: Three Championship managers already under pressure as promotion and relegation predicted
Sports.content:
Three Championship managers already under pressure as promotion and relegation predicted

The Championship is widely regarded as the toughest league in the world - which means predicting it is even harder.

But thankfully, talkSPORT Breakfast host Jeff Stelling and EFL expert Adrian Clarke have as much experience as anyone of the second tier.



10 Coventry ended their 25-year absence from the Premier League in style by lifting the title last season Credit: Getty

The pair have run the rule over which teams are most likely to lift the title come May, and the ones who should already be fearing the drop.

Wolves were held to a 2-2 draw against Blackburn on Friday night in the opening game of the season.

And on Saturday, it's GameDay Live from 12pm, with Adrian Durham presenting commentary of Bolton's return to the Championship against Preston.



Then from 2.30pm on Saturday, all the goals as they go in from the EFL, while Middlesbrough against Lincoln can be found on talkSPORT 2 at 3 o'clock.

That's followed by Sheffield United against Birmingham at 5.30pm. And then on Sunday, more action for you.



Watford against Southampton at 1.30pm. Burnley against West Ham at 4pm, both on talkSPORT 2 - And the Championship weekend concludes with Cardiff against Wrexham at 8 o'clock on talkSPORT 2.

But without further ado, Stelling and Clarke have put their encyclopaedic knowledge of the EFL to good use below...



Champions

Jeff Stelling - Middlesbrough

Middlesbrough to win the league - 10/1

"I'm going to go for Middlesbrough to win the league," he told Gabby Agbonlahor on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"They have spent, Steve Gibson, I don't know where he keeps digging into his pockets, £36.5 million so far.

"A lot of money for the Championship. Will Lankshear, hopefully, will get goals for them.

"Radek Vítek, signed in goal from Manchester United; they've got a couple of Americans...Kyle Joseph, I think this will be Boro’s year; I like the manager. Kim Hellberg a lot as well."



10 Middlesbrough are amongst the promotion contenders ahead of the new season Credit: Getty

Adrian Clarke - West Ham

West Ham United to win the league - 5/4

EFL expert said on the talkSPORT Daily Podcast: "It could be quite a fun year for Jarrod Bowen, for the West Ham squad, for the West Ham supporters, because the last few seasons, it's been a bit miserable. They've lost a lot of games. It's been very, very flat.

"They've taken some absolute batterings. This time around, they could be the ones dishing it out. And as a player, I wouldn't be that upset to be a part of that. And I think it speaks volumes about Bowen's personality.

"And the thing is, if you're in the West Ham dressing room and you think, 'I wish I was in the Prem,' right, and then you look, and you see Jarrod Bowen next to you, you think, well, 'I can't ask to leave, can I?' If he's staying, I've got to stay.



"I think it has a knock-on effect for [Valentín] Castellanos, Pablo

and [James] Ward-Prowse and others, I think, you know, most of them are going to stick around.

"And that makes West Ham favourites for me, clearly.

10 Jarrod Bowen marked the news that he will remain at West Ham this season with a goal against Portsmouth Credit: Getty

"They've brought in some good players as well, with [Joël] Veltman coming in, Manor Solomon as well. Yeah, they look exceptionally strong, and they've got a manager that's done it before.

"I remember Nuno's Wolves in the Championship, and they were unbelievable. One of the best teams I've seen with my own eyes get promoted from the Championship to the Premier League.



"West Ham fans have got plenty to look forward to."

Automatic promotion

Jeff Stelling - Wolves

Wolves Championship Top 2 Finish - 2/1

"I think Wolves might go up automatically too. I think they might need to spend again.

"They've got a lot of experience in Kieran Trippier and Raúl Jiménez, and you saw Raúl Jiménez at the World Cup; he looks well capable of scoring goals in the Championship."

10 Wolves booked their spot in the Carabao Cup second round with a convincing win over Port Vale last week Credit: Getty

Adrian Clarke - Middlesbrough

Middlesbrough Top 2 finish - 4/1

"West Ham, that is a stone cold, they're going up prediction. I don't see a world where they fluff their lines. I really don't.



"I think West Ham have the players, they have the manager, they have a big crowd as well. They're going to have a lot of support.

"So West Ham, I think, will win the title. Who's going to go up with them? There's two that really spring to mind, and that's Middlesbrough, who were so close last year.

"Great coach in Kim Hellberg. They've signed some good players. They signed a good striker in Will Lankshear. Really good prospect, I think he is. They've signed a great goalie in Radek Vítek as well from Man United.

"So strengthened at both ends of the pitch. The other one Norwich.

"Norwich were the team with a big momentum at the end of last season under Philippe Clement.



"I think they're definitely heading in the right direction, but I'll go for Boro. Boro alongside the Irons."

10 Lankshear struck a brilliant winner on his competitive debut for Middlesbrough Credit: Getty

Playoffs

Jeff Stelling - West Ham, Wrexham, Norwich, Southampton and Birmingham

"West Ham I've got in the playoffs; I think they've lost too many and not enough incoming. I've got Wrexham there as well.



"Spent a lot of money, and they'll keep on spending. They've brought a new goalkeeper, Anthony Patterson from Sunderland.

"A couple of decent players as well have signed for big money. Ben Whiteman has come in, Preston captain. So Wrexham for the playoffs for me.

"Norwich finished last season brilliantly, absolutely brilliantly. They won 16 and drew 2 of the last 25 last season. That's promotion form really.

"Southampton lost a couple of players. They've brought in Divin Mubama. Didn't set the world alight at Stoke. I think a lot of Stoke fans liked him. Lost Shea Charles, big loss to them. But I think they've got enough to make the playoffs.



"I think Birmingham City have got enough to make the playoffs as well. I thought they might make the playoffs last season.

"They spent £6.5m on a young midfielder from Girona. So a lot might depend on him."

When asked if Birmingham need to finish in the top eight, Stelling said: "Yeah, and I think they will: An opportunity knocks. Millwall, just because they're Millwall and they always finish in the playoff places, don't they?"

10 Wrexham narrowly missed out on the playoffs last season and will fancy their chances in their second Championship season Credit: PA



Championship dark horse

Adrian Clarke - Bristol City

Bristol City to be promoted - 10/1

"Norwich is one of them. But I don't know how dark a horse they particularly are at the moment. Obviously, you've got your Birmingham's and Wrexham. Massive ambition.

"I think of teams that haven't really been in the mix for a while, keep your eye on Bristol City.

"I know that they got off to a bad start, getting knocked out of the Carabao Cup, but they've got the manager Michael Skubala from Lincoln, clearly a manager on the rise.

"They've signed the two best League One strikers.

"I know it's a division below, but Lorent Tolaj from Plymouth and the guy [Dom Ballard] from Leyton Orient as well. Excellent players.



"And there's one or two other good acquisitions there.

"So maybe Bristol City can make that step up from sort of being nearly boys to a side that can challenge for promotion.

"But it's going to be Wolves, Burnley, these sort of teams, Norwich, Southampton maybe, Birmingham, Wrexham. But they're the teams that I expect to be there. Bristol City would be a surprise, along with sort of a Swansea City or someone like that."

10 Bristol have hired Skubala from newly-promoted Championship side Lincoln Credit: Getty

Which manager is under the most pressure?

Adrian Clarke - Chris Davies, John Mousinho and Chris Wilder

"Chris Davies at Birmingham, definitely. I think what happened with the ownership at Birmingham, with the owner, you know, he's a great guy, Tom Wagner, and he suffered a stroke, didn't he?



"I think he's focused on his recovery, which is the right thing to do. And I think that probably helped Chris Davies when they were struggling a bit towards the end of last season.

"They've decided not to do anything. But I do feel that if Birmingham get off to a poor start, then he'll be under pressure, which for me feels harsh because of the good stuff that he has done. But I think that is probably a fair comment.

"You're probably looking at Portsmouth, at John Mousinho as well. There's a lot of speculation around his future.

"There's even a lot of talk that he might choose to leave Pompey in the summer. He didn't. He stuck around.



"And then you've also got Chris Wilder at Sheffield United. Terrible season for them last year, really.

"If it's going to be bland again, if it's going to be a nothing campaign, maybe they might make that change.

"And of course, I shouldn't forget Watford. I mean, any manager that signs a contract to be the Watford head coach is immediately under pressure, right?

"I mean, how many coaches are going to have that season? It's in the contract. I reckon it's going to be between three and four coaches again this season down at Vicarage Road."



10 Birmingham were in 17th place in mid-April, but a late-season surge saw them finish 10th Credit: Getty

Relegation

Jeff Stelling - Lincoln, Charlton and QPR

Lincoln 4/6, Charlton 11/8 QPR 6/1 to finish in bottom 3

"You never want to do this. Lincoln, I mean, they ran away. They ran away with League One last season.

"So you can understand why their supporters would be optimistic. I just don't necessarily see it.

"Charlton, sorry boys. I know we've got a lot of Charlton listeners. Six from bottom last season. They haven't really strengthened particularly.



"And I'm going to offend every QPR fan. I think this could be their time. Having said that, Tariq Lamptey - brought him back into the Championship, I really hope he does well, because he's a kid with a lot of talent. Had so many injuries over the years.

"Dennis Cirkin from Sunderland is a good bit of recruitment from them as well. But I've got them down as third from bottom.

"I hope that I'm absolutely miles out. But those are my views."

10 Lamptey only made two appearances and 25 minutes for Fiorentina Credit: Getty

Adrian Clarke - Blackburn, Preston and Portsmouth

Blackburn 4/1, Preston 3/1 Portsmouth 9/2 to finish in bottom 3

"Blackburn, I'm afraid. I've watched Blackburn a fair bit for talkSPORT and talkSPORT 2, and they haven't been good.



"Whenever I've seen them, they've sort of looked a bit flat and disappointing, especially going forward. They're fairly solid, but they don't inspire.

"It's great that Tony Mowbray's back. It's a lovely story. But as far as I'm aware, they've only signed one player this summer.

"So, there's a feeling that they're treading water a little bit. There's a little bit of worry about Preston as well.

"Another team that's sort of been stuck in the Championship for a while. Are they sort of on a downward turn?



"You probably look at Portsmouth as well. Personally, I think Lincoln might be all right. I know they're favourites to go down, but…even so, they were such a good team last year together.

"They've got momentum. They've got great spirit. I think they can get some points on the board, particularly early on."

10 Mowbray has returned to the dugout after a year out Credit: Getty

Championship standout transfer signings

Adrian Clarke

"The ones at Middlesbrough do stand out in Lankshear and Vítek. I'm looking elsewhere. I think that Jimmy-Jay Morgan coming in at West Bromwich Albion could be a really smart acquisition.



"He's got off to a flyer at the weekend. He's a player from Chelsea. He was on loan last year at Peterborough.

"And I think he's absolutely flying at the moment. So Jimmy-Jay Morgan is a name to keep your eye on. So maybe West Bromwich Albion will be a bit stronger this year.

"I think Swansea, Simon Ross-Stewart from Southampton, proven player at Championship level if he can stay fit.

"The other one that they've signed is the guy, you might remember him from the World Cup, Elijah Just. He was terrific for New Zealand in the World Cup finals. Obviously, they weren't there long, but he made quite a big impression. So, yeah, there are a few that I like.



"Southampton, obviously, I think it's really important that they got the goalie on a permanent deal, [Daniel] Peretz.

"They also got Cyle Larin, another World Cup player from Canada. He's signed permanently too. So the Saints squad's looking good.

"It's just like, what on earth is going to happen with Tonda Eckert? Like, we just don't know.

"That's why I find it hard to talk about Southampton until we know whether the manager's got a long ban or not."

Sports.title: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg stripped of Marseille captaincy after rejecting Premier League switch
Sports.content:
Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has reportedly been removed as Marseille's captain after rejecting a £15million transfer to Newcastle last week.

Hojbjerg played 90 minutes for the French side against Atletico Madrid on Friday, but he did so without the armband.

3 Hojbjerg (left) has lost the captain's armband for Marseille after rejecting Newcastle Credit: AFP

French news outlet RMC Sport claim the Danish midfielder has been punished by club chiefs for angering them with his decision.

Newcastle approached Marseille to try and sign Hojbjerg as a potential replacement for Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies wanted some extra experience added to the squad after losing their captain to Arsenal for £75m.

However, Hojbjerg turned down the chance to return to the Premier League in a deal that was set to be worth £15m.

That would have frustrated Newcastle, but it has also left Marseille angry, with owner Frank McCourt alleged to be fuming.

And so much so, McCourt and the Ligue 1 side's management are said to have opted to strip their midfielder of captaincy, handing it to Timothy Weah instead.

They reportedly wanted the transfer to happen to bring in some much-needed funds and reduce their wage bill.

The club want individual interests to take a back seat to overall interests - so to prove that stance, they have punished Hojbjerg.

Could Hojbjerg still leave Marseille?

Hojbjerg's full involvement in Marseille's friendly on Friday, despite not being captain, indicated he could still stay at the club.

But there is still interest from other teams in Europe, including Serie A giants AC Milan, according to reports in Italy.

3 Hojbjerg angered Marseille chiefs by turning down a return to England Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Ruben Amorim could be looking to add some new faces to his squad amid a refresh of players following his appointment.

Amorim has recently put Fikayo Tomori, Christopher Nkunku and Youssouf Fofana up for sale.

Should any of those players leave, particularly midfielder Fofana, Milan could potentially make a move for Hojbjerg.

Hojbjerg labelled 'incredibly average'

Hojbjerg has played 254 Premier League games throughout his career, starring for Tottenham and Southampton.

But the 31-year-old opted not to make a move back to England, leaving Newcastle having to look at other options.

However, talkSPORT's Jeff Stelling doesn't think the Magpies missed out on much by the Dane rejecting them.

3 Stelling thinks Newcastle haven't missed out on much by Hojbjerg not joining Credit: Getty

"I know they wanted experience, he's 31 and he's done well at Marseille," Stelling said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"But his last season at Tottenham, he made eight Premier League starts and didn't play successive Premier League games at all.

"I think he's incredibly average."

Last season, Hojbjerg played 43 games for Marseille, scoring five goals and assisting another five.

But his future at the club remains in doubt, particularly now that he has lost the captain's armband.

Sports.title: How Liverpool are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match
Sports.content:
How Liverpool are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match

Alexander Isak will return to Newcastle for the first time since forcing an exit from the club in Liverpool's season opener.

Isak and his Reds teammates begin their Premier League campaign with a trip to St. James' Park on August 23.

6 Isak is going to return to take on Newcastle for the first time since leaving Credit: Getty

The match is also new manager Andoni Iraola's first competitive outing in charge after he replaced Arne Slot in the dugout.

Liverpool finished fifth in the top-flight last season, with Slot paying the price for what was a disappointing title defence.

They managed to qualify for the Champions League, and will be desperate to be back challenging for top spot this term.

Some new faces have arrived and club legends have departed, with Iraola starting fresh on the road against Newcastle.

And talkSPORT.com has taken a look at how they could line up for the match.

Isak's awkward return

One man who has a point to prove is Isak - and he's looking set to start up front for the Reds against his former club.

But he's going to have to play in some tough conditions in Newcastle, as he certainly won't be getting a good reception.

Isak left the Magpies last summer in a British transfer record move, signing for Liverpool for a whopping £125million.

He did so in controversial fashion, going on strike to force a transfer and releasing a shock statement demanding to leave the club.

Those actions will have destroyed any relationship with the Newcastle supporters, so Isak won't be welcomed back.

6 Isak is unlikely to get a nice reception back at St. James' Park on August 23 Credit: AFP

It will remain a big moment for the Sweden international though, after going through multiple injury issues last season, including a broken fibula that saw him sit out for five months.

He only played 14 Premier League games for Liverpool in his debut campaign, missing 30 matches for club and country.

However, after a full pre-season, Isak is regaining his fitness and seems sure to be leading the line in his side's opener.

How will Liverpool line up on opening day?

Iraola has been playing in a 4-2-3-1 formation in pre-season with Liverpool, similarly to former manager Slot.

Isak will be the lone striker as Hugo Ekitike continues his recovery after rupturing his Achilles - and there will be a talented three in behind him, including a seemingly settled Florian Wirtz.

Wirtz struggled to show his best in his first Premier League season, only scoring five goals and providing three assists in total.

6 Iraola will hope for a winning start to his tenure as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

6 Wirtz looks to be showing his best heading into the new campaign Credit: Getty

But in the friendlies leading up to the new campaign, he's already scored twice and looks very sharp as the No.10.

Out wide will likely be rising talent Rio Ngumoha, who was the subject of calls for more regular football last term.

Now, he's featured throughout pre-season and could be set to start, with Mohamed Salah's position up for grabs.

New signing Victor Munoz could also be a contender to play there, but he only played his first minutes on August 9.

On the left, Cody Gakpo is expected to start, despite being linked with a move away from the club to Tottenham this summer.

Meanwhile, it seems Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai will form the midfield, with Alexis Mac Allister not long back from World Cup duty with Argentina.

6 Recent arrival Araujo may have been thrown straight into the Liverpool defence Credit: Getty

Teenage star Trey Nyoni could also take some minutes in that position this season, along with Wataru Endo and Curtis Jones, should the latter stay at the club amid exit talks.

In defence, Jeremie Frimpong will be at right-back, with centre-back Virgil van Dijk and left-back Milos Kerkez certain to be joining him.

However, Jeremy Jacquet faces a race against time to be fit to make his Premier League debut in his side's season opener.

Jacquet has not played a game since February due to injury, so it may take him a while to get up to speed with the team.

That means Ronald Araujo could come straight into the starting XI, having just signed on loan from Barcelona, with Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni both still carrying injuries.

But young defenders Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Luke Chambers could potentially push for a start in place of Araujo after picking up plenty of minutes in pre-season.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta raises doubt over Arsenal star’s long-term future at club amid exit rumours
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has thrown Ethan Nwaneri's future at Arsenal into doubt by admitting regular minutes are key for the young star.

Nwaneri has featured in all of the Gunners' pre-season games so far after returning to the club from his loan at Marseille.



3 Nwaneri's future at Arsenal is up in the air heading into the new season Credit: Getty

The 19-year-old spent the second half of last campaign in France, but made just 11 appearances in all competitions - chipping in with two goals and one assist.

His last game for Arsenal was in January in the FA Cup, playing just 153 minutes in the Premier League spread across six outings, before leaving on loan.

And with the Gunners going on to win the top-flight title while he was away, combined with the summer arrivals Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis, his minutes are not expected to rise.



What has Arteta said about Nwaneri?

Speaking ahead of Sunday's Communtiy shield clash against Manchester City, Arteta hinted that a move for more game time could be what's best for Nwaneri, amid links to Turkish giants Galatasaray.

“I want him to be at the club, but something is in the medium and long term what is the best for the player as well,” he said.



“Ethan needs to play football. If he stays here, it's because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes.

"Otherwise, it's just something that is not good for anybody, I think."



Nwaneri had an incredible breakout in 2022, becoming the Premier League's youngest-ever player, aged just 15.

However, his career trajectory has seemingly lost some momentum at 19, with his loan at Marseille not going smoothly, as he was dropped in April due to his 'day-to-day commitment'.

Arteta has still been pleased with the teenager's progression though, saying during pre-season: "I don't know on the plans, but certainly it opens your eyes in terms of how much a young player can evolve in such a short period.

3 Nwaneri had a tough loan at Marseille, but Arteta still speaks very highly of him Credit: Getty



"An experience abroad with certain difficulties and challenges, what you can get out of that. I think he's done it in a brilliant way.

"It's unquestionable the talent, the desire, the love and the passion he has for the game. It's something that I always loved about Ethan.

"I think he had some great games, he's shown everybody that he has the ability to be here."

Could Nwaneri be sold this summer?

Arteta clearly still rates Nwaneri highly, but if minutes are the deciding factor on his future, it could lead to an exit.



Nwaneri has to compete with Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze in a midfield role, while being behind Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman and Gabriel Martinelli out wide.

With his game time to be limited, it's understood that Arsenal are willing to listen to offers for him this summer.

3 Talks have been held with Galatasaray regarding Nwaneri and Martinelli Credit: Getty

The Gunners have discussed Nwaneri with Galatasaray during their transfer talks, which also included a potential switch for Martinelli, who has now rejected a potential transfer to Turkey.



And Arteta has spoken openly about the reality of having to let some more players go before the deadline on September 1.

“We have certain possibilities that we can explore if the right possibilities come across," the Arsenal boss said.

"So far, with the numbers that we have, we are happy, but obviously we need to accept that there are certain players that probably have to move.”

Nwaneri may well be among that group of certain players that are going to need to go elsewhere for regular football.



If he doesn't feature in the Community Shield against City on Sunday, live on talkSPORT, then the writing may be on the wall.

Sports.title: Aston Villa record-breaker Brian Madjo set for period on sidelines through injury
Sports.content:
Aston Villa record-breaker Brian Madjo set for period on sidelines through injury

Aston Villa striker Brian Madjo is expected to miss the start of the Premier League season after picking up an injury.

Madjo, who has been a breakout star this pre-season, suffered a knock after Villa's UEFA Super Cup loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

3 Madjo has been dealt a cruel blow by picking up an injury ahead of the season Credit: Getty

The 17-year-old scored his club's only goal in that game against French giants PSG on what was his competitive debut.

But now he's suffered a cruel blow, just a week before the Premier League campaign gets going.

How long will Madjo be out?

According to The Athletic, Madjo is set to be sidelined until at least September.

If that is the case, he will miss Aston Villa's opening game against Brighton, as well as a clash against Arsenal.

The forward could also be sat out for matches against newly-promoted Hull City and Nottingham Forest, as well as Tottenham on September 19.

It is a nightmare scenario for Unai Emery, who would have planned to use Madjo in his side's opening fixtures this term.

As mentioned, the teenager has starred in pre-season, scoring once and making a huge impact in his three appearances.

His goal against PSG that levelled the tie at the time in the Super Cup saw him break a record in the special match.

He became the youngest ever scorer in the UEFA game that sees the Champions League and Europa League winners face off.

Madjo would have hoped to take some of his momentum into his maiden Premier League season, but he will now be out.

3 Madjo became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup, but now he's ruled out Credit: Getty

Who else is injured for Aston Villa?

Aston Villa will be very disappointed to not have Madjo available.

Ollie Watkins is sure to start now, but Tammy Abraham is Emery's only other option up front heading into the campaign.

And when it comes to injuries, Villa have another one to worry about alongside the youngster, who officially joined this summer.

Fellow new signing Joao Gomes has also been ruled out.

Similar to Madjo, after the loss to PSG, Gomes picked up an injury and he is set to be sidelined for the next two to four weeks.

Recovery timelines are yet to be fully determined, but both players are certainly going to miss the start of the season.

3 Gomes has also been ruled out following the Super Cup clash with PSG Credit: AFP

Emery has already been without Amadou Onana, who suffered an ACL injury while playing at the World Cup for Belgium.

And after losing Youri Tielemans to Manchester United, Villa are looking sparse in the midfield department...

They kick-start their season against Brighton on Sunday, August 23, with talkSPORT providing all the latest updates.
