Sports.title: Cristian Romero confirms Tottenham exit as he nears £34million transfer
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero has confirmed that he is leaving Tottenham in a social media post after agreeing a deal to join Atletico Madrid.

Atletico have reached an agreement in principle to sign Romero for a fee worth £34million, talkSPORT understands.

5 Romero's time at Spurs is over as he confirmed he'd be leaving the club Credit: Getty

The Spurs captain has long been tipped for a summer exit from north London, and he has now announced his departure.

Serie A giants Napoli were set to pay £34m for Romero, but were unable to agree terms with the player, while more recently, he was linked with a shock switch to Spurs' bitter rivals Arsenal.

Inter Milan also held talks with him earlier in the summer, but the Argentine is now set to get his dream move to Spain.

With a fee now agreed for him to join Atletico, Spurs will also retain a 15 per cent sell-on clause on any future transfer.

This comes after Romero agreed personal terms with the La Liga side, with a four-year deal on the table, which has the option of a further year.

Romero will join up with compatriot Diego Simeone at Atletico, in a move that will bring to an end his five-year stay at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Spurs are yet to confirm the sale of their centre-back, but he has already done it himself on his own social media.

What did Romero say in his goodbye statement?

Posting on his Instagram on Friday evening, Romero wrote: "Today, I say goodbye to a place that, for five seasons, was much more than a club. It was my home, my challenge and the place where my family and I built such an important part of our lives.

"I leave with a heart full of memories and enormous pride for everything we lived and achieved together.

"When I arrived, I had a clear dream: to leave my name in this club’s history. I knew the only way was through hard work, sacrifice and achieving something that had seemed so difficult for so long: lifting a trophy again. And we did it.

5 Romero played a key role in Tottenham's surge to Europa League glory in 2025 Credit: Getty

"The journey wasn’t perfect, but I don’t want that to define my goodbye. I choose to remember the happy moments, the lessons, the people who stood by me and, above all, the love I received during these five years.

"Thank you to everyone at the club who shared this journey with me. Coaches, teammates, staff and every person working behind the scenes you are all part of my story and have a place in my heart.

"And to the fans: Thank you for loving me, respecting me and making me feel like one of you from day one. Thank you for every hug, every song, every flag, every applause and for always being there.

"I know I wasn’t perfect, but one thing gives me peace: I always gave everything. I defended this shirt with pride and with all my heart.

"THANK YOU FOR EVERYTHING. I’m leaving the club, but a part of my heart will always remain here.

"Once I was one of you. Today, I leave as one of you forever. With all my love and respect. Thank you for everything. And goodbye."

5 Romero will join Diego Simeone and his Argentine contingent at Atletico Madrid

Tottenham's defensive overhaul

Spurs have signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer, with Micky van de Ven signing a new deal.

This has left Romero free to leave the club, despite penning a contract extension through to 2029 last August.

His imminent exit comes after he drew criticism from fans for his conduct and ill discipline last season.

Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances, and received ten yellow cards as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation.

The 2022 World Cup winner also became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the season in favour of a return to his homeland to watch formative club Belgrano.

With Spurs at risk of relegation and Romero getting wind of fan disgruntlement, he later changed his mind and instead was on hand to support his teammates in their quest for survival.

5 The Argentine seeing red became a frustratingly familiar sight for Spurs fans in recent seasons Credit: Getty

'Get rid of him'

As Romero closes in on a move away from north London, talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara had no qualms about Tottenham losing their captain.

Discussing the defender's links with Arsenal, the Sports Bar host and former Spurs player insisted the club would be better off without him, and claimed their new arrivals are better options.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, O'Hara said: “Get rid of him. I've heard there’s Arsenal chat about him - get rid of him.

“He was a liability for us last season. We’ve finished 17th in the last two seasons - he was the captain. He didn't want to be there on the last day. It was only because he got told that he had to come back that he ended up coming back.

“So get rid of him. We've got better players now. He's a liability.

“Van de Ven - make him captain. He's a player that you want in your side. You got Senesi, Van Hecke. Romero isn't even going to play.”

5 Van Hecke looks set to fill Romero's boots after his £52million arrival from Brighton Credit: Getty

After two disappointing league campaigns, Tottenham have set about kickstarting a new era under Roberto De Zerbi this summer.

Spurs have splashed the cash in a bid to rebuild, spending £237m in total, which includes twice breaking their club transfer record - first to sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle respectively.

And O'Hara insisted there is no place for Romero in De Zerbi's new-look team, even after playing a central role in Argentina's run to the World Cup final.

Continuing to blast Romero, he added: “I'm happy to see the back of him.

"We need a new era under De Zerbi and it looks like he's putting a right good team together. We'll see what happens, but it looks like we've got a right good team and the players seem to like him.

“But Romero isn’t part of it. Get rid of him, get as much as we can."

Sports.title: Chelsea could host another club’s Champions League matches at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
Chelsea could host another club’s Champions League matches at Stamford Bridge

Stamford Bridge could play host to the Champions League in the upcoming season after Shakhtar Donetsk asked to play there.

It's understood that the Ukrainian side want to play their home ties in Europe's premier competition in west London.



4 Shakhtar were in the Conference League last year, but they are back in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Shakhtar haven't been able to play at the Donbas Arena since 2014.

That is due to the Russia-backed annexation of Donetsk and the surrounding regions.

Negotiations are ongoing between the clubs with a strong relationship being developed.

This was, in part, down to the Mykhailo Mudryk transfer in January 2023 as well as their involvement in the Game4Ukraine.



There were other options with Fulham's Craven Cottage and Brentford's Gtech touted, but they appear to favour Stamford Bridge.

Why do Shakhtar Donetsk want Champions League games played in England?

Shakhtar reportedly hope to connect with an estimated 32,000 Ukraine-born residents living in London with this move to play Champions League games in the capital of England.



Due to the invasion of Ukraine by Russia, Shakhtar haven't played a home game in 12 years.

They play domestic 'home' ties all across the unoccupied parts of Ukraine, but for European ties, they have played in many different stadia.



In the Conference League last year, they alternated between Krakow in Poland and Ljubljana, Slovenia.

But after winning the Ukrainian top-flight, they are back in the Champions League and will be in from the League Phase of the competition.

4 There will be no form of European football at Stamford Bridge this summer, so the ground is available Credit: Getty

4 Chelsea's relationship with Shakhtar is very strong Credit: Getty



Nothing has been confirmed by Shakhtar or Chelsea, but they did reveal earlier this summer that they were in talks about playing in England.

They said: "Shakhtar is currently negotiating with several venues in the United Kingdom and Germany in order to secure a host stadium for its UEFA Champions League matches next season.

"We will not comment on the process until a decision is announced in the near future."

Shakhtar are one of two Ukrainian clubs to win a major European trophy, winning the UEFA Cup in 2009 by beating Werder Bremen.



2026/27 Champions League

Shakhtar are one of 29 teams to have automatically qualified for the Champions League.

There are still seven spots up for grabs, which are to be decided by a round of play-off games.

4 Shakhtar have a strong European pedigree and are hoping to sell out Stamford Bridge Credit: AFP

There are 14 teams remaining, with the winners from the two-legged ties sealing a place in the League Phase draw.



Among the teams competing to make it into the Champions League are Fenerbahce, Lyon, Celtic and Bodo/Glimt.

The draw for the League Phase is then scheduled to take place on Thursday, August 27.

It will take place in Monaco and is set to get going at 5pm UK time, where Shakhtar and all the rest of the Champions League sides find out what awaits.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star Francis Coquelin suffers 'suspected broken eye socket' as veteran is rushed to hospital after brutal clash of heads in Ligue 2 fixture
Sports.content:
Former Arsenal midfielder Francis Coquelin was taken to hospital after a frightening clash of heads in a league match in France.

Coquelin, now 35, had been making just his second appearance for Ligue 2 side Laval on Friday night.

The midfielder went down in the early stages of the match after clashing heads with Wilitty Younoussa, who was making his debut for Nantes.

Medical staff were called onto the pitch to attend to the players, with Coquelin and Younoussa both ultimately forced to leave the pitch on stretchers.

Reports in France stated that Coquelin was conscious as he was taken to hospital but has undergone a scan amid concerns he had suffered a broken eye socket.

'After his heavy collision with Younoussa, Coquelin was taken to the hospital but conscious,' French journalist Raphael Faurie-Pacaud wrote.

Francis Coquelin was stretchered off after a clash of head in a Ligue 2 match in France

Coquelin, seen playing for Arsenal in 2016, suffered a suspected broken eye socket

'Suspicion of an orbital floor fracture for the player who was making his first appearance with the Tango at Le Basser.

'He could be sidelined from the field for several months.'

Laval head coach David Vignes confirmed post-match he believes the injury was 'pretty serious' and would rule Coquelin out for the foreseeable future.

Coquelin had rejoined Laval in the summer, with the midfielder having started his career at the club.

The 35-year-old had been part of the youth set-up at Laval, before being signed to Arsenal's academy.

Coquelin went on to play 160 times for Arsenal and won the FA Cup twice, while he also had loan spells at Lorient, Freiburg and Charlton.

He spent three years at Valencia after leaving Arsenal, before a four-year spell at Villarreal, where he was part of their Europa League winning team in 2020-21.

Coquelin spent the last two seasons at Nantes and was facing his former side on Friday for the first time when his injury occurred.

Laval ultimately earned a 2-1 victory in the Ligue 2 match following a stoppage time winner.

Sports.title: Golden girl Keely Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as British star loses her 800m European Championship crown with second-place finish - with Olympic champion jokingly removing her medal in disappointed post-race interview
Sports.content:
Audrey Werro is fast becoming an unsolvable riddle for the leading lady of British sport. For the second time in 10 weeks, this Swiss phenomenon left Keely Hodgkinson staring at her heels in a race that lived up to its billing as the best of the European Championships.

To the most talented Audrey since Hepburn went the 800m gold medal. To Hodgkinson, there was presumably no silver lining to be found in finishing a close second on home soil.

If there is to be any consolation, it is that Werro, aged 22, clocked a championship record of 1:54.81 on a chilly, breezy evening in Birmingham to beat her. But warmer thoughts will be harder to find for Hodgkinson.

Instead, the Olympic champion must process the dawning of a serious rivalry and one that is not currently swinging in her favour. This one was settled by the margin of 0.2sec.

In the long run, Hodgkinson might view such moments as the competitive nectar needed for the breaching of new frontiers, of course, but the sting in the present will be real. Not many athletes have the finishing speed to match Hodgkinson, but in their past two races Werro has kicked away from her with the force of a donkey.

The decisive move here came after 500 metres, when Werro put the hammer down.

Hodgkinson, who had been near enough level at the bell after a 56sec opening lap, went with her, and they both separated from Femke Broeders-Bol in third, but the Brit had no answer. She never got her nose in front, and those moments of futility can leave lasting doubts in an athlete.

The 24-year-old, who was chasing a third straight European title, was evidently in little mood to indulge the celebrations of on-track interviewer Iwan Thomas. He assumed she would be thrilled with silver, but Hodgkinson responded: ‘I think I would be happier with a gold.’

Kely Hodgkinson was forced to settle for second in the women's 800m final on Friday

Hodgkinson jokingly took off her silver medal at the European Championships in Birmingham

She later added: ‘I think with that level of competition, any medal is a really good achievement and another one to add to my collection so I can never be disappointed with that. But I'm defending champion so I wanted to do that.

‘I knew it was going to come down to the wire but I really thought I was going to win today. But it wasn't meant to be. I didn't do anything wrong, it was just one of those things.

‘Congrats to Audrey. I am sure we will have more battles.’

That much seems certain. And for two women striving to break the oldest world record in track athletics, that will be a good thing.

But Werro has the edge. Having been beaten twice by Hodgkinson during the indoor portion of the season, she gained spectacular revenge in Stockholm in June when the Brit set a personal best of 1:54.33. Not only was that a win against a full-form Hodgkinson, Werro’s time of 1:53.98 was the third quickest in history. A month later, Werro ran quicker again with a 1:53.80 – if anyone is to better the dubious mark of 1:53.28 set by the Czech Jarmila Kratochvilova in the Eighties, Werro might have the edge.

To think, Werro was only cleared to race in this final on appeal after being tripped in her semi-final. It was a marginal call but also the correct one, so there should be no controversy around what it led to.

For Hodgkinson, the bigger picture will make for strange viewing. After the injury troubles of 2025, her times in 2026 have moved sharply on an upward trajectory, including the indoor world record in February, so she rightly resents any suggestion of ‘failure’ at losing a race or two. She was borderline tetchy in using that label prior to these Championships.

But in athletics, the clock is a secondary adversary to the field and Werro’s emergence is a huge fly in the ointment. For the rest of us watching, we can presumably take great pleasure in where it leads, because athletics needs rivalries. In these two gifted runners, it has one that has the potential to go on for years.

Sports.title: Manor Solomon opens up on his friendship with West Ham favourite Yossi Benayoun, not realising the rivalry with Tottenham and Championship ambitions after move
Sports.content:
Manor Solomon opens up on his friendship with West Ham favourite Yossi Benayoun, not realising the rivalry with Tottenham and Championship ambitions after move

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manor Solomon scrolls through the thousands of pictures on his phone before finding the one he’s after. Even amid the endless stream of snaps and selfies from over the years, he knows exactly where it is. He presses his finger to the screen and up it pops.

Two old images, one stitched above the other, taken 11 years apart, showing the same two men. At the bottom, a six-year-old Solomon stands in front of Israel icon and former West Ham favourite Yossi Benayoun.

‘I was in a football camp during the summer and he came to visit us as a surprise,’ says Solomon, sat around a wooden table in the sunshine at West Ham’s Rush Green training ground. ‘I had a picture with him. My father just got him outside of the room asking for a photo with me.’

Above it, the two of them once again, wearing the same colours of their country, this time as team-mates after 17-year-old Solomon was called up to the Israel national team.

‘We trained together. We shared the dressing room together. It was really amazing to share the dressing room with him. He’s really a hero. He's the hero of Israeli football. Him and Eyal Berkovic. They are the best footballers we've ever had in Israeli football.

‘He was my idol. First of all, he's Israeli. He made it to England. He played in the Premier League. He played for Liverpool, Arsenal, Chelsea, West Ham, the biggest clubs in England.

Manor Solomon has signed for West Ham from Tottenham this summer

‘Back then I was really little and I was looking up to him. If he made his dream come true, coming from Dimona, a small city in Israel, playing in the Premier League for the biggest clubs, maybe one day I can be the same.

‘I really love this game. He was a winger, a number 10, similar to me. Different, but similar. I always looked up to him and said: if Yossi did it, maybe in the future I will be able to get closer to him. I never thought I would get because he was for me the best one.’

Benayoun had two spells with the Hammers, helping the club to the FA Cup final in 2006, before returning on loan from Chelsea in 2012.

They are friends now. Solomon phoned him up when he knew he was leaving Tottenham and interest in him from West Ham and others started to surface.

‘I had a few options,’ he says. ‘I asked him what he thought was the best option because I want to hear his opinion. Obviously, he’s played for West Ham. And he told me that he sees me in English football. For him, I'm really suitable and I really fit English football. And West Ham can be a really, really good place for me.’

Solomon’s arrival means he’s the first player to make the switch from Spurs to West Ham since Callum Davenport in 2007. When Mohammed Kudus made the move the other way last summer, he was the first to do so since Scott Parker in 2011.

The 27-year-old, though, revealed he was not aware of the rivalry between the two. ‘I didn’t know it,’ he laughs. ‘So, let’s say I came from Manchester United it would be different?’

Oh yes.

‘Coming from Spurs… because they hate each other?’

Oh yes.

‘Okay. Yeah, I didn’t know. I know everyone in London hates each other, especially the big clubs. Tottenham, Arsenal, Chelsea, West Ham. They all hate each other but I didn’t know how big this is.’

Oh yes. So, any message to the West Ham fans so they take it easy on you?

‘It doesn't matter where I came from. It doesn't matter. I think if I came from Spurs, I came from Liverpool, I came from Fiorentina, for me it doesn't matter. I'll just try to give my best regardless of where I came from.’

Solomon says he was unaware of the rivalry between Spurs and West Ham

There is another rivalry he’s aware of, though.

‘I've heard about the rivalry between West Ham and Millwall,’ says Solomon. ‘I heard it's really big. I think it's one game before the national team break. So, there's plenty of games until this one. I think a friend of mine told me about the rivalry because I didn't know it before. And then also here at the club everyone told me it's a big rivalry. Of course, West Ham is the big club between the two. But Millwall fans I know are really harsh and tough. So for sure against West Ham it will be even bigger.’

Solomon’s time at Spurs was blighted by injury, but he does know what it takes to help fire a club to promotion. He was on loan at Leeds when they won the Championship in 2024-25, scoring the stoppage-time winner at Plymouth that secured the title.

‘There is a big difference between the Championship and the Premier League,’ he adds. ‘West Ham is a big club that can be back in the Premier League and then remain there for a really long time.

‘Everyone knows that West Ham belongs in the top half of the Premier League. Three years ago they won a European title. I'm sure if the club goes in the right direction, this club will fight again for Europe in the Premier League.’

Sports.title: Supercomputer backs Arsenal to retain Premier League title, predicts how Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City will get on under new bosses - and names the surprise team in Europe who might get relegated
Sports.content:
Supercomputer backs Arsenal to retain Premier League title, predicts how Liverpool, Chelsea and Man City will get on under new bosses - and names the surprise team in Europe who might get relegated

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The opening day of the Premier League season is fast approaching, with a supercomputer backing Arsenal to defend their title in the 2026-27 campaign.

Mikel Arteta's side ended a 22-year wait to be crowned champions last term, with the Gunners holding off Man City after finishing as runners-up in three successive seasons.

Arteta will look to become just the fourth manager in Premier League history to retain the title, following Sir Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho and Pep Guardiola.

According to Opta's supercomputer, which has conducted 10,000 data-led simulations of the campaign, Arsenal are the overwhelming favourites having been given a 38 per cent chance of lifting the trophy again in May.

By contrast, Liverpool were given a 28.5 per cent chance of retaining the title last year under Arne Slot, with the Reds ultimately finishing down in fifth.

A concern for Arsenal, however, has been highlighted over the back injury sustained by William Saliba with Arsenal's win percentage dropping from 68.7 to 47.6 per cent in the Premier League when the Frenchman is unavailable.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will look to be just the fourth boss to lead his side to back-to-back Premier League titles

Manchester City are seen as the second most likely team to be crowned champions

Man City are viewed as Arsenal's most likely challengers again, despite the departure of their legendary manager Pep Guardiola.

Enzo Maresca's side have been given a 20.5 per cent chance of glory following a summer of change, with Elliot Anderson the headline addition at £116m, although Rodri could follow Bernardo Silva in leaving the club.

PREMIER LEAGUE TITLE PROJECTION Arsenal – 38% Man City – 20.5% Liverpool – 9.2% Man United – 6.2% Aston Villa – 4.8% Chelsea – 4.1% Tottenham – 2.9% Source: Opta

Liverpool are third most likely champions at 9.2 per cent, despite new boss Andoni Iraola admitting in pre-season that his side 'cannot sustain the level we want' at this time.

The Reds are followed by rivals Manchester United, with Michael Carrick given a 6.2 per cent chance of winning the league.

Despite Aston Villa selling Morgan Rogers for a British transfer record £117million to Chelsea and the departure of Youri Tielemans to Man United, Unai Emery's side are fifth favourites at 4.8 per cent.

They are narrowly ahead of Chelsea under new boss Xabi Alonso at 4.1 per cent, with the Blues having a clear fixture schedule after missing out on Europe last season.

It is a similar situation at Tottenham, who are seen as having a 2.9 per cent chance of claiming the title under Roberto De Zerbi.

Tottenham have been among the biggest spenders in the transfer market this summer, with Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes among marquee signings at £100m and £85m respectively.

The spend comes with Spurs having recorded back-to-back 17th placed finishes in the top flight, with the Premier League status only confirmed on the final day of last season.

Hull City earned promotion to the top flight via the playoffs, but are seen as favourites to go down

Fulham are viewed as potential surprise strugglers under their new boss Alvaro Arbeloa

At the other end of the table, the three newly promoted sides have unsurprisingly been viewed as the most likely to go straight back down to the Championship.

Hull City, who came up from the play-offs, are deemed the most at risk of relegation at 38.7 per cent.

Ipswich and Coventry follow on 31.2 and 27.9 per cent, respectively.

The three clubs can take heart from Sunderland, who were viewed as the side most likely to finish bottom last season only for the Black Cats to qualify for Europe after a memorable campaign.

PREMIER LEAGUE RELEGATION RISK Hull City – 38.7% Ipswich Town – 31.2% Coventry City – 27.9% Sunderland – 25.9% Fulham – 23.4% Leeds United – 22.5% Crystal Palace – 20% Source: Opta

Sunderland's participation in the Europa League and their limited transfer activity this summer could have an impact on their prospects this campaign.

Opta's supercomputer has the Black Cats as fourth most likely club to be relegated at 25.9 per cent,

It follows Sunderland's underlying numbers last season, where they had the third lowest open-play expected goals, as well as facing the third-most shots and the fourth-most shots on target in the top flight.

Fulham are the next club at risk at 23.4 per cent, following a summer which has seen Marco Silva leave and be replaced by Alvaro Arbeloa.

Leeds United and Crystal Palace follow at 22.5 and 20 per cent, respectively.

Nottingham Forest and Brentford are next at 18.1 and 16.3, followed by Everton and Bournemouth on 13.6 and 13.1.

Sports.title: Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes get off to worst possible start as a DRONE crashes into the track before hurdles event - with British star, 33, underwhelming after first day
Sports.content:
Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes get off to worst possible start as a DRONE crashes into the track before hurdles event - with British star, 33, underwhelming after first day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A drone crash was the least of Katarina Johnson-Thompson’s concerns as she made an underwhelming start to her challenge for a European Championship medal in Birmingham.

After three disciplines, the 33-year-old was placed 15th and offering little indication she has fully recovered race sharpness from the calf niggle that ruled her out of the Commonwealth Games.

Serving as a portent of the hiccups that lay ahead, Johnson-Thompson’s first event, the 100m hurdles, was delayed during surreal scenes when a drone fly-by went hilariously wrong. In attempting to pass underneath the barriers, the driver lost his bearings and crashed into one of the hurdles.

When the gun finally set the field loose, Johnson-Thompson clocked 14sec – her worst time in 14 years of competing in major championships. From there, she regained some ground by clearing 1.83m in the high jump, allowing the two-time world gold medallist to climb to 10th, before tumbling four spots with a disappointing 12.79m in the shot put – 165cm short of her best.

Poland’s Adrianna Sulek-Schubert leads from Ireland’s Kate O’Connor.

Meanwhile, World Athletics president Lord Sebastian Coe has played down rumours that low crowds in Birmingham could harm London’s bid to host the 2029 World Championships.

"Maybe we need a stretcher? Medics?" 🚨



This scenic drone shot was going so well... 💥🤕 pic.twitter.com/UJEIm32LhJ — BBC Sport (@BBCSport) August 14, 2026

Katarina Johnson-Thompson's heptathlon hopes got off to a strange start when her 100m hurdles race was delayed by a camera drone crash

The Alexander Stadium, with a capacity of 23,000, was almost half-empty during some sessions earlier in the week, which has sparked awkward questions at a time when UK Athletics is bidding against Rome, Nairobi and Munich for the bigger event in three years.

Asked if pictures of empty seats in Birmingham might influence panel members looking at London’s presentation, Lord Coe said: ‘Look, it’s horses for courses. We had London (Olympics) in 2012, London (world championships) in 2017, London will point to having sold out Diamond League five months before the event took place. So I think it was a challenge. It’s always a challenge starting a championship on a Monday morning.’

Sports.title: How 'Gladiator' Amy Hunt became Britain's newest sprint superstar - as self-styled 'track goddess' eyes fantastic four golds in Birmingham and nipping at the heels of the international elite
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The fingers told the story of Amy Hunt’s incomplete mission in Birmingham on Thursday evening. First, she showed two for the gold medals she has collected so far in her domination of European sprinting and then she held up four to signify a job half done.

Even in this city of bovine obsessions, there presumably isn’t a bull stubborn enough to wager against that target being met over the weekend.

On Saturday, she will team up with Dina Asher-Smith in the 4x100m, for which the British quartet are favourites, and they will go again in the mixed relay on Sunday. Given the male talent pool includes Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu, respectively the European gold and silver medallists, Hunt’s chances of delivering on her astonishing projections are more than strong.

By now, folk are aware enough of her remarkable talents, both for the winning of races over short distances and her willingness to accompany the golds with spoken nuggets. In an era when too many of her contemporaries hide their personalities behind thick shields, Hunt, 24, is the open book athletics needed; a Cambridge graduate who isn’t afraid to share idiosyncratic declarations of self-confidence and one who, repeatedly, has backed up big talk with big performances.

By Thursday night, with the 200m title added to the 100m gold won on Monday, she was channelling Russell Crowe’s Gladiator on the track with the cry: ‘Are you not entertained?’ It was later followed by a charming explanation to reporters that her father is so obsessed by the film that his parting words to his daughter, prior to each race, include another Maximus classic: ‘Strength and honour.’

Added to the 200m world silver medal Hunt in Tokyo last year, the honours are adding up. So too is the strength of conviction that Olympic prizes and Asher-Smith’s British sprint records could soon be under threat by the next British speedster off the rank.

Newly crowned double European sprint champion Amy Hunt is the open book that athletics needs

On Saturday, she will team up with Dina Asher-Smith in the 4x100m

Hunt signalled she is halfway to her target of four gold medals after adding 200m glory to her 100m triumph

It is an enticing thought, especially as we approach the halfway point of the LA Olympic cycle. But there are a couple of caveats at play – by timings, the best of Asher-Smith, 30, remains some way ahead of what we have seen so far from Hunt, and more pertinent, the places on an Olympic podium are further clear again.

Some context here: Hunt’s best at the 100m is 10.97sec, which was delivered in Stockholm earlier this year, and at the longer distance she clocked 22.08sec in Tokyo last year. Fast as the sporting world likes to move on, let’s not forget Asher-Smith went 0.15sec faster in winning the 100m world silver in 2019 and was 0.2sec quicker while winning 200m gold at the same championships.

Asher-Smith, a world-class athlete at her best and, more importantly, an expert at managing the rounds at a championship, is no soft target. In other words, Hunt will need to maintain this steep trajectory to even get close to breaking her national records.

The other conversation involves catching the world’s elite and perspective is needed – in 2026, when we have seen the best of Hunt in the 100m, she only ties 25th in the global list, more than 0.3sec off the top, and her standard for the 200m places her 10th, more than half a second off Julien Alfred.

The purpose of mentioning these deficits is not to dilute any hype, but an accurate scaling of where she stands when non-European bibs are in the race might be necessary. In doing so, it should also be recognised, with some excitement, that Hunt is not close to being the finished article. That is a good thing.

Adam Gemili, her former training partner and an excellent analyst of the biomechanics in sprinting, told the Daily Telegraph that he can foresee Hunt reaching the 21.6s in the 200m, her stronger discipline.

The long stride of a 5ft 11ins runner has a certain ring of Usain Bolt about it; the trade off is slower starts in the 100m, but there are those around UK Athletics who believe she can the top-end speeds of the best women in the world. On the latter, it was demonstrated in how she ran down the field in the shorter distance on Monday and again when she passed Asher-Smith on the straight on Thursday.

Hunt's best times are still slower than Dina Asher-Smith at her peak and improvement will be needed to catch the world's best

It is exciting that Hunt is not the finished article with Adam Gemili forecasting she can go 21.6s in the 200m

Those strengths offer fascinating possibilities, as does her comfort in the unique challenge of a championship, where the pressure is greatest and fatigue accumulates between rounds. As Hunt previously demonstrated by describing herself as an 'academic badass and track goddess', some athletes are more born to the spotlight than others. Lord Sebastian Coe, president of World Athletics, has been among the luminaries at the European Championships to identify that ease with her circumstances as a decisive trait.

Doubtless it will be tested in more extreme circumstances at the world championships next year, by which point more time will have been afforded to understanding Hunt’s peculiar issue with low blood pressure. She revealed it in the wake of winning the 200m, with the consequence that felt close to fainting during a race in London earlier this year. Less than ideal.

But Hunt has overcome all manner of problems to get this far. It should not be forgotten that after breaking the under-18 world record for the 200m, she spent years tormented by injuries. A ruptured quadricep while at university left her in such a state that she needed help from her mother to get out of the shower.

These days, she might require assistance carrying the medals and little else.

Sports.title: Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo signed prenup agreement with new wife Georgina Rodriguez, as marriage certificate and full details of their wedding at £30m mansion emerge
Sports.content:
Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo signed prenup agreement with new wife Georgina Rodriguez, as marriage certificate and full details of their wedding at £30m mansion emerge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez got married at their new £30million mansion near Lisbon in front of just four witnesses and their children, it emerged today.

Cristiano's doting mum Dolores Aveiro and his three siblings Hugo, Elma and Katia, were not present at the intimate civil ceremony, which took place at 1.30pm on Tuesday.

Georgina's sister Ivana, Cristiano's long-time friend Miguel Paixao and a Spanish couple named as Jose Rodriguez Sangil and his wife Monica Goncalez Martinez were the only witnesses.

Registrar Maria Manuel Ferreira de Campos Folhadela de Oliveira travelled from the northern Portuguese city of Porto to Cascais to officiate the ceremony.

And the star couple, who married exactly one year to the day after they announced their engagement on social media, have decided to keep their prenuptial assets separate despite tying the knot after a decade-long romance.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez married with four witnesses in Cascais, Lisbon

The marriage certificate for Ronaldo and Georgina's wedding has now emerged

The couple posted photos of them wearing their wedding rings after the small ceremony

They signed a prenup agreement to define their property regime on August 10, a day before the ceremony, at a public notary's office in Lisbon.

Cristiano Ronaldo's representatives confirmed earlier this week the footballer and his long-time partner married on August 11 in an 'intimate' ceremony in Cascais after the couple posted photos of them wearing their wedding rings on social media.

It followed speculation which turned out to be false that they were due to marry at Funchal Cathedral in Cristiano's native island of Madeira on Saturday.

No details had emerged about where in Cascais they had wed or who exactly was at the ceremony apart from their children.

Overnight respected Portuguese newspaper Jornal de Noticias published a copy of the marriage certificate showing it took place at Cristiano's massive mansion in the upmarket residential area of Quinta da Marina.

And it also evidenced the fact so few people were invited there appeared to be no place for Cristiano's mum, who gave the union her blessing shortly afterwards by posting a heart emoticon on her son's Instagram in response to his wedding announcement, or the rest of his family apart from his children.

Jose Rodriguez Sangil was described as a Spanish jeweller by Portuguese press.

The marriage document listed Cristiano's full name and age of 41 as well as his birthplace and the names of his parents, including his late father Jose Dinis.

Cristiano's massive built-from-scratch mansion in Quinta da Marina was the venue

The home boats an impressive infinity pool, underground car park and a private cinema room

Ronaldo wore his wedding ring on his finger as he returned to training in Saudi Arabia

The same details were listed for 32-year-old Georgina, born in the Argentinian capital Buenos Aires, and referenced by her full name of Georgina Luisa Rodriguez Hernandez. They will both keep their pre-marriage names.

The marriage certificate was recorded as number 1,493 of this year but appears to have been listed at Porto's Registry Office instead of Cascais which is the municipality where the wedding took place.

Cristiano and Georgina are now back in Saudi Arabia where the Portuguese international plays his club football for Al Nassr ahead of the start of the new season tomorrow.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes names £60m Arsenal star they should 'get rid of' instead of Myles Lewis-Skelly amid Man United and Chelsea links
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes names £60m Arsenal star they should 'get rid of' instead of Myles Lewis-Skelly amid Man United and Chelsea links

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Man United legend Paul Scholes believes Arsenal would be making a mistake if they sold Myles Lewis-Skelly this summer - and highlighted another player the Gunners should move on instead.

Lewis-Skelly, 19, enjoyed a breakout campaign in 2024-25, and while he struggled for gametime last time out, he played an important role in the end-of-season run-in.

However, with the £75million addition of Bruno Guimaraes adding to the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze as options in central midfield, it has raised uncertainty over the 19-year-old's future.

Reports then broke earlier this week suggesting Arsenal had offered Lewis-Skelly to both Chelsea and Man United.

And, speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet, Scholes felt that if Arsenal sanctioned his departure it would be a big mistake.

‘I prefer Myles Lewis-Skelly in centre midfield to Zubimendi,’ Scholes said.

Paul Scholes believes Arsenal would be making a mistake if they sold Myles Lewis-Skelly

Lewis-Skelly has been linked with a move to both Chelsea and Manchester United this summer

‘I think Zubimendi struggled last year. If there’s one player you are going to get rid of, it would be him [Martin Zubimendi].'

Scholes also pointed to a wider issue if Arsenal were to sell their academy graduate, who can play at left-back and in central midfield.

He added: 'It reminds me a little bit of when Danny Welbeck left Manchester United. I hated it, didn’t like it.

'Now, Danny was a little bit older than Myles Lewis-Skelly, but when you’re losing your own players, it’s disappointing.'

Jamie Carragher agreed with Scholes' thoughts and admitted he was left shocked by the reports.

He said 'Do you think it’s from his side or the club’s side? That’s the thing that was a little bit strange about it. It felt almost like Arsenal offered Manchester United Myles Lewis-Skelly.

'It wasn’t Myles Lewis-Skelly saying I want to leave or his people putting something out. That’s where the shock came from.

'I still can’t believe it. Obviously, last season wasn’t great for him for the whole season, but when a young player has already put in performances like I’ve seen him put in at the Bernabeu...

'He was running the game at the Bernabeu from left-back and then his performance in the Champions League final in central midfield against Paris Saint-Germain.'

Scholes felt Arsenal should move on Martin Zubimendi instead of the young Englishman

Carragher continued: 'You can’t play at that level unless you’re pretty special at that age. All young players have ups and downs. Last season he didn’t play as much as he probably would have liked.

'But, as you just said, his ceiling is so high for the performances he’s already put in as a kid. I couldn’t believe that Arsenal would even think about letting him go.'

When pressed on Lewis-Skelly's future earlier this week, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta refused to give anything away.

'I’m not going to talk about any speculation,' he said. ‘If there is a speculation about our players, that’s a good sign. That means that we attract attention and they’re doing a good job.’

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson takes off medal during live BBC interview after crushing defeat
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson takes off medal during live BBC interview after crushing defeat

Keely Hodgkinson had mixed emotions after finishing as runner-up in the 800m in the European Championships

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson removed her silver medal after finishing second in the 800m at the European Championships. (Image: BBC)

Keely Hodgkinson made her feelings crystal clear after finishing runner-up in the 800m final at the European Championships in Birmingham tonight. The Olympic and defending champion ran a 1:55:01 but it wasn't enough to retain her crown in a tightly fought race.

‌



Swiss star Audrey Werro recovered from a dramatic fall in her semi-final race to run a 1:54.81 and set a new Championship record, boasting too much in the tank for her Team GB rival. Femke Broeders-Bol rounded off the top three and set a new national record for the Netherlands having only switched from 400m to 800m recently.

‌



Hodgkinson could not hide her disappointment in an interview after the race, removing her silver medal after missing out on the one she wanted.

‌



Keely Hodgkinson misses out European Championships gold medal in thrilling 800m final READ MORE :

As Amy Hunt strives to be fastest woman in the world ex teammate backs her for Olympic gold READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking after the race, Hodgkinson took off her medal and told the BBC: "I'm kidding, that was a joke. Yeah, a bit of mixed emotions. I think with that level of competition, any medal is a really good achievement.

"So another one to add to my collection. I can never be disappointed with that. But yeah, I'm defending champion, so I wanted to do that.

‌



"I knew it was going to come down to the wire. I really thought I was going to win today, but I guess it just wasn't meant to be. I didn't do anything wrong. It's just one of those things."

View 2 Images (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Werro led the race from the outset and when asked whether that was part of the plan, Hodgkinson said: "I think there were so many different ways it could play out.

‌



"It was all down to figuring out the first 100 metres. Audrey wanted to take it on. With that wind, I was happy to let her.

"But yeah, we're all really great athletes and I knew it was going to be close. I look forward to the next match-up."

Despite finishing second, the 24-year-old said competing against such a high calibre of athletes brings out the best of her.

‌



She said: "I've said all year it's really motivating to be in such a competitive event. I love it. I think it brings out the best in me.

"Championship racing is what it's all about. You don't know how it's going to go. Some people can have a good day. Some people can have a bad day.

"I had a pretty good day today, I think. It just didn't go the way that I wanted it to."

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson misses out European Championships gold medal in thrilling 800m final
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson misses out European Championships gold medal in thrilling 800m final

The women's 800m was one of the most anticipated events of the European Athletics Championships, as it promised a thrilling three-battle between Keely Hodgkinson, Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson went into the final as a two-time defending champion (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Great Britain's Keely Hodgkinson narrowly missed out a home gold medal in the women's 800m final at the European Athletics Championships. Hodgkinson, 24, came second behind the supreme Audrey Werro in her bid a three-time European champion at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham.

‌



Swiss sensation Werro recovered from a dramatic fall during her semi-final on Thursday afternoon to clinch the gold medal with a rapid time of 1:54.81. Hodgkinson made the fastest start under the Friday-night lights but had the 22-year-old on her shoulder.

‌



On the final lap, Werro made her move and gained the lead. Hodgkinson pushed to make it a dramatic finish but couldn't pip her rival to the finish line and had to settle for silver.

‌



Meanwhile, Femke Broeders-Bol set a new national record for the Netherlands as she earned bronze. Hodgkinson was all smiles after the final, although she jokingly took her silver medal off during an interview.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"It was a great race, I love a good challenge and that's what it was," the Atherton-born star reflected. "I have mixed emotions. With that level of competition, any medal is a good achievement. Another one to add to my collection and I can never be disappointed with that.

"I knew it was going to come down to the wire and I really wanted to win. I guess it just wasn't meant to be. There were so many ways it could have played out. Audrey wanted to take it on, with that wind I was happy to let her. We are all great athletes and I look forward to the next match-up.

"I've said all year it's really motivating to be in such a competitive event. I love it, it's such a competitive event. I had a pretty good day, it just didn't quite go the way I wanted it to."

‌



View 2 Images Audrey Werro pipped Keely Hodgkinson to claim gold in Birmingham (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

As for Werro, who ran the fastest time for 43 years earlier this season, she picked up her first senior international gold medal. But the rising star's chances of even racing were plunged into doubt following her aforementioned fall.

Werro was holding the inside line in a crowded field before disaster struck, as she went down due to an 'unintentional touch' involving Werro and France's Anais Bourgoin. Following a review, Werro and Lithuania's Gabija Galvydyte were reinstated to the final.

Article continues below

The organisers explained: "The incident resulted in the fall of two athletes, Werro and Galvydyte. Having reviewed the circumstances, the referee decided to qualify both athletes in accordance with the applicable rules."

Reflecting on Werro's final performance, Paula Radcliffe told BBC One: "Audrey Werro is young still and that was a huge amount of pressure even without the fall, without the bruising and then to pull it together to take the race by the scruff of the neck, which I think Keely did intend for her to do but she thought she could come back at her. But Werro had another gear."

Sports.title: Inside Ruben Amorim's 14 months at Man Utd – Smashed TV, quit threats, Grimsby debacle
Sports.content:
Inside Ruben Amorim's 14 months at Man Utd – Smashed TV, quit threats, Grimsby debacle

Ruben Amorim is all set to face former club Manchester United with AC Milan, seven months after his turbulent Old Trafford tenure came to an end

View 5 Images Ruben Amorim endured a torrid 14 months as Manchester United manager (Image: Getty)

Ruben Amorim will be reunited with Manchester United on Saturday afternoon as his AC Milan side takes them on in a pre-season friendly. The Italian club appointed the Portuguese as their head coach in June, just five months after he was sacked by United following a disastrous spell in charge.

‌



The 41-year-old was highly thought of before taking the United job due to his success with Sporting CP and arrived bright-eyed and bushy-tailed. But thanks to his own actions and the wider chaos at the club, he endured a miserable time at Old Trafford.

‌



His opposite number in the dugout for Saturday's friendly is Michael Carrick, whose relative success with United since January has only evoked more negative feelings towards Amorim's own dismal reign.

‌



Ahead of what will surely be a strange reunion for the manager in Poland - and one he will be desperate to emerge victorious from- Mirror Football takes a look back at Amorim's turbulent reign as United boss and how his time with the club unravelled.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

Smashed TV

Having left his top-of-the-table Sporting side in November 2024 to join United mid-season, Amorim quickly realised the monumental scale of his task. A 3-1 home defeat to Brighton in January 2025 marked a seventh loss in his first 15 games in charge.

‌



View 5 Images Amorim had to apologise for his outburst (Image: Getty)

The impact of that on the initially charismatic manager was clear to see as he cut a miserable figure both on the touchline and during post-match interviews. After the loss, Amorim branded his United team the worst in the club's 147-year history - something he quickly admitted he shouldn't have said.

His brutal comments demonstrated his frustration with the lack of progress as United's players failed to adapt to his much-criticised 3-4-2-1 formation. That frustration also spilt out in the dressing room as he damaged a TV used for tactics at half-time in a display of fury.

‌



Whilst he later took responsibility and admitted he would try to do better as a young head coach, the two incidents showed a degree of volatility. They raised questions about whether he had the necessary man-management skills to oversee the difficult project ahead of him, sowing the seeds of future struggles.

Europa League final heartbreak

As the season wore on, United's dreadful form made it increasingly clear that they would not qualify for Europe for the 2025/26 campaign via the Premier League. Winning the Europa League, of which they had reached the final, became of the utmost importance for securing Champions League qualification and getting the club back on the right trajectory.

View 5 Images United finished as runners-up in the Europa League (Image: Getty)

‌



However, Amorim's side showed very little quality in the Bilbao showpiece and were not helped by his selection decisions, including leaving Alejandro Garnacho and Kobbie Mainoo out of the starting line-up. Tottenham secured a 1-0 victory and ended a 17-year trophy drought.

The defeat, along with a 15th-place finish in the league, was a humiliating end to an already exhausting and miserable campaign. Amorim's rigid tactics, questionable man-management and overall negative demeanour led many in the media to demand his sacking. Amorim even said he was willing to walk away the very next day if that's what the board desired.

"In this moment, I am not going to be here defending myself, [it] is not my style," he said. "I cannot do it, is really hard for me. So I have nothing to show to the fans to say I am going to improve because of this, I had these problems, I will not do nothing.

‌



"In this moment, it's a little bit of faith. So let's see. Like I said before, coming here before in the flash, I am always open. If the board and fans feel that I'm not the right guy, I will go the next day without any conversation about compensation. But I will not quit again. I am really confident in my job and, as you can see, I will not change nothing in the way I do things."

INEOS and the United board were desperate to break the club's decade-long cycle of sacking managers every 18-24 months. They stuck with him, believing he deserved a full pre-season and a summer transfer window to shape the squad to his own preference. Crucially, he also still seemed to have the support of the majority of his players.

Grimsby Town debacle

Following a summer where United notably backed him by signing three high-quality forwards in Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, fans expected to see improvements. But after a defeat to Arsenal and a draw at Fulham came perhaps the lowest point in Amorim's United career.

‌



View 5 Images Pressure mounted on Amorim following United's defeat at Grimsby (Image: Getty)

In August 2025, United suffered a shock defeat to League Two side Grimsby Town in the Carabao Cup second round. As his side lost the penalty shootout, images of Amorim hunkering in the dugout rather than showing real leadership became ingrained in viewers' minds.

Memes of him fiddling with his tactics boards against the lower-league opposition also went viral on social media and cries of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the home crowd marked the ultimate humiliation.

‌



Having managed just 17 wins across 45 games. Amorim cut a defeated figure post-match, adding to a sense of foreboding. He said when asked if he understood what had happened at Blundell Park: "No. But I'm the manager. It should be my job to understand what happened." That only added to the general feeling that the United boss was already signalling he was ready to leave.

Quit threats and exit

A period of good form in October proved to be merely a brief respite and poor results quickly returned, with United again finding themselves on a winless run at the turn of the year. His self-deprecating comments, which had become more evident throughout his tenure, became an acceptance that his time at United was destined to be cut short.

He had said earlier in the season: "Sometimes I want to quit, sometimes I want to be here for 20 years, sometimes I love to be with my players, sometimes I don't want to be with them. So, again, I need to improve on that. It's going to be hard. But now I'm good with the next one."

‌



View 5 Images The manager's sacking seemed only a matter of time (Image: Getty)

In the new year, he began to more obviously call out United's hierarchy, seemingly egging them on to scrap his contract. Things came to a head after a 1-1 draw at Elland Road, in what would prove to be his final post-match outburst as the man in charge at Old Trafford.

"I came here to be the manager of Manchester United, not to be the coach of Manchester United. That is clear," Amorim said. "I know that my name is not [Thomas] Tuchel, it's not [Antonio] Conte, it's not [Jose] Mourinho, but I'm the manager of Manchester United. And it's going to be like this for 18 months or when the board decides to change.

‌



"I'm not going to quit. I will do my job until another guy is coming here to replace me. I just want to say that I'm going to be the manager of this team, not just the coach. I was really clear on that. That is going to finish in 18 months, and then everyone is going to move on. Thank you, guys."

United's higher-ups ultimately decided enough was enough and dismissed him the following day, putting an end to his miserable tenure. Under-18s coach Darren Fletcher was brought in as caretaker boss with the club sitting in sixth place.

Carrick stepped in later that month and changed United's fortunes. It is very difficult to imagine the team ever securing Champions League qualification with Amorim at the helm. Now, things will go full circle as the Portuguese boss takes on the man who ultimately supplanted him.
