World.title: CIPM President calls for people-centred transformation of Nigeria’s public service
World.content:
The President and Chairman of the Governing Council of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPM), Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, FCIPM, fnli has called for a fundamental transformation of Nigeria’s public service, anchored on innovation, accountability, participation, inclusion and strategic people management.

The CIPM President made the call while delivering the keynote address at the Ogun State 2026 Public Service Day Celebration Lecture, held at the Cultural Centre, Kuto, Abeokuta, on Thursday, August 13, 2026. The lecture was themed “Transforming the Public Service: Advancing Innovation, Accountability, Participation and Inclusion.”

Speaking to public and civil service leaders, scholars, organised labour, private-sector representatives and other stakeholders, Gobir emphasised that the ultimate purpose of public service is not merely to process paperwork, but to improve citizens’ lives.

He noted that citizens experience government primarily through the quality of public services they receive, stressing that “Government is an idea. Public service is its experience.” He therefore urged public institutions to move beyond measuring activity and processes to measuring the actual value and impact delivered to citizens.

According to him, innovation in the public service must go beyond simply digitising existing processes. He cautioned against “digitising dysfunction”, noting that technology cannot compensate for institutions that have failed to rethink inefficient processes.

He challenged public-sector leaders to ask whether existing procedures still create public value and encouraged institutions to redesign processes around citizens’ needs rather than institutional convenience.

On accountability, the CIPM President described it as “the mathematics of trust,” emphasising that public institutions must earn citizens’ confidence through competence, fairness, transparency, consistency and responsiveness.

He also stressed the importance of meaningful citizen participation, noting that participation should go beyond inviting citizens to events after decisions have already been made. Rather, citizens should have opportunities to influence decisions that affect their lives.

On inclusion, Gobir called for public services to be designed to accommodate citizens across different socioeconomic, geographic, technological and demographic circumstances. He warned that a service cannot be considered truly inclusive if it is technically available but practically inaccessible to significant segments of the population.

The CIPM President further highlighted the critical role of human resource management in public-sector transformation, noting that no institution can transform beyond the capacity of its people.

He called for a strategic approach to talent management, leadership development, performance management and capability building within the public service.

“The greatest infrastructure of a nation is not concrete. It is capability. Only capable people move institutions.”

He urged public-sector organisations to build workplaces where competence, integrity, innovation and excellence are recognised and rewarded, while challenging leaders to develop the right people and capabilities for emerging public-sector needs.

Speaking specifically on Ogun State, Gobir acknowledged the state’s development ambitions and encouraged it to pursue a model of transformation that goes beyond infrastructure and technology to focus on building institutions that are responsive, effective and centred on citizens.

He distilled the lecture’s theme into four key imperatives: innovation must change the method; accountability must change the culture; participation must change the relationship between government and citizens; and inclusion must change the architecture of public service.

He added that leadership remains central to achieving all four imperatives, stressing that institutions do not transform themselves—people transform institutions, and leaders determine whether those people are empowered, constrained, inspired or ignored.

The CIPM President concluded by calling for a public service where innovation becomes an institutional habit, accountability becomes a professional ethic, participation becomes consequential and inclusion becomes a design principle.

He said the ultimate measure of public-sector reform should not be the number of policies or projects launched, but the number of lives improved and the extent to which citizens can access government services without unnecessary friction.

“The ultimate measure of institutional reform will not be the number of policies launched. It will be the number of lives improved,” he said.

The engagement reinforces CIPM’s commitment to advancing professional human resource management and supporting stronger, more capable and people-centred institutions across Nigeria.

World.title: Outrage grows as stakeholders raise airport security, safety concerns over picketing of Air Peace
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

The decision of aviation unions to picket Nigeria’s largest airline, Air Peace, Tuesday, has elicited sharp criticism from stakeholders in the country’s air transport sector, with many saying the action constituted serious safety and security concerns.



From the early hours of Tuesday until about noon, members of the National Union of Air Transport Employees, NUATE, and the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, ATSSSAN, backed by the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress, TUC, disrupted Air Peace’s operations over the alleged non-remittance of the five per cent Ticket Sales Charge, TSC, to the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, and the right of workers to unionise.



The industrial action followed a series of ultimatums the unions said they issued to the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON. The latest came on August 7, when the unions gave airlines a three day notice, threatening to picket operators that failed to remit the statutory five per cent TSC to the NCAA and allow their staff to join aviation unions.



Acting on the threat, union members converged on the domestic terminals of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, where they singled out Air Peace, blocked access to its counters and prevented the airline’s scheduled flights from departing until the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, intervened.



The action, which disrupted more than half of the airline’s operations that day, left thousands of passengers stranded and caused the airline to lose more than N2 billion in revenue.

Memories



The incident, which sparked debate over the implications of industrial disputes for aviation safety, airport security and passenger confidence, revived memories of previous occasions when labour disputes led to the disruption of airline operations, exposing travellers to the fallout.



Over a decade ago, precisely March 13, 2013, members of NUATE and ATSSSAN grounded Aero Contractors’ operations over allegations of poor staff welfare and anti-union practices. The action stranded more than 100 passengers at the Domestic Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport 2, MMA2, in Lagos.



On March 23, 2017, aviation unions also grounded Arik Air’s operations at the General Aviation Terminal, GAT, of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Three years later, specifically on September 13, 2020, NUATE and ATSSSAN again disrupted Arik Air’s operations by barricading the entrance to the airline’s operational headquarters in Lagos over unresolved labour issues.

Passengers lament



However, passengers caught in the disruption that happened on Tuesday were left to grapple with missed appointments and what could be an unexpected financial loss. Speaking to Saturday Vanguard, a passenger who simply identified himself as Chinedu said: “I had a flight for 7:00 am. My mum fell sick last night (Monday) and she was rushed to the hospital. I had hoped that I would get to Abuja early today so that I could look after her, as my siblings are not there to do so.”



Kitty Kat, who took to X to express her frustration, said: “I received a flight reminder at 2 am both via text and email only to arrive at the airport and encounter this development. No proper information, no communication from the airline. We’re just being told that no Air Peace aircraft is leaving the airport today, regardless of your destination. Honestly, this is beyond frustration. You plan, you prepare, you get to the airport on time, and then this happens with zero explanation.”

Experts’ views



Commenting on the issue, former commandant of the Murtala Mohammed International Airport, Lagos, Group Captain John Ojikutu, retd, described the unions’ action as unlawful.



Ojikutu, in a chat with Saturday Vanguard, also called for regulations prohibiting acts of unlawful interference with aviation activities at airports.



He said: “As far as I am concerned, there is a regulatory authority in aviation and that is the NCAA. Aviation is governed by international law. That is why I said it is the negligence of the NCAA that resulted in the action. The NCAA should produce a law that removes acts of unlawful interference in the activities of aviation in the airport. Or put it as a guideline for the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN.



“If they (the unions) have to picket the airline, let them go to the airline’s office, not the airport. The airline has an office outside the airport. They should go there and protest there. The picketing did not affect only Air Peace; it also affected others. It has a negative effect on this country. I am surprised that the NCAA is not treating this as its responsibility.



“Suppose there were people who had infiltrated them (the unions). I am also surprised that the DSS was there and did not look into it. What is aviation? Aviation is a national security asset.

Contempt



For former Acting Director-General/Managing Director of the NCAA, Engr Benedict Adeyileka, the unions acted in contempt of court because there was a subsisting judgment of the Federal High Court on Air Peace and the unions.



Speaking to Saturday Vanguard, Adeyileka said: “From a neutral and a regulatory point of view: the minister, to the best of my knowledge, had intervened in the issue. They were all still in the process of talking about strike or no strike and remittance or no remittance. However, if you want to picket, take it completely away from the restricted areas. Moreover, the court had given an order. That is contempt of court, and it is a very serious thing.



“The unions are saying that some airlines owe money. Are they the collecting agency? There are legal avenues through which the NCAA can recover its money. They can go to court and obtain judgments, after which court bailiffs can lawfully seize assets equivalent to the amount owed. There is also an allegation that Air Peace and some other airlines do not allow unions in their organisations. But being a member of a union is voluntary.”

Airline’s position



Meanwhile, Air Peace’s Chief Operating Officer, Mrs Oluwatoyin Olajide, warned that if affected passengers seek compensation over the disruption, the unions responsible for the picketing should be held liable for the consequences of their actions.

World.title: NDC primaries: Leadership moves to heal wounds, avert defections
World.content:
By Juliet Umeh

The National Democratic Congress, NDC, has commenced moves to reconcile aggrieved aspirants following its recent primaries, as the party seeks to heal internal wounds and avert possible defections ahead of the 2027 general elections.



A chieftain of the party, Patrice Akwara, who spoke on Arise Television Friday, said reconciliation committees had been constituted at the national and regional levels to address grievances and unite members.



Akwara said some aspirants were disappointed after losing the contests, particularly after investing financial and emotional resources in their campaigns. He, however, said the party would persuade aggrieved members to remain and work for its success in 2027.



According to him, the challenges were normal “teething problems” associated with a new political organisation. “From an observer’s point of view, we expect internal reconciliation to smoothen some of the rough edges and some of the issues that arose during the primaries.



“NDC is a very new organisation and, like every newborn baby or every new organisation, there are always teething problems. NDC is not immune to such things,” he said.



Akwara said the committees would “weave the party together” by resolving issues capable of weakening its unity. He explained that grievances were inevitable in competitive primaries, stressing that unsuccessful aspirants should support whoever emerged as the party’s candidate.



“The primaries are like any other competition. You win some, you lose some. If you lose, you didn’t actually lose. It’s just that somebody has to fly the flag of the party, so that everybody will come together,” he said.



On reports that some candidates could not find their names on the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, portal, Akwara attributed the situation to technical glitches during the uploading process.



“There are some glitches and at the point of uploading some names, the timeline caught up with those uploading and some names appeared vacant,” he said. He, however, expressed confidence that the affected candidates would be properly captured, citing statutory provisions allowing such corrections.

“There is no cause for alarm. I don’t think we’re alarmed,” he said.



On possible defections by aggrieved aspirants, Akwara said the leadership had made arrangements to retain them. “Associations like political parties are like a market square – free entry, free exit. But I can assure you that the national leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, and his team have made adequate arrangements to ensure that every aggrieved aspirant, every aggrieved member, is persuaded to still remain in the party,” he said.



Akwara said the party’s larger objective was to help rebuild Nigeria and restore confidence in its economic system. He urged members to look beyond the primaries, saying: “What lies ahead is much better, it’s much to be fought for than what is behind.”

World.title: Omo-Agege, Iyovwaye allegedly escape assassination bid in Delta community
World.content:
Senator Ovie Omo-Agege

By Jimitota Onoyume

The Delta central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and the governorship candidate of the party in the state , Deacon Chris Iyovwaye, have escaped alleged assassination attempt.



Senator Omo-Agege disclosed this yesterday , saying the incident occured at Usiefuru community, Ughelli South Local Government Area on Thursday where they went for political activities.



Omo-Agege in a statement expressed gratitude to God for the failed assassination bid, noting that six other members of his party however sustained injuries.



He alleged that suspected thugs sponsored by a rival political party opened fire at them during their visit to the community.



According to his statement, “Yesterday, Thursday, August 13, 2026, armed men attempted to take my life in Usiefrun, Ughelli South LGA. They also targeted Deacon Chris Iyovwaye, our NDC Governorship Candidate, and other members of the NDC leadership in Delta. Thankfully, by God’s grace, they failed.



“In Usiefrun, thugs opened fire on NDC members who had gathered to welcome us during our tour of Delta Central. Let it be on record: I was the main target. Six NDC members were injured, including Mr. Believe Biadoyo, Mr. Joshua Oghenetega Oyibocha, Owhos Peter, Ojiyovwin Dennis and two others “, he said.



Assuring that they would not be intimidated, OmoAgege enjoined the police to bring those behind the alleged assassination bid on him and the governorship candidate of his party, the NDC to book.



“We refuse to be intimidated or silenced. Our ward-to-ward visits across Delta Central Senatorial District will continue”, he added.



The police had not reacted to this allegation as at the time of filing this report. Senator Omo-Agege was a former deputy president of the Senate and a governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the state during the last governorship election.

World.title: Trump says US may take control of Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
US President Donald Trump speaks during a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on July 21, 2026. (Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP)

President Donald Trump has said the United States could take control of the strategically important Strait of Hormuz after what he described as the defeat of Iran.

Trump made the remark on Friday during a political rally at a police academy in New York State, where he told supporters that he would soon declare the waterway a US territory.

“After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated, pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States,” Trump said, drawing cheers from the audience.

“It’s true,” he added.

The comments came amid escalating tensions over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital international waterway linking the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and a major route for global energy shipments.

Trump said the United States had effectively imposed a blockade on Iranian ports as part of efforts to pressure Tehran economically.

“We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to,” he told the gathering.

The development follows the outbreak of hostilities between the United States, Israel and Iran, with Washington and Tel Aviv saying their military campaign was aimed at curbing Iran’s nuclear programme and weakening its ability to threaten regional security.

Iran has retaliated with attacks and increased military activity around the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns over the safety of commercial shipping through the waterway.

The strait is considered one of the world’s most strategically important maritime routes, with a substantial share of global oil and gas shipments passing through it.

Trump’s latest comments suggest that Washington may seek a more direct role in controlling access to the waterway as the confrontation with Iran continues.

AFP

World.title: Why we’re worried over Osun governorship election — CISLAC
World.content:
Raises concerns over violence, intimidation, vote buying, military deployment

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) has expressed concern over the growing threat of electoral violence, political intimidation and vote buying ahead of Saturday’s governorship election in Osun State.

CISLAC, in a statement by its Executive Director, Auwal Rafsanjani, said its concerns were based on independent monitoring, media reports and ongoing assessments of the electoral environment in the state.

The organisation said reports of killings, shootings, clashes, attacks on political gatherings, destruction of property and other forms of intimidation had emerged from different parts of Osun in recent months.

While noting that the circumstances surrounding some of the incidents and those responsible remained subject to investigation, CISLAC said the reported loss of lives and rising tensions underscored the urgent need for stakeholders to prioritise peace and the protection of citizens.

Rafsanjani said the organisation was particularly concerned about the alleged recruitment, financing and deployment of political thugs and other agents of violence to intimidate voters, attack opponents, disrupt political activities and influence electoral outcomes.

He warned that such practices could create an atmosphere of fear and prevent citizens from exercising their constitutional right to vote freely and peacefully.

Vote buying

CISLAC also raised concerns over the alleged commercialisation of the electoral process, saying vote buying exploits economic hardship and the vulnerability of citizens.

It warned that treating votes as commodities could reduce democracy to a transaction rather than a genuine expression of the people’s will.

On recent arrests linked to alleged electoral offences, Rafsanjani said the development, including the reported recovery of cash, Permanent Voter Cards and voter registers, underscored the need for increased vigilance by law enforcement and electoral authorities.

He urged authorities to investigate allegations of electoral offences transparently and prosecute offenders strictly in accordance with the law, without political favour or discrimination.

Concern over military deployment

The organisation also expressed concern over reports of the deployment of military personnel to the Osun State office of the Independent National Electoral Commission ahead of the election.

CISLAC acknowledged that extraordinary security measures might be necessary where there were credible threats to lives, electoral materials or critical infrastructure.

It, however, insisted that any military deployment in connection with an election must have a clear legal and operational basis and remain within its defined mandate.

The organisation called for such deployment to be guided by neutrality, proportionality and respect for citizens’ rights.

“CISLAC therefore calls on the relevant authorities to clearly communicate the purpose, scope and legal basis of the military presence at the INEC office and to ensure that the deployment does not interfere with the independence of electoral officials, intimidate voters or undermine public confidence in the neutrality of the electoral process,” Rafsanjani said.

He also urged all security agencies deployed for the election to operate under clear rules of engagement, respect fundamental rights and maintain professionalism and political neutrality.

Calls for peaceful election

CISLAC said the combination of violence, intimidation, vote buying and heightened security concerns posed a serious threat to the credibility of the election and could have wider implications for Nigeria’s democratic development ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The organisation urged candidates, political actors, supporters and other stakeholders to reject violence, demobilise agents of intimidation, avoid inflammatory rhetoric and commit themselves to peaceful and issue-based participation.

It called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to maintain strict neutrality, intensify intelligence-led operations in identified high-risk areas, protect voters and electoral personnel, investigate reported killings and attacks, and prosecute anyone found culpable, regardless of political affiliation or status.

CISLAC also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure that all aspects of the election were conducted transparently, securely and in accordance with established laws and guidelines.

The organisation called on the National Peace Committee, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and the media to intensify peace advocacy, voter education and public awareness campaigns against electoral violence and vote buying.

It also appealed to Osun residents to reject violence, intimidation and electoral inducements and exercise their right to vote freely, peacefully and responsibly.

CISLAC reaffirmed its commitment to monitoring developments before, during and after the election, while advocating transparency, accountability, peaceful participation and credible democratic processes.

“Democracy can only thrive when citizens are able to express their choices freely, without fear, intimidation or financial coercion,” Rafsanjani said.

World.title: Gombe Govt rejects N133bn–N138bn water spending claim
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Gombe State Government has rejected claims that it spent between N133 billion and N138 billion on water supply projects, describing the figures as inaccurate and misleading.

The government said the figures in circulation appeared to lump together recurrent expenditure, capital allocations, inherited contractual obligations, development-partner interventions and budgetary provisions without distinguishing between funds appropriated and actual expenditure.

In a statement issued on Friday night by the Director-General, Press Affairs, Government House, Gombe, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the government said the clarification was aimed at providing the public with an accurate account of its investments and interventions in the water sector.

According to the statement, water supply has remained a longstanding challenge in the state due to population growth, urban expansion, ageing infrastructure, inadequate storage capacity, rising energy costs and a distribution network originally designed for a much smaller population.

It said the administration of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, since assuming office in 2019, had adopted a phased approach covering water production, treatment, storage, transmission, distribution, energy supply, metering, maintenance and institutional capacity.

The government recalled that Yahaya made the Gombe State Water Board and Dadin Kowa Water Treatment Plant among his early points of inspection after assuming office, following concerns over the poor performance of existing facilities.

It said the assessment identified inadequate production and storage capacity, ageing infrastructure, unreliable electricity supply, limitations in the transmission and distribution network and other operational challenges.

The administration subsequently constituted a Water Supply Task Force, headed by Engineer Abubakar Bappa, to undertake a comprehensive assessment and recommend sustainable interventions.

Government explains expenditure figures

The government said the N133 billion to N138 billion figure being cited did not represent actual expenditure on a single water programme.

It said the administration inherited an outstanding contractual obligation of about N5 billion to CGC, the company responsible for operating and maintaining the Dadin Kowa facility.

It added that recurrent and subvention-related commitments between 2019 and 2025 to sustain water infrastructure amounted to more than N9.5 billion.

The government argued that such operational expenditure should not be presented as capital expenditure on new water infrastructure.

Capital investments, donor interventions

The statement said substantial capital provisions had been made between 2020 and 2025 for water infrastructure, including piped-water expansion, borehole development and interventions implemented through the Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency, RUWASSA, and development partners.

It noted that Gombe was among states benefiting from World Bank-supported interventions under the Programme-for-Results component of the Sustainable Urban and Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene programme, SURWASH.

According to the government, the interventions had contributed to the drilling and rehabilitation of hundreds of boreholes across communities.

N88.4bn 2026 budget provision

On the N88.4 billion figure referenced in some commentaries, the government explained that it represented a broader 2026 budgetary provision covering the Ministry of Water Resources, Environment and Forest Resources and agencies under its supervision.

These include the Gombe State Water Board, RUWASSA, SURWASH, the Gombe State Environmental Protection Agency and other related programmes.

The government said the provision covered several interventions involving water, energy and environmental infrastructure, including conversion of water facilities to solar and hybrid power, rehabilitation and expansion of the Malam Inna Water Scheme, rehabilitation of industrial boreholes serving the northern axis and water infrastructure for the Agro-Livestock Development Zone.

It stressed that a budgetary provision was not synonymous with expenditure already incurred, just as a sector-wide allocation could not automatically be attributed to a single project.

N11.4bn Regional Water Expansion Project

The administration also highlighted the N11.4 billion Gombe State Regional Water Expansion Project, implemented in collaboration with the Federal Government under a 70:30 funding arrangement.

According to the statement, the project, awarded to Jidadu Ventures Nigeria Limited, had been completed and was undergoing test-running ahead of its formal transition to the appointed operator for operation and maintenance.

At Wuro Juli, the project provided 14 new boreholes, conversion of 14 existing pumps to hybrid systems, a packaged water treatment plant with a capacity of 200 cubic metres per hour, hybrid pumping systems and solar, generator and grid power arrangements.

The intervention at the Special Development Zone included 1,000 cubic metres of surface storage, 500 cubic metres of overhead storage, new pumping infrastructure and hybrid power systems.

The project also covered Tunfure, where additional storage and hybrid pumping infrastructure were provided, alongside a five-kilometre pipeline connection to the NTA Booster Station.

At the NTA Booster Station, the intervention included rehabilitation of existing facilities, additional storage, hybrid pumping and power infrastructure, as well as a six-kilometre pipeline extension towards the International Conference Centre.

The government said the project also incorporated network expansion, pressure-control infrastructure, smart metering, water-data management, maintenance equipment, staff training, network mapping and digitisation.

Govt tackles power challenge

According to the statement, unreliable and expensive electricity remained one of the major constraints to water production and distribution in Gombe.

It said the government had therefore prioritised independent hybrid power infrastructure for critical water facilities, particularly the Dadin Kowa system.

The administration said the previous arrangement could require more than N500 million monthly for water treatment, production and pumping from Dadin Kowa to Gombe, making energy reform necessary for the sustainability of the water system.

N54.66bn new water, power investments

The government further disclosed that contracts valued at approximately N54.66 billion had recently been approved for major water and power infrastructure projects.

It said N24.26 billion was earmarked for the rehabilitation, upgrading and expansion of water infrastructure at Malam Inna, Gombe metropolis and the Agro-Livestock Development Zone.

The project includes rehabilitation of nine existing boreholes, drilling of 11 new boreholes, solar-powered hybrid pumping systems, upgraded treatment and pumping facilities, a new 4,000-cubic-metre ground storage tank, additional reservoirs, about three kilometres of transmission pipelines and more than 50 kilometres of distribution pipelines.

A further N7.07 billion contract awarded to Ceylon Construction Services Limited is targeted at strengthening dedicated power infrastructure at Dadin Kowa and Tabra.

The government also said N23.33 billion had been committed to solar power infrastructure through a contract awarded to Off-grid Electric Nigeria Limited.

It said the objective was to establish a more resilient hybrid energy system for critical water facilities, reduce dependence on conventional energy sources and lower operating costs.

Government calls for evidence-based scrutiny

The administration said it welcomed scrutiny of its projects and expenditure but urged critics to base allegations of financial mismanagement on verifiable documents.

It argued that claims of N133 billion to N138 billion expenditure should be supported with appropriation laws, releases, expenditure records, payment certificates, contract documents and audited accounts.

In a separate reaction, Hon. Aminu Turaki also challenged those circulating the alleged N138 billion figure to provide documentary evidence to substantiate the claim.

Turaki said political criticism of government was legitimate but maintained that allegations concerning public expenditure should be subjected to documentary verification.

He specifically called for clarification on the actual amount paid, certified work, project completion status and operational infrastructure under the N11.491 billion Regional Water Supply Scheme.

The government said its water programme was designed to address the structural challenges affecting water supply by combining investments in production, treatment, power, pumping, storage, transmission, distribution, metering and maintenance.

It expressed optimism that the completed and ongoing projects would improve water production, storage capacity, distribution coverage, pressure and reliability across Gombe State.

Ultimately, the government said, the success of the investments would be measured not merely by the value of contracts awarded or projects announced, but by completed infrastructure, verifiable expenditure and sustained improvement in access to potable water.

World.title: Senate committee leads National Assembly delegation to monitor Osun poll
World.content:
Senate

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Electoral Matters has led a delegation of the Joint National Assembly Committee on Electoral Matters on an oversight visit to Osun State ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

The delegation, led by the committee chairman, Senator Simon Lalong (APC, Plateau South), visited the state on Thursday as part of efforts to assess the preparedness of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the off-cycle election.

A statement issued on Friday by Lalong’s Media Office said the visit was conducted in line with the oversight powers vested in the National Assembly under Section 88 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended.

Members of the delegation, comprising senators and members of the House of Representatives, were received by the Osun State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Barrister Babalola, and other national commissioners deployed to the state for the election.

Lalong said the purpose of the visit was to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of INEC’s level of preparedness and identify any challenges that could affect the conduct of the election.

He said the exercise was also aimed at ensuring that the electoral process met the required standards for a free, fair and credible election.

The committee was briefed on security arrangements, as well as the deployment of sensitive electoral materials to polling units across the state.

According to the statement, INEC officials assured the delegation that the commission was fully prepared to conduct the election.

The committee noted the issues raised during the briefing and pledged to initiate further legislative action where necessary.

The delegation is expected to continue its oversight activities as stakeholders make final preparations for Saturday’s election.

World.title: Indigenous Itsekiri Brands Rally Behind Itsekiri Global Homecoming 2026
World.content:
In a strong demonstration of community pride and homegrown enterprise, leading indigenous Itsekiri brands are rallying behind the Itsekiri Global Homecoming (IGHC), lending their platforms, expertise and resources to support the landmark celebration taking place across the Warri Kingdom, Delta State, from August 16 to 23, 2026.

The homecoming, held under the authority of His Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatse III, the Olu of Warri, and under the auspices of The Royal Order of Iwere (ROI), will bring together Itsekiri sons, daughters, friends and global allies for a week-long celebration of heritage, culture, community and the future of the Warri Kingdom, while commemorating the fifth Coronation Anniversary of His Majesty.



Among the indigenous Itsekiri businesses supporting the Homecoming are Overland Airways, VouchLinks and REYON Water-each bringing its expertise to help deliver a memorable experience for guests across Nigeria and the global diaspora.

Overland Airways is supporting the movement of guests travelling into the region, and connecting returning Itsekiris, visitors and other guests to the Homecoming. On its own, VouchLinks, a Nigerian peer-to-peer recommendation platform, is supporting the celebration through its digital platform and innovative approach to trusted recommendations. REYON Water is supporting the week as the hydration partner, helping to ensure that guests are catered for across the various Homecoming events.

Joining the growing network of partners is also Agile Cycle, an indigenous electric mobility venture, and the Official Mobility Partner of the Homecoming.

The organisers said that Agile Cycle would support mobility throughout the week, including the highly anticipated Scooter Ride event with His Majesty, Ogiame Atuwatse III, one of the Homecoming’s most talked-about signature experiences. “The activation reflects Agile Cycle’s commitment to smart, sustainable mobility and its vision of getting people moving through accessible, innovative solutions.

“The growing support from indigenous businesses is complemented by a wider network of brands and organisations that have also come on board. Other partners include MAGGI® (Nestlé Nigeria), Sterling Bank, Seaman’s Schnapps, Loatsad Promomedia, Enugu Air, and ORÍKÌ, alongside other supporting organisations contributing to the success of the Homecoming,” the organisers stated.

Speaking on the growing support for the event, a member of The Royal Order of Iwere (ROI) and IGHC Organising Committee, Ade Mabo, expressed appreciation to the indigenous Itsekiri businesses and other organisations supporting the initiative.

According to him, “It is deeply encouraging to see indigenous Itsekiri brands and organisations nationwide recognise the significance of the Itsekiri Global Homecoming, and choose to support it. “Their involvement reflects the strength of our entrepreneurial community and the shared belief that we can come together to celebrate our heritage while creating meaningful opportunities for our people and our Kingdom. We are sincerely grateful to every partner lending their platform, expertise and resources to make this Homecoming possible.”

He added that the Itsekiri Global Homecoming (IGHC) would feature a rich programme of royal pageantry, cultural showcases, culinary experiences, business and development conversations, heritage tours, entertainment and the iconic Royal Warri River Regatta, culminating in celebrations marking the 5th Coronation Anniversary of His Majesty, the Olu of Warri.

“With indigenous businesses and leading brands continuing to rally behind the initiative, the Homecoming is building momentum as a major platform for celebrating Iwere heritage, strengthening connections, supporting enterprise and showcasing the Warri Kingdom to Nigeria and the world. Learn more on our social media for live updates from the IGHC week in Warri,” he stated.

World.title: Osun Poll: Police Announce 42-Hour Restriction of Movement in Osun
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

As Osun voters go to the polls today to elect a governor who will drive the state’s development agenda and economic prosperity over the next four years, the Nigeria Police Force has announced a 42-hour restriction of movement from 12:00 midnight on Friday, 14 August 2026, until 6:00 p.m. on Saturday, 15 August 2026, as part of comprehensive measures to ensure the peaceful, secure and orderly conduct of the election.

The Force therefore urged the public to comply fully with the restriction and cooperate with security personnel deployed across the state, stating that only persons specifically exempted by the restriction order would be permitted to move during the period. The Police, however, was silent on the categories of persons covered by the exemption.

According to a statement by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, the Force also reiterated the prohibition on the participation of Amotekun and other non-state security actors in election-related security operations.

The Force emphasised that only security agencies recognised and established under the Constitution and laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria are authorised to perform security and law-enforcement duties alongside the Nigeria Police Force in connection with the election.

“No non-state security group, vigilante organisation or other unauthorised body is permitted to assume or exercise the functions of a recognised security agency. Accordingly, such groups are directed to stay away from election-related security operations and refrain from any activity capable of intimidating voters, disrupting the electoral process or undermining public peace and security,” the statement said.

The Force advised political parties, candidates, supporters and other stakeholders to conduct themselves peacefully and responsibly and refrain from any act capable of causing violence or disrupting the electoral process.

CSP Anietie said the Force reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining peace, security and a level playing field for all political actors and eligible voters throughout the electoral process.

He urged the public to remain calm, law-abiding and cooperative, and to promptly report any suspicious or unlawful activity to constitutionally and legally recognised security agencies.

World.title: Tinubu To Diaspora Nigerians: Make Investing in Nigeria A Priority
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerians in the Diaspora to consider the country a prime destination for their investments, expertise, and entrepreneurial initiatives.

Speaking Friday while declaring open a three-day Nigeria Diaspora Economic Conference (NIDEC) 2026 at the Apollo Convention Centre, Toronto, Canada, the President who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila,

assured them that the administration’s ongoing reforms are designed to strengthen the economy, improve the business environment, and unlock opportunities for sustainable investment.

Tinubu commended Nigerians in the diaspora for their courage, enterprise, resilience, and outstanding contributions to the global economy and Nigeria’s image.

The President described Nigerians in the Diaspora as important ambassadors of the country, noting that their accomplishments across different fields of endeavour demonstrate the talent, ingenuity and determination of the Nigerian people.

He said the Federal Government recognises the immense economic, intellectual, and professional value of Nigerians in the Diaspora, affirming his administration’s commitment to creating an environment that enables Nigerians at home and abroad to contribute meaningfully to national development.

Speaking on the conference, themed “Thrive Abroad, Invest in Nigeria,” Tinubu commended Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman/CEO of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM), and her team for convening the first-ever conference.

The President said economic power earns the diaspora a seat and a voice at the conversation table, pointing to diaspora voting as one issue that could be influenced once that economic power is established.

“Nigeria sees you. Nigeria values you. Nigeria needs you, ” the President told hundreds of Nigerians and other stakeholders gathered in Toronto.

Tinubu particularly encouraged them to bring home not only their capital, but also their knowledge, technology, networks and international experience, stressing that such contributions would accelerate Nigeria’s development and create opportunities for younger generations.

He noted that while economic growth, political stability and security remain the primary factors guiding where investors put their money, Nigeria’s indicators point to a country in genuine recovery.

The President cited real GDP growth of 3.89 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, manufacturing expansion of 3.29 per cent, inflation easing to 15.91 per cent, and foreign reserves closing 2025 at 45.4 billion US dollars.

Tinubu said the International Monetary Fund projected Nigeria’s economy to grow by 4.1 per cent in 2026, and credited the past three years of reforms with improving the country’s macroeconomics.

He said the World Bank had similarly acknowledged meaningful progress in restoring macroeconomic stability, strengthening Nigeria’s external and fiscal position, and sustaining growth.

On the domestic front, the President pointed to a new tax architecture designed to simplify compliance and ease the burden on low-income earners and small businesses. He added that the Bank of Industry recorded its highest annual financing volume in 2025, disbursing 636 billion naira to businesses nationwide.

Tinubu said the federal government continues to invest in roads, rail, ports, power, digital connectivity, healthcare, housing, and agricultural value chains, as catalysts for sustainable development.

The President added that remittances, though invaluable in sustaining millions of Nigerian households through school fees, medical bills and small businesses, must now become the floor of diaspora engagement rather than its ceiling.

He called on the diaspora to organise beyond scattered, personality-driven transactions into professionally governed investment clubs, sector funds, co-investment vehicles and venture networks, pooling capital, demanding audited accounts, insisting on proper governance and conducting due diligence with credible professional advisers.

Tinubu said government owed the diaspora predictable rules, transparent project pipelines, efficient consular services and stronger protection from fraud, noting that instruments such as the Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account, the Non-Resident Nigerian Investment Account and the Non-Resident Bank Verification Number were practical steps to ease diaspora participation in the Nigerian financial system.

He, however, appealed for unity ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general election cycle, stressing that while political contest is a feature of democracy, no partisan interest should threaten the country’s stability.

Earlier, Chairman/CEO, Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM), Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, said the conference presented a unique opportunity to deepen engagement with the Nigerian Diaspora by harnessing their expertise for national development and accelerated economic growth.

Dabiri-Erewa urged Nigerians outside the country to see Nigeria not only as home, but also as a destination for investment.

World.title: Building a Legacy: How Abiodun Turned Housing into Engine of Urban Transformation in Ogun
World.content:
By Kayode Akinmade

Drive along the Siun-Sagamu Expressway today and it is easy to miss how recently the landscape around Kobape was little more than open bush. Today, standing prominently on that corridor is Prince Court Estate — a thriving residential community of completed and occupied homes, with its own electricity supply, shopping mall, health centre, ATM gallery and security post.

It is more than an estate.

It is a statement of what housing policy can become when it is conceived not merely as the provision of shelter, but as an instrument of economic development, urban renewal and wealth creation.

That is perhaps the most important story behind the housing transformation taking place quietly across Ogun State under Governor Dapo Abiodun.

When the first phase of Prince Court Estate took shape at Kobape, few would have imagined that it would become the anchor of a rapidly developing residential corridor. The estate has since expanded through four phases, while the surrounding area has recorded significant growth in residential and commercial activity.

The model has subsequently been replicated across the state.

From Idi-Aba in Abeokuta to Sagamu, Itanrin in Ijebu-Ode, Ilaro and the Gateway Aviation Village at Iperu, the Abiodun administration has deliberately spread housing development across Ogun’s three senatorial districts.

The objective is clear: to ensure that the benefits of Ogun’s rapid economic expansion are reflected not only in factories, roads and commercial investments, but also in the quality and availability of homes for the people who live and work in the state.

Housing as economic policy

The significance of the programme lies in its architecture.

The Abiodun administration has approached housing as both a social responsibility and an economic asset. Its portfolio cuts across affordable housing for ordinary families, premium housing for middle- and high-income earners, public-private partnerships, urban regeneration and the redevelopment of underutilised government assets.

The first phase of the Kemta, Idi-Aba scheme, comprising 150 two- and three-bedroom homes, sold out rapidly. That response was an early indication of the enormous pent-up demand for decent and affordable housing in Ogun.

At Kobape, some of the early Prince Court homes were sold to civil servants and members of the public for between about N4.95 million and N5 million. According to figures provided by the state’s housing authorities, similar properties are now worth substantially more on the open market.

That transformation is significant.

It means the government’s intervention did not simply put roofs over people’s heads. For many early beneficiaries, it created an appreciating asset and opened a pathway to household wealth.

In a country where housing remains one of the biggest barriers to economic security for working families, that is a powerful dimension of public policy.

From estates to communities

The most striking feature of the Ogun model is that the government has not treated housing as the construction of isolated blocks of buildings.

Prince Court illustrates the philosophy.

Electricity, healthcare, security, banking and commercial facilities have been integrated into the development, creating a community rather than merely an estate.

That approach matters because modern housing policy is ultimately about the quality of life around the house.

A home without reliable infrastructure, access roads, security, healthcare, commerce and other essential services can quickly become another form of urban vulnerability. But when housing is integrated with these services, it becomes the foundation for a functional community.

This is where the Ogun intervention acquires a broader development significance.

Housing generates demand for roads, electricity, water, retail, transportation, security and other services. Construction itself creates jobs across a long chain of activities involving artisans, engineers, architects, surveyors, suppliers, manufacturers, estate managers and financial institutions.

Every new estate therefore has an economic footprint that extends well beyond the walls of the individual houses.

Unlocking forgotten public assets

The administration’s housing philosophy is perhaps even more evident in its urban regeneration projects at Ibara in Abeokuta and Igbeba in Ijebu-Ode.

For decades, more than 200 civil servants’ quarters constructed over 50 years ago had deteriorated and become largely unusable across approximately 25 hectares of valuable government land.

The Abiodun administration chose not to allow those assets to continue decaying.

Instead, it moved to replace obsolete structures with modern buildings, producing more than 250 smart buildings across the two locations.

The policy significance is substantial.

Government land in prime urban locations is a finite public asset. When buildings on such land become obsolete and unusable, the state faces a choice: continue spending scarce resources maintaining failing structures or redevelop the land in a way that creates new value.

Ogun chose the latter.

The result is not simply new housing. It is the conversion of underutilised public land into productive urban assets, while simultaneously modernising the physical character of some of the state’s most important government layouts.

That is urban regeneration with a balance sheet.

A programme still gathering momentum

Far from winding down, the programme is expanding as the Abiodun administration enters the final stretch of its tenure.

The Ogun State Executive Council has approved another package of projects comprising 450 two-bedroom semi-detached bungalows with supporting infrastructure, 28 official quarters for members of the Ogun State House of Assembly, 28 sellable duplexes at the Ibara Government Reservation Area Scheme II and the reconstruction of the Ogun State Governor’s Lodge in Asokoro, Abuja. (Trending News)

Taken together, the approvals reveal the breadth of the administration’s housing and urban-development strategy.

The 450 bungalows will expand the supply of affordable housing. The Assembly quarters will provide modern accommodation for legislators and preserve institutional assets. The 28 Ibara GRA duplexes will unlock further value from a prime government location, while the reconstruction of the Governor’s Lodge will preserve an important state asset and provide a modern institutional facility.

The projects also reflect a broader government policy of replacing obsolete public infrastructure with modern, functional and durable facilities capable of serving the needs of a growing state.

That policy is particularly relevant to public housing and government quarters inherited from previous decades. Where structures have become severely degraded and rehabilitation is no longer economically sensible, redevelopment offers an opportunity to create more valuable, efficient and sustainable assets.

The new housing projects, meanwhile, extend the administration’s affordable-housing intervention while stimulating activity across the construction value chain.

From contractors and engineers to artisans, manufacturers, suppliers and service providers, housing construction generates employment and creates demand across multiple sectors of the economy.

The Ibara GRA Scheme II duplexes add another dimension: the strategic use of prime public land to generate modern residential assets, attract private investment and strengthen the value of the state’s property portfolio.

In that sense, the latest approvals are not isolated construction projects. They are part of a deliberate policy of combining housing delivery with urban regeneration, institutional development and asset optimisation.

The numbers behind the ambition

The scale of the intervention is reflected in the numbers.

At a briefing in January on the 2026 housing roadmap, the Commissioner for Housing, Jamiu Akande Omoniyi, disclosed that Ogun planned to deliver no fewer than 3,000 additional housing units in 2026, backed by more than N100 billion allocated to the housing sector. The plan forms part of the administration’s broader ambition to deliver 10,000 housing units by 2027. (Punch Newspapers)

The commissioner had also said that more than 4,000 affordable housing units were delivered between 2019 and 2023, with additional units subsequently taking the reported delivery figure above 5,000.

The numbers are important not simply because they represent houses. They represent the scale of public intervention required to respond to a rapidly growing state whose strategic location next to Lagos continues to drive population growth, industrialisation and investment.

Ogun’s housing challenge is therefore inseparable from its economic success.

As more factories, businesses and people move into the state, demand for housing will increase. A government that fails to anticipate that demand risks allowing economic growth to produce housing shortages, informal settlements and uncontrolled urban expansion.

The Abiodun administration’s response has been to get ahead of that curve.

Housing the workforce of a growing economy

There is also a strategic economic dimension to affordable housing.

Ogun has positioned itself as one of Nigeria’s leading investment destinations, with major industrial clusters and expanding commercial activity. But investors do not operate in isolation. Workers need homes. Families need schools and healthcare. Businesses need functioning communities around them.

Housing is therefore part of the infrastructure of investment.

By expanding residential communities around major growth corridors, government is helping to create the conditions for a more balanced relationship between where people work and where they live.

That has implications for productivity, commuting, family welfare and the long-term sustainability of urban growth.

It is why the state’s housing programme should not be viewed as a collection of government estates scattered across Ogun.

It is part of the broader infrastructure supporting the state’s economic transformation.

The legacy taking shape

Perhaps the clearest evidence of the programme’s significance is the way individual projects have begun to alter their surrounding environments.

Kobape is a case in point.

What began as a housing project has become part of a broader residential and commercial ecosystem. The same principle is now being applied in other parts of the state, while the regeneration of Ibara and Igbeba demonstrates that the administration is also looking inward — renewing old government assets rather than endlessly expanding into new land.

This is the policy legacy taking shape.

Governor Abiodun’s housing programme has evolved from providing houses to creating communities; from constructing buildings to unlocking land value; from meeting immediate shelter needs to supporting economic growth; and from developing new estates to regenerating ageing urban centres.

The ambition to reach 10,000 housing units is therefore more than a numerical target. It represents an attempt to institutionalise a housing culture in which government, private developers and residents all participate in expanding the state’s housing stock.

And the programme is not being designed merely as a legacy of photographs and commissioning ceremonies.

The administration has repeatedly affirmed its determination to complete the projects it has initiated before the end of its tenure.

That distinction matters.

A legacy is not defined by what a government announces. It is defined by what remains standing, occupied, functional and valuable after the government has left.

Across Kobape, Kemta, Idi-Aba, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Ilaro, Iperu and the regeneration sites at Ibara and Igbeba, the evidence is increasingly visible.

The quiet transformation of Ogun’s housing sector is, in reality, part of a much larger story — one in which housing has been repositioned from a welfare item on a government balance sheet to an engine of urban renewal, economic participation, asset creation and social stability.

That may ultimately be one of the most enduring dimensions of the Dapo Abiodun legacy.

World.title: Flood: Niger Plans ‘Two Abode’ Policy to Reduce Disaster
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

In order to mitigate the effect of flood in communities the Niger state government is to introduce the “two abode” system of living, especially for people in flood prone areas of the state.

Under the policy, people living in the riverine areas would also be provided residences with social amenities upland where they could relocate their wives and children during rainy seasons, thereby shielding them from overflow of the rivers.

The Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management Dr Ahmed Ibrahim Inga, who disclosed this in Minna on Wednesday explained that the initiative was conceived after the government discovered that many riverine communities were deeply attached to their ancestral settlements because of the water resources that supports their livelihoods.

Dr Inga said government had begun discussions with partners on the modalities for the establishment of the two abode projects, saying that during their relocation women and children would be given special attention because “they are always the most affected during such disasters”.

On the recent flash flood that destroyed hundreds of houses in Minna following a heavy downpour, Inga described the incident as “a major disaster”, adding that government was currently compiling data of victims and property and the extent of damage to determine appropriate assistance for those affected.

Inga however attributed the cause of the incident to indiscriminate construction along waterways, warning residents against erecting structures on natural drainage channels.

“We want to advise people to be more conscious of their attitude towards the environment pointing out that structures are erected alongside waterways.

“The truth is that whatever happens, water will naturally find its way and, in the process, destroy houses and other properties”.

Inga appealed to development partners and the Federal Government to support the state with additional interventions after the ongoing assessment of affected communities is completed by the Niger State Emergency Management Agency.

He also disclosed that the Niger State Emergency Management Agency help desk and offices had been activated across the state to enable residents to report flood-related cases and access timely assistance.

The commissioner said the activation became necessary following the inclusion of Niger among states identified by the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) as being at risk of flooding during the current rainy season.

World.title: Obla Fulfils Promise, Pays £33,000 Tuition, N25m Upkeep for Idoma First-Class Law Graduate
World.content:
Less than a year after making the promise in Otukpo, Chief Godwin Obla, SAN, has fulfilled his pledge to sponsor the first female of Idoma extraction to graduate with a first class from the Nigerian Law School for postgraduate studies abroad.

Through the Godwin Obla Foundation, Obla has paid the full £33,000 tuition for Ochanya, who has been admitted to Queen Mary University of London for an LLM in Artificial Intelligence and the Law.

The tuition was paid directly to the university, while another ₦25 million has been paid into Ochanya’s personal account for her upkeep during her studies in the United Kingdom. The dummy cheques presented to her at a ceremony in Abuja were therefore symbolic of payments already made.

Obla had made the promise at a reception organised in Otukpo by the Association of Idoma Lawyers for newly elevated Senior Advocates of Nigeria of Idoma extraction, where he pledged to mentor and sponsor the first Idoma female to make a first class at the Nigerian Law School for postgraduate studies in any institution in the world.

“Today marks a fulfilment of that promise,” Obla told guests at the Abuja event.

He said: “I can confirm today that her school fees of £33,000 and her upkeep of ₦25 million have been fully paid. The tuition was paid directly to the school’s account and the upkeep to Ochanya’s personal account.”

Obla said the scholarship went beyond rewarding academic excellence and reflected a conviction that Idoma people must deliberately create opportunities for one another.

“As a minority that is overwhelmed by the tyranny of the majority, we must be our brother’s keeper and helper at all times,” he said.

Turning to Ochanya, he added: “This scholarship is a challenge and a call for you to commit to the ideals of carrying others as you have been carried.

“I expect you to be a future burden bearer for our people and to live this ideal all your life.”

Obla said she would also be introduced to members of the Idoma community in the United Kingdom who would provide guidance and support during her stay.

Among those at the presentation were the President General of Ochetoha K’Idoma Forum Worldwide, Professor Yakubu Ochefu; representatives of the Federal University of Health Sciences Teaching Hospital, Otukpo; senior members of the Association of Idoma Lawyers, including Senior Advocates of Nigeria; Moses Onyiloko; as well as Tanya and Sandra, whom Obla welcomed as scholars of the Foundation.

Ochefu commended the Foundation for interventions he said had largely been carried out without much publicity and urged Ochanya to make the most of the opportunity.

He particularly challenged her to pay attention to AI ethics and algorithmic bias from an African perspective, noting the need for Africans to become more involved in shaping the legal and ethical standards governing emerging technologies.

He also assured her that members of the Idoma community in the United Kingdom would be available to support her.

The Foundation’s intervention in Ochanya’s education follows several projects in health and education, including the Judith Ogwa Obla Memorial Kidney Centre at the Federal University of Health Sciences Teaching Hospital, Otukpo, equipped with six dialysis machines and other medical facilities; an ongoing 23-bed VIP and amenity ward at the hospital; a ₦40 million endowment for outstanding medical students at the Federal University of Health Sciences, Otukpo; internet connectivity for the university; and the renovation and equipping of science laboratories and other facilities at St. Francis College, Otukpo. A skills acquisition facility estimated at about ₦1 billion is also being planned.

A Senior Advocate who spoke at the ceremony described Obla’s leadership style as one built around creating opportunities for others rather than seeking accolades, recalling his role in encouraging the emergence of more Senior Advocates of Nigeria from Idoma land.

The gathering also remembered a late female colleague whom members of the Association of Idoma Lawyers had hoped would someday attain the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

Obla commended the leadership of the association and acknowledged the designation of its Vice-President, Moses Onyiloko, for elevation to the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria in 2026.

For Ochanya, studying for a master’s degree abroad was an opportunity she admitted she had never imagined.

She recalled receiving a telephone call from Obla asking about her plans after the Nigerian Law School, only for the conversation to end with an offer to fund her postgraduate studies.

Expressing gratitude to Obla and the Foundation, she said the opportunity had changed the direction of her immediate future.

The message from those at the gathering was, however, consistent: her first class was a beginning, not a destination. She was urged to work hard, remain focused and remember to extend to others the opportunity she had received.

Obla disclosed that the Foundation was already considering where its next scholarship intervention might go, this time outside the legal profession.

“Our next scholar may be in the area of aeronautics,” he said.

“Possibly, we are looking at sponsoring a young Idoma girl as a pilot. Fingers crossed as we work on this.”

World.title: JEF Medical Outreach Delivers 9,601 Interventions to Over 3,000 Osun Residents
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

More than 3,000 residents of Ifewara, Osun State, have benefited from a five-day free medical outreach organised by the Jennifer Etuh Foundation (JEF), with a total of 9,601 medical interventions recorded during the exercise.

The outreach, held in partnership with Pro-Health International, brought together doctors, nurses, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists and other healthcare professionals to provide free medical services to members of the underserved community.

The intervention covered a broad range of services, including medical consultations, routine screening, health education, eye care and surgeries, dental services and other surgical procedures.

The Foundation said the initiative was designed to address some of the barriers that prevent vulnerable Nigerians from accessing timely healthcare, including financial constraints, inadequate health awareness, distance from healthcare facilities and poor health-seeking behaviour.

Beyond providing treatment, the outreach placed significant emphasis on prevention and health education, with members of the community receiving information on healthy lifestyles, disease prevention and the importance of regular medical check-ups.

The Foundation, established in memory of the late Jennifer Ramatu Etuh, has made healthcare interventions for underserved communities a key component of its activities, particularly in improving the wellbeing of women, young girls and other vulnerable groups.

A major feature of the Ifewara outreach was the deployment of digital health data management to complement the medical services.

OLGNova Limited, the Foundation’s data partner, led the digitisation of health information generated during the exercise, replacing reliance on exclusively paper-based records with a centralised digital database.

Through the system, participants’ information was captured, organised and securely stored for subsequent analysis and planning.

The Foundation said the approach improved the accuracy and reliability of health records while creating opportunities for better-informed healthcare planning and continuity of care beyond the outreach.

The deployment of digital data management also highlights the growing importance of technology in community healthcare, particularly in environments where fragmented or paper-based records can make it difficult to track patients, assess health needs and plan future interventions.

The outreach also recorded a significant spiritual dimension, with 629 people making decisions to follow Christ during the programme.

The organisers stressed that the scale of the intervention demonstrated the impact that strategic partnerships between healthcare organisations, volunteers, development partners and community stakeholders could have in closing healthcare gaps among underserved populations.

They called for sustained investment in community-based healthcare, routine screening and health education, urging government agencies, corporate organisations, development partners and non-governmental organisations to deepen collaboration aimed at bringing quality healthcare closer to vulnerable populations.

The Foundation maintained that while major healthcare challenges remain across Nigeria, community-driven interventions that combine medical services, preventive education and digital innovation can deliver measurable improvements in health outcomes.

The Ifewara outreach, it said, was another step towards ensuring that people who might otherwise delay or completely forgo medical attention can access essential healthcare services while generating reliable health data to guide future interventions.

World.title: TUC Chair, Osifo, Praises DSS For Arrest, Prosecution of Terrorists, Bandits
World.content:
Chairman of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), Comrade Festus Osifo, has commended the leadership of the Department of State Services (DSS) for the arrest and prosecution of terrorists and bandits across the country.

Speaking on Tuesday in Abuja, Osifo said the arrests and prosecutions were sending the right signal to criminal elements terrorising communities nationwide.

“When they are arrested and prosecuted, the bad guys get the clear message,” he noted.

Osifo backed the position of the DSS leadership that terrorists and bandits , whose activities led to the loss of human lives face the death penalty, saying such punishment would serve a deterrent to other criminal elements.

“When that is done, the other bad guys will know it is no longer business as usual,” Osifo noted.

The TUC chairman urged the DSS to sustain the tempo of arrests and prosecutions, noting that citizens have a duty to hold government accountable on all fronts.

“When government does wrong things, we condemn them. When they do positive things, we are also duty bound to commend,” he noted.

Osifo lauded the DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for what he described as ongoing reforms in the Service, and urged him to do more in tackling insecurity across the country.

World.title: The City of Cape Town wants to give you R10 000 to report crime
World.content:
See something, say something. Image: Pexels / Mary Alson

In its crime-fighting efforts, the City of Cape Town (CoCT) distributed notices to residents asking for their help.

The call?

R10 000 for reporting crime that leads to an operational result.



Cape Town Continues its Crime-Fighting Efforts

During an early-morning roadblock on 14 August 2026, the City of Cape Town metro police handed out notices to residents asking for their help.

The notice asks residents to “say something” and “get rewarded.”

In it, the City suggests residents could “earn up to R10 000” if what they report “leads to an arrest, impoundment or confiscation.”

The incidents residents can report include:

Illegal firearms

Dumping and littering

Drug dealing

Stolen property

Metal and cable theft

Vandalism

Gangsterism

To report these crimes, residents can call the city any time, day or night.

They can contact the City on 0800 11 00 77. The line is available 7 days a week, 24 hours a day.



Residents can also use the Citizen Safety App to report crime. The app is available on Android and iOS.

The app is available for what the city describes as “non-life-threatening incidents.”

These include noise complaints, suspicious activity, by-law violations, and illegal dumping.

When filing a report, the app will automatically capture residents’ GPS to hasten response times.

Residents can participate anonymously

According to the notice, you can make a report anonymously, and your identity will be protected.

However, the city highlighted it will only pay a reward when “information leads to an operational result.”

These include arrests, recovering stolen goods, and confiscating contraband or illegal firearms.

Residents also have to be aware that not every tip will net them a big payday even if action is taken.

The notice stresses that it’s possible to “Earn up to R10 000.” However, it doesn’t stipulate the minimum reward a resident could earn from a tip.

Crime in Cape Town

This call to action comes as 21 of the city’s 62 precincts have recorded an increase in crime.

According to data from the South African Police Service (SAPS), the precincts where crime has risen sharply include Makhaza. There’s been an 18.9% increase in crime in the suburb.

Ravensmead follows with a 12.3% increase in crime.

Sea Point on the Atlantic Seaboard and Bishop Lavis on the Cape Flats tie for third place, with crime rising 11.1% in these suburbs year-on-year.

It’s not all bad news. The city’s efforts appear to be making some strides. Fewer crimes were reported in 28 of the 62 precincts.

During these challenging economic times, this initiative may increase reporting and encourage active citizenship.

World.title: St Stithians teen couple: When does memorial, funeral take place?
World.content:
It’s been over 10 days since the deaths of St Stithians teen couple Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee in an alleged murder-suicide, and South Africans are no closer to knowing the truth about what happened. There has also been no official word on funeral or memorial services that will take place

ST STITHIANS TEEN MURDER-SUICIDE LATEST

This week, Mpumalanga Police spokesperson Colonel Mavela Masondo confirmed that they would not divulge any new information to the public relating to the St Stithians teens’ alleged murder-suicide due to an ongoing investigation.

Cameron Waldeck-Cooks – a Grade 11 learner at the Johannesburg private school – and Ethan Coetzee, a 2025 matriculant, were found dead on the morning on Monday, 3 August at the Waterval self-catering lodge in Mumpalanga.



The bubbly blonde had been invited to participate in a multi-day hike, which she hoped would help her towards her goal of the Gold level of The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment.

According to a statement by Etha’s family, the teen couple appeared happy the night before their death. Their bodies were discovered by Ethan’s father, Graham Coetzee.

Police initially investigated the deaths as an inquest and initially suspected that no foul play was involved.

However, post-mortem findings changed the direction of the investigation regarding to the St Stithians teens.

According to preliminary findings as well as the opinion of an independent forensic pathologist involved, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks died from strangulation/suffocation.

Ethan’s death is believed to be a suicide.



Police have subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death.

No person has been charged with Cameron’s murder, and police have not publicly announced that Ethan was legally determined to be her killer. The investigation continues.

CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS, ETHAN COETZEE: WHEN DOES FUNERAL, MEMORIAL TAKE PLACE?

In a statement to the public, the parents of Cameron Waldeck-Cooks shared that a memorial service would take place during the month of August. A date has yet to be made public.

It’s unclear if she, or Ethan Coetzee, has been laid to rest via a funeral service.

St Stithians, the President’s Award for Youth Empowerment and anti-gender-based violence activists, Women For Change, have paid tribute to Cameron.

A group of cyclists who took part in the Trans Baviaans Race dedicated their mountain biking race to Cameron. The teen’s dad, Derrick Cooks, was moved by the gesture, sharing: “What you and the team did for Cam is incredibly special….knowing you carried her with you means everything. Cam would have absolutely loved this”.
