World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has only a majority of nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. World.title: Poland says it foiled Russian plot to “execute” US-Ukrainian citizen in Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and may be updated as further details emerge. Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. World.title: Poland hit by theft of 19 million patients’ data from medical platform
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The personal data of almost 19 million people, including medical information, has been compromised in a major cyberattack on a company that provides services to thousands of medical facilities in Poland. “We are dealing with one of the largest incidents in Poland’s history,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on Wednesday. He urged people to use government services to check whether their data is affected and to “lock” their national identity number to prevent potential fraud. (￼🧵 1/2) 💬 Dziś doszło do poważnego wycieku danych w firmie MyDr, który może obejmować blisko 19 milionów osób korzystających z opieki medycznej. W związku z sytuacją krytyczną zostały natychmiast podjęte działania mające zabezpieczyć dane i wyjaśnić okoliczności incydentu –… pic.twitter.com/nIp6EvbKiu — Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji (@CYFRA_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The attack targeted MyDr, a company that provides services used by many medical facilities in Poland. Its data includes patients’ personal information, as well as medical details such as diagnoses and prescriptions. It was first reported on Monday by Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service, which said that it had been contacted on Saturday by the alleged perpetrators, who claimed to have accessed the data of around 18.8 million people. The hackers, who have not been identified, had also sent a screenshot from the compromised database showing the personal data of “one of the most important politicians in Poland”, added Zaufana Trzecia Strona. Shortly afterwards, MyDr confirmed that it had “become the target of an external, deliberate criminal activity involving some of our data”. In an update on Wednesday, it said that, at the time of writing, there was no evidence that the data had been published anywhere. Największy wyciek danych osobowych w historii Polski i co możemy z nim zrobić – nasza analiza incydentu w MyDr i jego potencjalnych skutków.https://t.co/vXUmVfpPAP Opisujemy aktualny stan wiedzy i możliwe scenariusze rozwoju sytuacji. pic.twitter.com/uqhjz1CjZ1 — ZaufanaTrzeciaStrona @zaufanatrzeciastrona@infosec (@Zaufana3Strona) August 13, 2026 Gawkowski addressed the issue at a press briefing on Wednesday. He noted that “there is no indication we are dealing with an external attack…from Russia or any other country”. Poland has recently regularly been targetted by Russian state-linked hackers. It is “very likely” that cybercriminals are behind the attack on MyDr, said Gawkowski, who pledged that there would be an “uncompromising” response from the Polish security services. The minister advised Poles to check in a secure government database whether their data had been leaked. He also advised citizens to use the state web portal, known as mObywatel, to “lock” their identity number, known as a PESEL, which prevents fraudsters from using it. Around 12,000 medical facilities use MyDr’s services, the digital affairs ministry told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The company claims that it processes three million medical consultations and 2.7 million prescriptions a month, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. World.title: Fugitive Polish opposition politician reportedly in pro-Russian Moldovan breakaway region
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A letter sent to a Polish court by Marcin Romanowski, who served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government and is now on the run from criminal charges, suggests that he is residing in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. The Polish authorities have been trying to locate and extradite Romanowski, whose whereabouts have been unknown since he fled Budapest earlier this year after Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who had granted him asylum, lost power. Były wiceminister sprawiedliwości ma przebywać w Tyraspolu, stolicy zbuntowanej mołdawskiej prowincji znajdującej się pod patronatem Rosji. Spod tego adresu w Naddniestrzu polityk PiS miał wystąpić o wydanie listu żelaznego.https://t.co/m05dtQv3KV — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) August 12, 2026 On Wednesday, following media reports that Romanowski had sent a letter to the Polish authorities from Transnistria, a spokeswoman for Warsaw’s district court, which is responsible for extradition matters, confirmed to news website Gazeta.pl that this was the case. “The letter and envelope indicate that the package was sent to the court from Tiraspol in Transnistria,” said judge Anna Ptaszek. “It bears his handwritten signature.” Przemysław Nowak, the spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, also confirmed to broadcaster RMF that Romanowski had sent the letter, in which he indicated that he was residing in Tiraspol, the capital of Transnistria, and requested safe passage to Poland. The fugitive politician said that he would be willing to appear in court or before prosecutors, on the condition that he was not placed in detention, said Nowak, who added that prosecutors had not yet taken a position on Romanowski’s request. Transnistria is a region of eastern Moldova, bordering Ukraine, that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s, even fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. The territory’s flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Romanowski’s apparent presence in the Russian-linked territory was condemned by figures from Poland’s government. “I would say that Romanowski is now very likely under the influence of Russian intelligence,” said deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. Paweł Wojtunik, the former head of Poland’s Central Anticorruption Bureau (CBA), who previously worked in Moldova, wrote that “it is impossible to enter [Transnistria], let alone to live there, without the consent of the local KGB, which is directly managed by the Russian GRU and FSB [intelligence agences]”. – Dzisiaj powiedziałbym, że Romanowski z dużym prawdopodobieństwem jest pod wpływem rosyjskich służb – ocenił wiceszef MON Cezary Tomczyk. Sprawę skomentował też szef MSZ Radosław Sikorski.https://t.co/LuWw0bkh2j — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 12, 2026 Even a deputy leader of Romanowski’s own party, the national-conservative PiS, was unwilling to defend him. In an interview with Polsat News, Przemysław Czarnek noted that it is still not confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. But he agreed, when asked by the host, that it “would be crossing a line” for Romanowski to be in the territory. Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government between 2019 and 2023. He remains a member of parliament, despite having fled Poland in December 2024 after prosecutors sought to bring charges against him for 11 alleged crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group. Those alleged offences relate to Romanowski’s time at the justice ministry, which was then led by Zbigniew Ziobro, who is also wanted on multiple charges. Both Romanowski and Ziobro obtained asylum in Hungary when the country was led by PiS-ally Orbán. The Polish government says that Hungary has revoked the refugee status and travel documents granted to fugitive ex-justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro by Viktor Orbán. Poland will now seek Ziobro's deportation from the US, where he fled after leaving Hungary https://t.co/TcVw0AiEMX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 However, after Orbán lost power earlier this year, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains. Last month, Poland requested his extradition, though that is a process that could take years. Romanowski, meanwhile, disappeared completely, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians have denied the allegations against them and have claimed to be victims of “political revenge” by the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk that took power in December 2023. They have argued that they would not be able to receive a fair trial in Poland while Tusk remains in power because of the government’s influence over the judicial system. On Wednesday, Romanowski’s lawyer, Bartosz Lewandowski, confirmed that his client had requested safe passage to Poland and that he was “outside the territory of the European Union”. However, he did not confirm that Romanowski is in Transnistria. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. World.title: Around 300 Czech Citizens Evacuated Due to Fire in Croatia
World.content:
Some 300 Czech tourists are among the 1,000 evacuees with a Czech police officer sent to coordinate the emergency response.

Croatian prime minister Andrej Plenković is in the town holding a coordination meeting with all emergency services this morning. Croatian president Zoran Milanović is also expected later today.

“All those injured in last night’s fire are being provided with the necessary medical care,” Plenković said in an earlier update on X.

No fatalities have been reported. The spokesman said there were also no reports of serious injuries among Czech citizens.

Some tourists left the area on their own, while others are staying at evacuation centres in Omiš and Split. A Czech consul is on site and is in contact with local authorities and security forces.

Fire spreads across up to 1,000 hectares

Around 160 firefighters, supported by specialised firefighting aircraft, are battling the blaze.

The fire has caused significant material damage, according to eyewitnesses, with dozens of cars and homes reportedly destroyed. Strong winds have helped the flames spread across an area estimated at between 900 and 1,000 hectares.

Witnesses reported hearing gas cylinders exploding inside burning homes, while the streets were filled with the sirens of fire engines, ambulances and police vehicles. Large parts of Omiš have also been left without electricity.

Mass evacuation underway

Hundreds of people have fled the affected area, with some tourists escaping by boat, catamaran and other small vessels.

The organised evacuation is being coordinated through the Ribnjak sports hall in Omiš. From there, evacuees are being transported by bus to the Gripe sports centre in Split.

According to Omiš fire chief Slavko Tucaković, foreigners make up the majority of those evacuated.

World.title: Czech Villages Face Water Shortages as Drought Deepens
World.content:
Residents say they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pool.

Communities across the Czech Republic are struggling with worsening water shortages as wells dry up and small streams disappear after years of increasingly severe drought, according to local media on Thursday.



In the village of Krsy in the Plzen Region, tankers are delivering drinking water daily to a reservoir above the village. Some private wells have already run dry, while others are close to empty.

Residents said they are cutting water use wherever possible, taking shorter showers, reducing garden watering and abandoning plans to fill swimming pools.

Authorities are urging households to connect to public water networks where available.

The shortages are also putting pressure on tourist destinations. In Horni Becva, in the Beskydy Mountains, the population doubles during the summer holidays.

The municipality’s two wells have been operating close to their limits, with firefighters called in to deliver water.

Hotels with wellness facilities are among the largest users, prompting local officials to ask businesses to reduce consumption.

Officials hope conditions will improve when the tourist season ends and autumn rains arrive.

World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: This Website Tracks How Many Trams Are Still Running Without Air Conditioning
World.content:
A new website is giving Prague residents a live picture of how many trams are operating without air conditioning, highlighting an issue that has become particularly noticeable during the city’s summer heat.

The service, Smrdime.cz, was created by developer Christoph Korb. Its name is a play on the Czech word smrdíme, meaning “we stink,” and refers to the uncomfortable conditions passengers can face inside overheated trams.

The website uses live data to calculate the share of Prague’s trams that are currently running without air conditioning. The figures change throughout the day as new vehicles enter and leave service.

When the service was checked on Thursday, August 13, Prague was experiencing temperatures of around 37 degrees Celsius. At that point, 188 of the 256 trams in operation did not have air conditioning, representing about 71 percent of the fleet being tracked.



Of the 147 air-conditioned trams available, 77 were operating at the same time.

The figures provide a snapshot rather than a fixed daily total. As trams are taken out of service and replaced, the balance between air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned vehicles changes continuously.

The project draws attention to a long-standing issue facing Prague’s public transport system: a substantial part of the city’s tram fleet still lacks air conditioning.

The website is based on data from two publicly available sources. Transport information comes from Golemio, Prague’s open-data platform, while weather information is provided by Open-Meteo. The two data sources are used to calculate the current situation displayed on the site.

Korb built the service with Anthropic’s Claude Code development tool. He has also published the project’s source code on GitHub, allowing other developers to inspect the project and contribute to its development.

World.title: From a Student’s Dream to a Japanese Bakery in Prague: The Story Behind Yaki-Pan
World.content:
For Hoan, opening a bakery in Prague was not a sudden business idea. It was a dream that had been taking shape for more than a decade.

After arriving in Prague as a student, Hoan watched members of the Vietnamese community build businesses across the city, most commonly in restaurants, grocery shops and nail salons.

She worked in grocery stores and restaurants herself, gradually gaining experience in the food industry while studying.

But after finishing school, she still was not sure what kind of business she wanted to open.



One thing was clear: she loved baking.

“Its my dream. It’s been my plan for a long time, more than 10 years,” she says.

Rather than opening another coffee shop, she decided to focus on what she knew best. She had visited bakeries around Prague and noticed what she saw as a gap in the city’s food scene: there were few places specialising in Japanese-style baking.

Around six years ago, she decided that she wanted to fill that gap herself.

The result was Yaki-Pan, a small bakery built around Japanese pastries and flavours. Before opening, Hoan spent roughly a year and a half — and much of that time at home — testing recipes and trying to recreate the textures and flavours she associated with Japanese baking.

Getting there was not straightforward.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Yaki-Pan (@yakipan_brunch)

Learning to work with Czech ingredients

For Hoan, authenticity was essential. She wanted the pastries at Yaki-Pan to resemble Japanese baked goods as closely as possible, but she quickly discovered that one of the most important ingredients presented a major challenge: flour.

Japanese flour differs significantly from the flour commonly available in the Czech Republic. The differences affect the texture, consistency and ultimately the finished pastry.

“The flour here is not the same as when I learnt,” she says.

Instead of simply following recipes she had learned elsewhere, Hoan had to adapt them to local ingredients. She experimented with different combinations of flour and spent months trying to achieve the texture she was looking for.

Three years ago, she travelled to China to study Japanese baking under professionals. There, she was able to work with Japanese ingredients and gain further experience. Returning to Europe meant starting another process of adjustment.

She considered importing Japanese flour to the Czech Republic, but eventually found it difficult to maintain as a long-term solution. Instead, she continued experimenting with locally available ingredients.

“I needed to test for about two years at my home,” she says.

The process has not necessarily ended with the bakery’s opening. Hoan continues to work on her recipes and ingredients, looking for ways to improve the pastries while staying as close as possible to the style she wants to create.

A warm welcome from Prague

If Hoan was worried that Japanese flavours might be unfamiliar to Prague customers, the first day quickly put those concerns to rest.

When Yaki-Pan opened, she had not prepared significantly more food than usual. Within 30 minutes, the bakery had sold out.

The first two months were particularly busy, especially at weekends. Today, the customer base includes tourists, Japanese residents and visitors who have become regulars.

Japanese customers have also played an important role in validating Hoan’s approach, frequently complimenting her on how closely the pastries resemble those they know from Japan.

Among the most popular items is shio-pan, a Japanese-style bread known for its soft texture and salty flavour. At Yaki-Pan, the vegan version has become one of the bakery’s bestsellers and regularly sells out.

Hoan’s own favourite pastry, meanwhile, changes from day to day.

The bakery’s success has also brought an unexpected question. Some customers have asked why a Vietnamese woman decided to open a Japanese bakery.

For Hoan, the answer is simple. “It’s my dream,” she says. “I put all my energy into my recipes.”

Her background, she suggests, is less important than the work she has put into learning the craft and developing the food.

Building Yaki-Pan’s future

For now, Hoan is focused on the bakery she has already built. Yaki-Pan is run by Hoan and her husband, and her previous experience working in restaurants has helped her manage the busy days herself.

The couple are already thinking about the next stage. They hope to add outdoor seating next year and, eventually, open another location.

But there is no immediate rush to expand.

“Now I want to put all my energy into this one,” Hoan says.

There are also plans to introduce another type of matcha, giving customers more choice alongside the bakery’s existing drinks.

For a business that began as an idea Hoan carried with her for more than 10 years, Yaki-Pan remains very much a work in progress. The recipes continue to evolve, customers continue to discover Japanese-style baking, and Hoan is still searching for the ingredients and techniques that bring her original vision closest to reality.

World.title: Prague Taxi Driver Arrested After Taking CZK 3.5 Million Left in His Car
World.content:
A 21-year-old taxi driver in Prague has been arrested after allegedly taking a suitcase containing CZK 3.5 million in cash that passengers accidentally left in his car.

The money was recovered by police after the driver eventually admitted what he had done and told investigators where he had hidden it. He now faces up to five years in prison.

The incident happened in late July, although police only released details of the case several days later.



The passengers were a married couple who had taken a taxi to Václav Havel Airport in the early morning. They were heading on vacation and only realized after reaching the airport that one of their suitcases was still in the vehicle.

The couple immediately contacted the driver and asked him to bring the suitcase back. According to police, he initially agreed, but the luggage never appeared despite further calls and reminders.

The couple eventually reported the matter to police. Given the amount of money involved, forensic specialists from the Prague 1 police precinct joined the investigation.

Investigators quickly located the taxi and detained the driver. A search of the vehicle, however, produced no suitcase.

The 21-year-old initially denied that the passengers had left anything behind, telling police that he had not found any luggage in the car.

His account later changed.

After being placed in a cell, the man confessed and revealed where he had hidden the cash. Police officers and forensic specialists then located the money in a forest near Kladno.

The investigation also uncovered an attempt to destroy evidence. Near the cash, investigators found the burned remains of the suitcase. Police say the driver had taken the items to the forest, piled them together and set them on fire.

The driver remains under investigation and could face a prison sentence of up to five years if convicted.

World.title: Six Prague Rooftops and Terraces to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are six rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

6. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Brazilian Summer Vibes Coming to Střelecký ostrov This Weekend
World.content:
Prague’s Střelecký ostrov will turn into a Brazilian-inspired summer spot this Friday and Saturday, with live music, DJs, food, drinks and a riverside atmosphere.

The two-day event will take place from 12 p.m. to 10 p.m. on both days, bringing Brazilian music and summer energy to one of the city’s most picturesque islands.

Visitors can expect live Brazilian music and DJ sets, alongside a selection of food and drinks. The menu will include wine, cheese, Czech dishes, cocktails, frozen margaritas and frozen daiquiris.

The event offers a relaxed way to spend the weekend in central Prague, with music, drinks and food overlooking the Vltava.

World.title: Budapest braces for major traffic restrictions starting Saturday ahead of 20 August celebrations
World.content:
Budapest motorists and pedestrians should prepare for major traffic restrictions from this Saturday as the city gears up for Hungary’s 20 August national holiday celebrations. According to the Budapest Police Headquarters (BRFK), road closures and other restrictions will remain in place until 25 August.

Several key roads, bridges and public spaces will be affected, with the Chain Bridge and Margaret Bridge among the locations facing closures.

Traffic restrictions begin this Saturday

According to a statement published on police.hu, partial closures will begin on Saturday, affecting, among other areas, Műegyetem Quay and several sections of both the Buda and Pest lower quays. In the Buda Castle District, parts of Szentháromság Street and Tárnok Street will also be closed to traffic.

Chain Bridge to close from Sunday morning

The Chain Bridge will be closed to motor traffic from 6 AM on Sunday. From 7 AM, both the northern and southern pavements will also be closed to pedestrians. These restrictions will remain in place until noon on 21 August.

The Margaret Bridge will also be affected on Sunday. From 9 PM, one lane on the northern side of the bridge will be closed. From 10 PM, both pavements will be closed to pedestrians. These restrictions are likewise expected to remain until noon on 21 August.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

More closures coming next week

From next Tuesday, motorists can expect restrictions on sections of Zoltán Street, Nádor Street and Akadémia Street, as well as on Műegyetem Quay.

On Wednesday, Várkert Quay will be closed along its entire length. In the evening, restrictions will also be introduced on Kós Károly Promenade, between Heroes’ Square and Állatkerti Boulevard, and on Széchenyi Quay, between Kossuth Square and Széchenyi Square. Salkaházi Sára Quay will also be affected.

Full Margaret Bridge closure on 20 August

On 20 August, Hungary’s national holiday, further restrictions will come into force across the capital. Among other locations, Szent István Square will be closed, while the entire Margaret Bridge will also be inaccessible. Later that evening, motorists will face another major restriction: the Elisabeth Bridge will be closed to motor traffic between 7 PM and 11 PM.

With preparations for Budapest’s 20 August celebrations already beginning, residents and visitors are advised to plan their journeys carefully and allow extra time for travel across the capital.

World.title: Man attacks two Hungarian police officers and service dog, officers use tear gas to stop him – video
World.content:
A man in his twenties has been arrested in Hungary after allegedly attacking two police officers and a service dog during an incident at his home in Komárom-Esztergom County.

The man was reportedly behaving aggressively and damaging property inside his home when police were called to the scene. He was subsequently detained on suspicion of violence against a public official and attempted grievous bodily harm. A court ordered his detention on Friday following a motion by the Győr Regional Investigative Prosecutor’s Office, the Hungarian News Agency reported.

Man attacked officers and police dog

Four police officers arrived at the man’s home and told him that he would be taken to hospital by ambulance for a medical examination. However, the man allegedly refused to cooperate and instead became aggressive towards the officers and the service dog deployed at the scene.

Despite being ordered to stop, he allegedly punched two officers several times, kicked one of them twice and also attacked the service dog. Police eventually managed to restrain him by using tear gas before handcuffing him. He reportedly continued to resist even after being detained.

Two officers injured

The confrontation left two police officers injured. One suffered a head injury and bruising to the hip, while the other sustained a skull contusion. A specialised unit from the Győr-Moson-Sopron County Police Headquarters and Hungary’s National Protective Service also assisted with the arrest at the request of the investigative prosecutor’s office.

The suspect was taken into custody and questioned as a suspect but did not make a statement. He did not file a complaint against the charges brought against him.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Suspect previously convicted of drug offences

The case is being treated particularly seriously because the man had previously been convicted several times of drug-related offences. According to prosecutors, he allegedly attacked the police while still serving the probationary period of a suspended prison sentence.

The offences he is suspected of committing – taking the applicable cumulative sentencing rules into account – carry a potential prison sentence of between one and seven and a half years. The investigative prosecutor therefore requested his detention, arguing that the circumstances justified the measure. The court granted the request on Friday.

The investigation into violence against a public official and attempted grievous bodily harm is ongoing.

World.title: Croatia wildfire: Foreign ministry shares important update on Hungarian tourists
World.content:
All Hungarian citizens affected by the wildfire near Omiš in southern Croatia are safe, according to Hungary’s Foreign Minister Anita Orbán.

The situation in the Omiš area has stabilised, although smoke and a strong smell of burning are still lingering in the air. Two Canadair firefighting aircraft remain in operation to prevent the flames from reigniting. Hungarian consular officials are continuing to assist citizens affected by the evacuation.

Dozens of Hungarians evacuated

The Hungarian consul from Split personally spoke to 26 Hungarian citizens at the reception centre in Omiš. None requested further assistance or help returning to Hungary, with those still at the centre waiting for authorities to allow them to return to their accommodation and collect their belongings.

Another 25 Hungarian citizens who had previously been accommodated at the reception centre have already left the area. Seven Hungarians were also staying at a reception centre in Split on Friday morning. Officials had managed to contact two of them, and they were likewise waiting for the opportunity to return to their accommodation.

Authorities have since reopened roads that had previously been closed because of the fire, and those affected have been informed. However, electricity supplies remain intermittent in parts of the area. According to Anita Orbán, several Hungarians have already returned to their accommodation, while others have started their journey back to Hungary.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Four Hungarians suffered minor injuries

Four Hungarian citizens sustained minor injuries in the wildfire, but none suffered burns. All four were expected to be discharged from hospital on Friday. In one case, a Hungarian grandmother needed medication, which was provided by the Croatian authorities.

The Hungarian consul in Split remains at the scene, while a replacement consul is also travelling from Zagreb to help with the ongoing response.

Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković also visited the affected area and asked the Hungarian consul about the condition of Hungarian citizens. Meanwhile, Anita Orbán spoke with her Croatian counterpart about the situation.

The Hungarian foreign minister thanked staff from the Foreign Ministry for their work and expressed hope that everyone affected would be able to return home safely.

Thousands affected as deadly wildfire tears through Omiš area

The severe wildfire broke out near Omiš on Thursday evening before spreading to residential areas overnight. Around 1,000 local residents and tourists were evacuated from the affected area. A total of 36 people have been injured, seven of them reportedly in life-threatening condition. Croatian police also discovered one body on Friday afternoon while searching the burned area.

Although the situation has stabilised, firefighting operations are continuing, with aircraft working to prevent renewed outbreaks. Authorities are also gradually reopening roads in the affected region. For Hungarian travellers currently in or planning to visit the Omiš area, the Hungarian authorities continue to monitor developments closely.

World.title: Hungary unveils huge EUR 3 billion housing plan as new government takes aim at controversial mega-projects
World.content:
The Wekerle Sándor programme could deliver affordable rental homes and student accommodation, while the government also moves to revisit the M6 motorway deal and several controversial investments

Hungary could launch a multi-billion-euro rental housing programme by the end of the year, with the Wekerle Sándor Housing Construction Programme potentially reaching a value of up to EUR 3 billion, partly financed through EU funds, Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said at Friday’s government briefing.

The government has not yet approved the programme’s detailed framework. For now, it is drawing up a list of tasks and the legislative changes needed to implement the scheme.

Vitézy said the Hungarian property market had slowed significantly and argued that the government needed to stimulate new housing construction. The planned programme would focus on affordable rental homes and additional student accommodation, with developments primarily targeted at brownfield and underused urban areas with good public transport connections.

Dávid Vitézy and Vanda Szondi at Friday’s government briefing. Photo: Facebook/Vitézy Dávid

Former Fudan University site could become housing development

One of the locations being considered is the Budapest site originally earmarked for the planned Fudan University campus. According to Vitézy, the government wants to prioritise brownfield sites and underused urban areas in Budapest and other major Hungarian cities. Choosing locations with existing public transport connections would make it possible to develop new housing without creating entirely new transport infrastructure.

The minister said the detailed development of the Wekerle Sándor programme could get under way by the end of December, with the overall programme potentially worth as much as EUR 3 billion.

Vitézy also criticised the housing policy of previous governments, arguing that the emphasis had been placed on helping people purchase their own homes rather than developing a sizeable rental housing sector. He said this had contributed to difficulties with social mobility, as people could become tied to the location where they own property.

Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy speaking at 14 August’s government briefing. Photo: MTI

Government to retender controversial M6 motorway project

The government is also planning to retender a major project connected to the M6 motorway, after Vitézy raised questions about the price and legality of a previous decision. The minister said that a section of the M6 between Dunaújváros and Érd had been awarded to MKIF, a motorway concession company linked to businessmen Lőrinc Mészáros and László Szíjj.

According to Vitézy, competing bidders were prepared to carry out the work for approximately HUF 50 billion, while MKIF quoted HUF 149 billion for the same work and services. The minister described this as a threefold overpricing and said the government would now put the project out to tender again, with the cheapest bid to be selected.

Vitézy also claimed that the original order had been unlawful because, in his view, the decision should have been made by then-Economic Minister Márton Nagy rather than by former Construction and Transport Minister János Lázár.

The ministry will file a criminal complaint in connection with the M6 case, Vitézy said. He also argued that the entire motorway concession system should be reviewed. The minister further criticised additional costs paid to the concession company, which he said had been requested on the grounds of the war in Ukraine.

Vanda Szondi government spokesperson. Photo: MTI

Tougher environmental rules for battery factories

The government is also preparing changes affecting battery factories operating under special investment status. According to Vitézy, the government will review which battery plants have been granted priority status and will amend the relevant decrees.

If a factory violates environmental or nature conservation regulations, its special status could be suspended for at least six months. If the violation is not remedied, the suspension could remain in place for longer. Vitézy stressed that the aim was not to prevent battery factories from operating, but to ensure that companies comply with Hungary’s environmental regulations.

Several controversial projects lose priority status

The government has also decided to withdraw national economic priority status from a number of projects that have attracted controversy in recent years. The projects include:

a brownfield development on the site of the former brickworks in Törökbálint;

redevelopment of the former Lang factory site in Budapest’s 13th district;

the Club Aliga development in Balatonvilágos;

the planned Tihany Castle Hotel and Training Centre;

the Fiatalokért Központ project in Sukoró;

the National Tennis Competition Centre on Margaret Island;

a logistics and general economic property development in Soroksár and Gyál;

the Pázmány Campus development; and

the planned National Circus Arts Centre near Nyugati railway station.

The withdrawal of priority status means these projects will no longer benefit from the special framework previously granted to them.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

New national transport bodies established

Another major change concerns Hungary’s public transport system. The National Transport Organiser and the Train Fleet company were established at the beginning of August following legislation adopted by the Tisza-majority parliament.

The National Transport Organiser is intended to perform functions similar to those of Budapest’s BKK, but on a national level. The Train Fleet company, meanwhile, could play a key role in planned rolling-stock purchases.

In particular, the new structure is expected to facilitate the planned procurement of new HÉV suburban trains and InterCity trains, for which the government intends to make use of around EUR 1.8 billion in EU funding.

The announcements form part of a broader overhaul of Hungary’s investment, housing and transport policies under the new government, with several large-scale projects inherited from the previous administration now being reviewed or reconsidered.

World.title: PM Magyar: Hungary begins sinking two huge barges to raise Danube water levels near Paks
World.content:
Hungary is set to begin the controlled sinking of two 80-metre-long barges near Paks on Friday afternoon in an extraordinary effort to raise water levels in the Danube and help safeguard the operation of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced the latest stage of the emergency construction project in a video filmed at the site of the Danube’s temporary bottom sill.

According to the prime minister, all of the anchoring piles, drilled eight metres into the riverbed, have now been installed. The two barges will be secured to them using steel cables approximately four centimetres thick before being deliberately sunk.

80-metre barges to be lowered into the Danube

The controlled sinking of the two vessels was expected to begin at around 3 PM on Friday, according to Magyar. The operation forms part of a major project designed to increase the Danube’s water level near Paks amid prolonged drought and exceptionally low river levels.

Work is continuing around the clock, involving the Hungarian Defence Forces, industrial divers, water management specialists, contractors and staff from the National Defence Authority. The scale and complexity of the construction work has been described by Magyar as unprecedented in Hungary in recent decades.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Government invites opposition leaders to Paks

Magyar has invited the leaders of Hungary’s parliamentary parties to Paks at 10 AM on Saturday. The prime minister said he wanted to show them the construction site and explain why the government had been forced to undertake such a complex and large-scale project.

He also intends to discuss what he described as failures over the past decade that contributed to the current situation.

However, the leaders of Fidesz and Mi Hazánk declined the invitation, citing holidays and other reasons.

If you missed it: Government press conference: Paks nuclear power plant faces shutdown risk

Magyar attacks Orbán over absence

The prime minister sharply criticised former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán for declining to attend. Magyar accused Orbán of remaining silent despite the prolonged drought, low Danube water levels and Hungary’s energy situation.

He argued that the current circumstances required national cooperation regardless of political differences, and said Orbán should have visited Paks to see the work being carried out and hear about the government’s efforts to stabilise the country’s energy supply.

Magyar also suggested that Orbán could have brought contributions from business figures to help with the project. The prime minister concluded by thanking everyone involved in the emergency construction effort, saying that around 145,000 cubic metres of rock will ultimately be used for the temporary and permanent structures.

World.title: Orbán fails to block return of billions in state assets as Hungary’s top court rejects Fidesz
World.content:
Hungary’s Constitutional Court has rejected a petition submitted by Fidesz challenging the constitutional amendment concerning public interest asset management foundations, known as KEKVAs.

The court dismissed the petition without examining its substance, ruling that it did not have the jurisdiction to review the challenged constitutional provision. The decision concerns the 16th amendment to Hungary’s Fundamental Law, adopted under the new Tisza government,

which abolished the public interest asset management foundations into which the previous Orbán government had transferred thousands of billions of forints in state assets.

Constitutional Court says it lacks jurisdiction

According to the Constitutional Court’s decision, the full bench rejected the Fidesz petition because the court lacks the necessary jurisdiction to carry out a substantive review of constitutional amendments. The issue stems from the Fourth Amendment to Hungary’s Fundamental Law in 2013, when

the Fidesz-led parliamentary majority removed the Constitutional Court’s power to conduct substantive constitutional reviews of amendments to the Fundamental Law.

Since then, the court has generally been limited to examining whether constitutional amendments were adopted in accordance with the required procedural rules, rather than assessing their substantive constitutional content.

Fidesz had argued in its petition that the disputed provision did not establish a general constitutional institution for the future. Instead, the party claimed that it introduced transitional rules specifically concerning identifiable foundations that were already operating when the amendment entered into force.

The Constitutional Court nevertheless concluded that it could not examine the substance of the challenge.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Two constitutional judges dissent

The decision was not unanimous. Outgoing Constitutional Court President Péter Polt and Constitutional Court Judge Tünde Handó issued separate opinions, arguing that the petition should have been examined on its merits.

Their dissent sets them apart from the majority of the court, which considered itself unable to rule substantively on the constitutional amendment.

The decision is particularly significant given the political and financial importance of the KEKVAs. Under the previous government, substantial amounts of public assets were transferred to such foundations, including assets connected to Hungarian universities and other public interest institutions.

Separate decision on Sulyok still pending

The Constitutional Court has also been asked to consider another politically significant constitutional amendment. According to 24.hu, the court has not yet ruled on the challenge seeking to annul the constitutional amendment that ended President Tamás Sulyok’s mandate. A decision on that case has been postponed.

World.title: Croatia wildfire forces at least 58 Hungarians to evacuate: foreign minister monitors the situation – UPDATE: 4 injured
World.content:
At least 58 Hungarian citizens have been evacuated from areas affected by the devastating wildfire on Croatia’s Dalmatian coast, Hungary’s Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said on Friday.

Around 45 of those evacuated were accommodated in a sports hall, while another 13 were taken to a separate location. Croatian authorities and the Red Cross are providing them with assistance. The wildfire broke out near Omiš on Thursday evening and spread rapidly through dry vegetation and pine forest before reaching residential areas.

One Hungarian tourist injured

According to the Foreign Ministry, one Hungarian citizen was taken to a hospital in Split with a minor limb injury. No other Hungarian injuries are currently known. The Hungarian consular service remains in contact with the hospital and is monitoring the situation in case additional Hungarian citizens require medical assistance.

Hungarian consular officials spent the entire night responding to calls from citizens in the affected area and contacting people registered for consular protection. The exact number of Hungarians seeking consular assistance is not yet known, as officials are still contacting affected citizens individually to establish what help they require.

The ministry’s 24-hour consular emergency number is +36 80 36 80 36.

Seven Hungarians escaped on foot

The requests for assistance have mainly concerned evacuation, accommodation, safe onward travel and personal belongings or vehicles left behind.

Two Hungarian families, consisting of seven people in total, reportedly had to escape the affected area on foot. Their vehicles may have been destroyed by the fire, according to the Foreign Ministry.

Two Hungarian police officers currently serving in Zadar are also assisting with the consular response. Following consultations with Hungary’s Interior Ministry, they have been asked to remain in the area and continue supporting the operation. Their accommodation is being provided by Hungary’s embassy in Zagreb.

More information on the wildfire: Hungarian tourists flee as huge wildfire engulfs Croatian coast near Omiš

Minibuses sent from Hungary

Two minibuses have been sent from Hungary to collect the 13 Hungarian citizens evacuated to the second location. The Hungarian embassy in Zagreb and the Consular Service are currently contacting all known Hungarian citizens affected by the fire, assessing their individual needs and coordinating with Croatian authorities.

Where necessary, Hungarian officials will also help organise onward travel, accommodation and other consular assistance.

Fire contained, but firefighting continues

According to Anita Orbán, Croatian authorities have managed to prevent the fire from spreading further, although firefighting operations are continuing with the assistance of specialised aircraft. No further evacuations are currently known to have taken place.

The wildfire near Omiš forced around 1,000 residents and tourists to flee the affected area. At least 36 people were injured, seven of them in life-threatening condition.

The fire spread to residential areas overnight amid strong winds, causing significant disruption along the popular Dalmatian coast. Hungarians still in the affected region are advised to follow instructions from Croatian authorities and contact the Hungarian Consular Service if they require assistance.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

UPDATE: 4 injured

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs received reports that four Hungarian citizens were injured in connection with the forest fire in Croatia, according to a post on Facebook. Two Hungarians are currently in the hospital and are expected to be discharged today. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs took immediate action to provide assistance to the injured Hungarians.

World.title: Hungary’s new president Baka already more popular than predecessor Sulyok ever was, poll finds
World.content:
Hungary’s newly elected President András Baka has already achieved a level of public support that his predecessor, Tamás Sulyok, never managed to reach, according to a new poll commissioned by Telex.

The survey, commissioned by Telex and conducted by the 21 Research Centre on 11 and 12 August – the day Baka was elected and the following day – examined how well Hungarians knew the new president and whether they considered him suitable for the position.

The findings suggest that although Baka was largely unknown to the public before his nomination, he quickly won substantial support, particularly among voters of the governing Tisza Party.

Most Hungarians have heard of Baka

Some 84% of respondents had heard about Baka’s nomination as president. However, only 57% felt sufficiently familiar with him to say whether they considered him suitable for the role. Among those who expressed an opinion, 72% said Baka was suitable for the presidency, while 28% disagreed.

Across the entire sample, 41% considered him suitable for the post, compared with 16% who said he was unsuitable. The remaining respondents either did not know enough about him or declined to answer.

Baka’s initial level of recognition is difficult to compare directly with previous presidents because of the unusual circumstances surrounding his nomination. His name only became widely known after Prime Minister Péter Magyar posted a photograph of himself with Baka and Tisza politician Ruff Bálint on 5 August.

Before that, relatively few voters were likely to have remembered Baka as the former head of Hungary’s Supreme Court, a position from which he was removed in 2011.

András Baka. Photo: MTI

Baka starts with stronger ratings than Sulyok

Despite his relatively low public profile, Baka appears to be starting his presidency from a considerably stronger position than Sulyok ever enjoyed.

The 21 Research Centre’s earlier research found that Sulyok’s popularity remained relatively low throughout his presidency. By contrast, Baka has already attracted a significantly higher level of support just days after becoming president.

That does not necessarily put him among Hungary’s most popular political figures, however. Former presidents János Áder and Katalin Novák both reached much higher levels of popularity at their peaks. Still, Baka has already surpassed Sulyok’s highest recorded level of popularity, according to the polling data.

Tisza voters overwhelmingly back the new president

Baka’s support is strongly connected to current party preferences. Among Tisza voters, 69% consider him suitable for the presidency, while just 1% believe he is unsuitable. By comparison, only 8% of Fidesz voters consider Baka suitable, while 47% consider him unsuitable.

Among voters of other parties and those without a party preference, 20% consider him suitable and 17% unsuitable. A much larger 63% in this group either do not know enough about him or did not express an opinion.

The figures suggest that Baka has managed to attract some sympathy outside the Tisza camp, despite being nominated by the party at a particularly politically polarised moment.

At the same time, the researchers caution that Tisza voters were much more likely to have heard about Baka’s nomination and therefore much more likely to form an opinion about him. A large proportion of those who remain uninformed are Fidesz, Mi Hazánk or unaffiliated voters, meaning winning over these groups could prove considerably more difficult.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Is Baka independent or close to Tisza?

The poll also asked respondents how they viewed Baka politically. Some 37% considered him independent, while 15% believed he was close to Tisza. Another 47% could not decide, while just 1% considered him a Fidesz politician.

There is a clear link between perceptions of Baka’s independence and his perceived suitability for the presidency. Among those who consider Baka suitable, 88% see him as independent, while only 7% regard him as a Tisza-aligned figure.

Among those who consider him unsuitable, the picture is almost reversed: 76% believe he is close to Tisza, while just 9% consider him independent.

Have you read this? New President Baka could stand up firmly to PM Magyar – so why is the opposition attacking him so viciously?

Baka also tops the list of preferred presidential candidates

Respondents were also asked to name, without being given a list, the person they considered most suitable for the presidency. The question produced highly fragmented results, with 62% unable to name anyone. Among those who did provide a name, however, Baka came out on top, with 14% mentioning him. Sulyok was named by just 5%.

Other names receiving one or two percent of mentions included chess grandmaster Judit Polgár, Péter Márki-Zay, Ákos Hadházy, Viktor Orbán, Mi Hazánk’s presidential nominee Máté Tóth, Katalin Novák, historian Ignác Romsics, former justice minister Péter Bárándy, Ágnes Forsthoffer and András Schiffer.

Fidesz voters were more likely to mention Sulyok, Orbán, Schiffer and former justice minister Judit Varga, although they were generally less likely to name anyone than Tisza voters.

The fact that Sulyok received just 5% of spontaneous mentions is also notable. According to the analysis, this suggests that even among Fidesz voters, relatively few appear to have a strong personal attachment to the outgoing president. Much of their opposition to his removal may therefore be connected to the procedure itself rather than support for Sulyok personally.

World.title: Romanian swimmer David Popovici claims third European 200m freestyle title after 100m triumph
World.content:
Romanian swimming star David Popovici has won the 200m freestyle race at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, his third consecutive European title in the event.

The win on August 14, following the August 12 gold in the 100m freestyle race, makes him the only athlete to have won both races at three consecutive editions of the European championships.

The 21-year-old Romanian swimmer finished the race with a time of 1:44.15, 0.40 seconds ahead of runner-up Tomas Navikonis of Lithuania, and 0.72 seconds ahead of Britain's James Guy.

In the 200m freestyle event, Popovici also won the Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, as well as two world titles, in Budapest in 2022 and in Singapore in 2025.

His personal best in the 200m freestyle came at the 2022 European Championships, when he clocked 1:42.97, the third-fastest time in history.

World.title: Romanian executive to submit fifth payment request under Recovery and Resilience Facility
World.content:
The Romanian government is set to submit the fifth payment request under the EU-backed Recovery and Resilience Facility, or PNRR, according to an announcement from European Investments and Projects minister Dragoș Pîslaru.

Payment no. 5 is worth EUR 2.84 billion, and is the penultimate request that Romania will submit within the PNRR. Once approved, the fifth payment will bring Romania’s absorption rate of PNRR-related grants to 78%, from 66% currently.

“One final request remains, request no. 6, worth EUR 2.58 billion in grants and EUR 1.76 billion in loans. From a total of EUR 13.57 billion allocated at the time the PNRR was signed, we will reach EUR 10.56 billion after request no. 5,” Pîslaru said during a press conference.

Initially, the European Commission planned for a single final payment request, reuniting the now separated requests no. 5 and 6, the minister noted.

The final payment request will be submitted at the end of September, and with it “we could reach 97.2% of the PNRR,” he said, referring to the grants component.

“47% was the percentage of the PNRR when I came to the ministry, after four years since the program was launched. The annual average was about 10.4% of the PNRR. In one year and two months, under the Bolojan government, we added 31% of the PNRR,” the minister also said.

Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan is financed through EUR 21.41 billion under the EU mechanism, including EUR 13.57 billion in grants and EUR 7.84 billion in loans. The fourth payment request, worth EUR 2.62 billion, was approved by the European Commission in May of this year.
