World.title: Land gains ground with independent MPs in bid for presidential nomination
World.content:
TalTech rector Tiit Land says a meeting with the Riigikogu's independent MPs may have boosted his chances of securing a nomination in Estonia's presidential race.

Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) rector Tiit Land met with the MPs on Friday, as interest in nominating him for president of Estonia has continued to grow.

According to the rector, former Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) MP Leo Kunnas had indicated following the meeting that Land had his support.

MP Kalev Stoicescu, who recently quit the coalition Eesti 200, said Land could secure the 21 signatures needed to formally nominate him. He described Land and Justice Chancellor Ülle Madise as equally strong candidates.

"I welcome the fact that we can choose between not one but two candidates," he said. "I'm entitled to my own opinion, just like anyone else."

Stoicescu said MPs asked Land about topics ranging from his potential presidential New Year's Eve address and Estonia's Nordic alignment to how he would respond if war reached the country.

After asking how to better encourage more young people to study in STEM fields, Stoicescu praised Land's idea of encouraging more young men into STEM, given that the future is closely tied to those fields.

Education policy, the MP noted, ultimately has implications for family policy as well.

Undecided for now

Stoicescu said he plans to ask Madise similar questions at their meeting on Monday. He said Land could thrive as president, but for now just needs time to get used to the media attention.

"I wish both candidates good luck," he added.

TalTech rector Tiit Land met with independent MPs Friday about his potential presidential election run. August 14, 2026. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Tõnis Mölder, another unaffiliated MP, called Friday's meeting meaningful. He said Land laid out his vision for tackling social problems facing the country, and they also discussed the records of Estonia's previous heads of state.

He believes Land would need sound expert counsel on security and justice policy.

MPs also asked pointed questions about Land's past.

"The personal and difficult questions were answered as well," Mölder said, adding that he likewise plans to meet with Madise before deciding which potential candidate to support.

'I'm confident in myself'

Land said the smaller group Friday made the meeting more productive than talks with the Riigikogu's parliamentary groups. "When there are fewer people, it's easier to connect," he acknowledged.

He said independent MP Enn Eesmaa asked about the "skeletons in his closet," which Land considered a natural question for someone seeking the presidency.

The TalTech rector said domestic and foreign policy are equally important, but he believes Estonians also expect a president who is visibly present.

"Personally, I feel confident in myself," Land said.

The Riigikogu will convene to elect the next president of Estonia on September 2, with candidates to be formally nominated August 21–24.

World.title: Estonian pork industry squeezed as cheap imports fill production gap
World.content:
A year after a major African swine fever (ASF) outbreak, Estonia's pork industry is struggling again as cheap European imports push local prices below production costs.

Although pig farms have disinfected facilities and rebuilt production since last year's outbreak, many producers are operating at a loss, forcing some smaller farms to close.

"If we stop production and ever want to restart, this isn't a case where you can say today you will, tomorrow you won't," said Saime Agro Group CEO Valmar Haava. "Restarting [pork production] isn't cheap, and it's a very, very lengthy process."

Farmers are having little trouble selling their pork, he added, but are doing so below cost.

Some of the effects of last year's ASF outbreak are only just hitting the meat processing industry, as farms emptied during the outbreak left months-long gaps in pork supplies.

"The farms that were hit were ones whose pigs would normally have reached the market just at the beginning or during the first half of this year, which is why recovery has taken quite a while," said Nõo Meat Factory CEO Ragnar Loova.

Lower pig numbers are also hurting businesses that supply the industry, including feed producers, said Atria Farms board member Meelis Laande.

"Volumes have fallen quite low, and that in turn has meant feed producers no longer have enough work either," Laande explained, adding that those resulting rising costs ultimately show up in pork prices as well.

Price wins over preference

Domestic pork now covers about 60 percent of Estonia's consumption, down from roughly 70–80 percent last year, Laande said. That leaves the market increasingly dependent on imports.

The Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture is seeking ways to ease producers' losses, while the government has already approved €14 million to help rebuild and expand domestic pork production, including sow farms.

"It's also important to continue discussions with the European Commission, because this isn't just Estonia's problem," said ministry deputy secretary general Madis Pärtel.

Despite consumers' preference for domestic pork, cheaper imported meat often wins at the grocery store.

World.title: Levadia football training hall set for Lasnamäe after several years' delays
World.content:
Meistriliiga side FCI Levadia says a long-awaited training hall should be completed next year, in the Lasnamäe district of Tallinn.

The club has sought to build a football training facility for around five years now, and the revised project replaces an earlier plan to erect one in the Maarjamäe district.

"Construction is expected to begin in spring 2027, and the football hall could be completed by the end of 2027," club CEO Jevgeni Gurtšioglujants said.

A 2025 price-tag estimate of €4 million to build the hall remains reportedly unchanged, despite rising construction prices.

The deadline for completing the hall's design is tomorrow, Saturday.

The original planned location was close to the Memorial to the Victims of Communism, where the club's training base is still located. This met with public pushback as it was felt that noise from training sessions and activities would not be location-appropriate.

Artist's rendition of the original planned facility in Maarjamäe. The training hall will now be located at Punane 69b in Lasnamäe. Source: FCI Levadia

€800,000 in state compensation was approved and resulted in the club agreeing to build it at an address on Punane tänav in Lasnamäe instead.

Most of the €4 million to build the facility will come from the City of Tallinn. The Estonian Football Association (EJL) is also due to repay the city €750,000 owed from several years ago as a result of the project.

The club caters to just over 400 registered youth athletes, Gurtšioglujants added.

In 2020, the Estonian Football Association assumed FC Flora's previous obligations to the city, totaling nearly €1.6 million. Of this, the association invested €650,000 in the development of Hiiu Stadium, at least €750,000 will be allocated to the Levadia football hall at Punane 69b, and a separate agreement on the remaining obligation of €196,765 will be reached by the end of this year at the latest.

Levadia and its fan base is broadly identified with the Russian-speaking community.

World.title: Nordic–Baltic hydrogen corridor project still in early stages
World.content:
At the beginning of this year, the government launched a special national planning process to identify a suitable route in Estonia for hydrogen pipelines as part of a six‑country project. A consultant is still being sought; once selected, the planning and location assessment can begin.

According to Monika Korolkov, project manager for the national special plan at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the project is extensive but important, and planning requires thorough studies, analyses and close cooperation with various stakeholders. She added that the project involves 24 municipalities, all of whom must be consulted during the planning process.

"We hope that if the procedure proceeds as planned, we can continue preparing the project according to the intended schedule," Korolkov said. The aim is to outline potential routes by next year so the ministry can present them to landowners.

There is also an idea on the table to build the corridor along the bottom of the Baltic Sea, creating a direct connection between Finland and Germany. Korolkov said work is being done to ensure the route also passes through Estonia.

The Nordic–Baltic hydrogen corridor is a project spanning six countries. Source: Nordic‑Baltic hydrogen corridor / Gemini AI

"If the route comes over land, Estonia can serve as a link between the Nordic and Central European energy networks," Korolkov said. She added that this would strengthen energy security, bring new investments to Estonia and create conditions for developing a hydrogen economy. "If Finland decides it is more beneficial to build the route along the seabed, we will miss out on a great deal," she noted.

Siim Iimre, head of research and development at Elering, said the preferred approach is to use existing gas and electricity infrastructure to minimize the amount of new land needed.

"It is certainly a challenge that Estonia has dispersed settlement and many scenic areas and nature reserves," Iimre said. Because of this, it is difficult to find a corridor that would have minimal environmental impact or cause minimal disturbance.

Both Korolkov and Iimre stressed that building a hydrogen pipeline does not pose a danger to people or the environment. Iimre added that the main impact of an underground pipeline occurs only during construction. "As with building a natural‑gas pipeline, construction machinery will move around and excavation work will take place," he explained.

According to Elering, the project's progress depends both on the successful completion of Estonia's special planning process and on other countries staying on schedule.

Iimre said an investment decision could be made in early 2030, at which point it will be decided whether the infrastructure will be built. If approved, it could be completed by 2035.

He added that the project is necessary because around 80 companies have already expressed interest in producing or using hydrogen.

This week, the tender period for cooperation on the hydrogen corridor's national special plan concluded. The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications will now review the bids, and a contract with the successful bidder will be signed no later than October.

World.title: Police: more than 50 irregular migrants detained in Estonia claim to be minors
World.content:
Since 21 July, police in Estonia have detained 109 foreign nationals, more than 50 of whom claim to be unaccompanied minors, says Indrek Aru, head of the border guard bureau of the Northern Prefecture.

Aru said that Estonia's detention centers currently hold 119 foreign nationals. Since 21 July, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) has detained 109 people in Tallinn who crossed the Belarus–Latvia border illegally during the migration pressure. No irregular migrants have been detected elsewhere in Estonia at the moment.

The detention center in Rae municipality currently holds 30 possible unaccompanied minor irregular migrants.

Nineteen irregular migrants have been handed over to Latvia under the agreement between Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Aru said all of these transfers took place within the past week.

Aru noted that since 21 July, police have detained 109 foreign nationals in Estonia, more than 50 of whom claim to be unaccompanied minors. He added that they only claim this, because several individuals have changed their statements.

If one day a person says they are 30 years old, the next day they may say they are 16. Aru said that fewer than ten individuals appear genuinely likely to be underage. He added that a person with a long beard and wrinkles around the eyes cannot convince police they are a minor.

According to Aru, irregular migrants hope that by lying about their age they will receive different and more lenient treatment. He said they primarily try to avoid being held in a detention center and assume they will be moved to accommodation where everything is provided.

Irregular migrants in Rae municipality

In an ERR radio program, Indrek Juss, senior specialist at the Social Insurance Board, spoke about 30 possible minor irregular migrants who arrived at the Rae municipality detention center. By law, the municipality must provide guardianship for them. On Wednesday, the municipality asked the Social Insurance Board for assistance.

Juss said that the unaccompanied minors are believed to be from Ethiopia and Eritrea. Most are older than 16. Their native language is Tigrinya, and communication takes place through two interpreters. First, Tigrinya is translated into English, then into Estonian.

Aru said that age becomes an issue when a minor has no accompanying adult. First, a legal representative must be appointed, which is a local government employee. Once a legal guardian is in place, other necessary parties are involved and the procedures begin.

In addition to determining the country of origin and identity of possible unaccompanied minors, their actual age must also be established. Aru said that the PPA believes the majority of those claiming to be unaccompanied minors are not actually minors.

Age is difficult to determine

He said that this is not a situation where the assessment is based on the opinion of a single police officer. An expert commission participates in the assessment, consisting of a PPA expert, a local government representative, a Social Insurance Board representative, a psychologist and a medical professional.

All of these experts speak with the individuals claiming to be unaccompanied minors. After that, an assessment is formed regarding what the person's actual age might be.

Aru said that the first interviews have taken place, but it is too early to discuss results. The expert commission is still forming its assessments, which must then be formally documented.

Juss said that cases like the one in Rae municipality differ from typical child protection cases. The Social Insurance Board has scheduled meetings with the Ministry of Social Affairs and Rae municipality, which will take place in the near future.

World.title: Tallinn Fringe Festival gets underway next week with biggest program yet
World.content:
The annual Tallinn Fringe Festival (TFF) turns 10 next week and will mark it by bringing its biggest program yet.

The festival, featuring international comedians, cabaret, burlesque and theater across venues in Tallinn, mostly in the cultural quarters of Telliskivi and Kalamaja, starts next Tuesday.

What began as a street art festival a decade ago has grown into a key stop on the Nordic-Baltic fringe circuit, drawing performers from as far afield as Iceland and the U.S. and bringing the inevitable comparisons with the famous Edinburgh Fringe Festival.

TFF is Estonia's only open-access, multi-genre performing arts festival, and this year runs from August 18 to September 18. The events bring together local and international artists and will feature more than 80 shows across genres including circus, dance, music, burlesque, visual arts and theater, and organizers note that as artists work directly with venues rather than being selected by a committee, this leads to a diverse lineup.

Organizer and blues and cabaret performer Kaisa Ling says the festival has come a long way from its street art origins. "It is the 10th anniversary of fringe in different incarnations. It started out as a street art festival more than anything, but now it has grown organically, and the 10th anniversary is the biggest. If we go with the same tempo, it will become bigger and bigger – I'm not going to say Edinburgh look out! But…" said Ling, who was herself heading off to the Scottish capital for a few days before returning for the Tallinn event's start.

Kaisa Ling. Source: Anton Serdjukov / Tallinn Fringe Festival

That growth has also put Tallinn on the international fringe map. "Some people are actually touring – this is part of the Nordic-Baltic touring circuit. Tallinn is on the map strongly at fringe festivals, and people find it nice to come off the Edinburgh hard work, take it a bit easier here, enjoy the beautiful town, and then continue to other Baltic-Nordic fringes in Sweden, Finland, Iceland," Ling went on.

For the performers, TFF is as much about the audience as the shows. "I'm seeing more and more international artists coming in, and this is my favorite time of the year because I get to visit a lot of shows of people who are not performing in Estonia the other 11 months of the year," said blues pianist and raconteur Rene Paul.

"The Estonian audience is not expecting a show in a cellar to have a touring comedian who is the real deal. This is not some kind of open mic – these are people who are doing it all night every night," Paul went on.

Both Paul and noted comic Sille-Kadri Simer highlighted the festival's growing audience and international flavor.

"New audiences, new faces, new artists, more people coming in. We have so many great acts – each year there's surprises, somebody coming from Iceland, the United States. It's so lovely to see that Tallinn is such a vibrant city for performing arts," said Simer, known as the Estonian Comedy Barbie.

Some of TFF's local talent at a launch event in Tallinn's Raekoja plats. Source: Anton Serdjukov / Tallinn Fringe Festival

"I've done Edinburgh twice. It went pretty well – I have done over 40 shows there and someone shows up every time. Same with Tallinn – so many shows, but all the shows have people," Paul added.

"I hope people can come and see multiple shows – the fringe is all about seeing different genres," Simer noted.

Burlesque is also a major part of the fringe festival's itinerary. Performer Katarina von Schatz told ERR News she brings a different kind of energy to the stage.

"The burlesque community is so safe. Men are afraid of us, because they see we have the power. What I want to bring on stage is that there will be all different sexes, all different bodies – you don't have to be fit, you can look however. Everything is good on the burlesque stage," von Schatz explained.

"We have our own stories – not like in theater where you have to tell other people's stories. We decide how we tell them and we make our own costumes. Sometimes the audience also affects how we tell it – if it's a different room, different vibe, different people, we just get inspiration from that."

Burlesque artist Katarina von Schatz says the art is open to all, including in the 'Boylesque' variant. Source: Anton Serdjukov / Tallinn Fringe Festival

"Daytime I'm home with my three cats and I make costumes (laughs). I love being a full-time artist, I've done it for three years now, I would never go back to work in a bank," von Schatz said of being a full-time performer.

The festival will see stand-up from Estonian and international comedians alike, with shows in both Estonian and English, a mix of Estonian and visiting companies across venues in the Telliskivi creative quarter and Old Town, while the Heldeke! venue in Kalamaja hosts English-language late-night cabarets throughout the month, as it does at other times of the year.

Retaining its street art roots, the festival includes outdoor performances and live music too.

World.title: Ilu-hack, pop-up pood: Estonian-English mixing thrives in compound nouns
World.content:
In recent years, English is finding its way into everyday Estonian mainly through compound nouns, with video bloggers leading the trend, a new study finds.

Tallinn University (TLÜ) linguists Anna Verschik and Helin Kask analyzed texts from more than 40 blogs, 10 video blogs and eight podcasts, examining hundreds of thousands of words to see how younger adults in Estonia mix English into Estonian.

The researchers found clear differences across platforms: video bloggers, or vloggers, mixed languages about twice as often as bloggers in written content and podcast hosts.

Compound nouns accounted for 85 percent of all mixed-language expressions, including terms such as "bomber-jakk" ("bomber jacket") and "trummi-set" ("drumset"). English verbs and longer phrases such as "ära friikima" ("freak out") or "must-have asjad" ("must-have items") were much less common.

English-derived terms also often outcompete their official Estonian equivalents online.

Google searches returned about 3.5 million results for "foto-shoot," ("photoshoot") compared with 173,000 for the recommended Estonian term "fotosessioon." "Auto-trip" ("roadtrip") appeared nearly five times more often than the Estonian "autoretk."

The researchers say speakers may turn to English because it can better convey a particular meaning or emotional tone more naturally. For example, "üli-happy" ("incredibly happy") can sound more casual and expressive in everyday speech than the formal Estonian "üliõnnelik."

Original grammar still intact

Despite the influx of English vocabulary, the researchers found no evidence that language mixing is disrupting the mechanics of Estonian grammar, with English elements generally being adapted to fit within Estonian sentence structure and inflection rules.

The two languages also share a tendency to create new words by combining existing ones, making it relatively easy for native speakers to seamlessly slot English word stems into their Estonian.

The findings were published in the International Journal of Bilingualism.

World.title: Popular Lebanese restaurant Al Beiruti to open in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Al Beiruti, a popular Lebanese restaurant, is set to build its first Iraqi branch in Iraq Mall in Baghdad, adding another significant regional dining name to the capital’s growing restaurant scene.

The Baghdad inauguration will be the next chapter of Al Beiruti’s regional development, after previous launches in Jordan and Qatar, as well as its established presence in the UAE.

The restaurant announced that its Iraq Mall restaurant is about to open, with a local franchise arrangement handling the expansion.

Al Beiruti has become a renowned location for Lebanese food in the Middle East, providing both classic dishes and a more modern restaurant experience.

The menu includes Lebanese favorites, including manakish, fattoush, hummus, baba ghanouj, and grilled halloumi, as well as shawarma, wraps, and mixed grills. Larger meals include steak, chicken escalope, and grilled salmon.

Al Beiruti joins a growing number of international and regional food and beverage companies in Baghdad, as new malls and commercial expansions change the city’s retail and entertainment markets.

Iraq Mall has emerged as a focal point of that expansion, drawing new restaurants, boutiques, and entertainment ideas as consumer spending and private-sector investment continue to rise in the capital.

World.title: Baghdad and Erbil agree on unified digital customs system across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Baghdad and Erbil have agreed to fully adopt the digital ASYCUDA customs system across border crossings, with non-oil border earnings shared equally by the federal and Kurdistan regional governments.

The deal is a significant step toward standardizing customs processes across Iraq and addressing long-standing disagreements over border revenues and claimed import quantities.

ASYCUDA, designed by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), digitizes customs declarations, payments, and clearing processes, allowing authorities to better monitor products entering the nation and the income they earn.

Linking customs operations to Iraq’s banking and electronic payment systems may help limit the potential for underreporting, revenue leakage, and corruption at border crossings.

The deal comes as Iraq’s Finance Ministry and Central Bank work to digitize customs, payments, and government financial data in collaboration with UNCTAD.

A combined computerized customs system for Baghdad and Erbil might give more accurate revenue data while resolving one of the two governments’ ongoing financial issues.

The change is also significant for Iraq’s overall economy.

More open and uniform customs processes might facilitate cross-border commerce, boost governmental revenues, and enhance the business climate as Iraq pursues more foreign investment and closer integration with international markets.

World.title: Iraq’s Chief Justice Faiq Zidan meets Syrian President Al-Sharaa in Damascus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Thursday, marking another high-level Iraqi outreach to a neighboring Arab state as Baghdad seeks to bolster regional relations under rising security problems.

Al-Sharaa welcomed Zidan and an Iraqi delegation to the People’s Palace, which also included Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Justice Minister Mazhar al-Wais.

According to the Syrian president, the talks focused on extending judicial and legal cooperation between Iraq and Syria, as well as resolving mutual concerns.

The visit also resulted in more practical conversations among the two nations’ judicial officials. Iraqi and Syrian authorities agreed to set up joint judicial committees to continue working on cases involving Syrian prisoners and other cross-border legal issues.

Zidan’s visit is crucial as he is one of the most prominent persons in Iraq’s state institutions, and it coincides with Baghdad’s increased diplomatic, security, and judicial interaction with its neighbors.

The Damascus meetings come after a separate Iraqi security group visited Riyadh, where senior military official Abdul Amir al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman.

Zidan had also just visited Ankara as part of a larger Iraqi effort to build ties with Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey.

That approach has become more urgent in light of the regional escalation involving Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

In late July, the United States and Saudi Arabia conducted synchronized attacks against locations used by Iran-aligned organizations in Iraq, after Riyadh accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones against Saudi energy infrastructure.

The incident put Baghdad under strong pressure to prevent armed organizations from exploiting Iraqi territory to launch assaults on neighboring nations and also highlighted the potential that militia activity may harm Iraq’s improved ties with Arab governments.

Against this setting, Zidan’s encounter with Al-Sharaa is significant beyond regular court cooperation.

Iraq and Syria share a long border and confront shared concerns such as terrorism, organized crime, prisoners, and cross-border security. Baghdad also has a strategic interest in preserving stable ties with Damascus, as Iraq strives to boost regional connections and prevent unrest from spilling over its borders.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration sees recent diplomatic efforts as part of a larger effort to strengthen Iraq’s ties with its neighbors while keeping the nation out of the developing conflict between Iran and its regional adversaries.

Baghdad has increasingly emphasized that choices on security, armament, and relations with neighboring governments must be made by Iraqi official authorities rather than armed groupings.

The travels to Damascus and Riyadh therefore convey an essential message: although Iran-aligned militias have exacerbated tensions between Iraq and certain of its neighbors, Iraqi official institutions are working directly with those nations to restore cooperation and avoid further escalation.

Strengthening judicial, diplomatic, and security ties with Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey might serve as an essential regional buffer for Iraq as it seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, control armed groups, and avoid being drawn further into the region’s crises.

World.title: Iraq’s Al-Shammari visits Riyadh to meet Saudi Defense Minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A top Iraqi security team has traveled to Riyadh for meetings with Saudi Arabia’s leadership, as Baghdad and the Kingdom work to improve security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

First Lieutenant General Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman on Thursday to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

According to reports from the visit, the conversations included cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration.

The conference is especially significant in light of the combined US-Saudi attacks on Iran-linked militia locations in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

The strikes drastically escalated tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, highlighting the Iraqi government’s problems in preventing armed groups from exploiting its territory to target neighboring nations.

Thursday’s visit indicates that both parties are now attempting to move beyond that conflict via direct military and intelligence collaboration.

Prince Khalid underlined Saudi Arabia’s commitment to Iraq’s security, stability, and economic growth, identifying it as an essential neighbor with whom the Kingdom has strong political and social relations.

The meetings in Riyadh follow Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali al-Humaidan’s visit to Baghdad last week, during which he met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and reiterated an offer for the Iraqi leader to visit Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad’s security cooperation with Riyadh has grown more vital as the government seeks to prevent Iran-backed militias from drawing Iraq into a larger regional conflict.

Al-Zaidi has frequently said that Iraqi soil should not be used to attack other nations and has stepped up efforts for weaponry to be put solely under state control.

The most recent Iraqi trip to Riyadh symbolizes more than just normal defense diplomacy. It is part of a joint effort by Baghdad and Saudi Arabia to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into conflict.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: 40 queries in Census Phase-II: Caste, bank accounts, Covid jabs...
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The second phase of Census 2027 â involving population enumeration â will, for the first time, capture caste âas declared by the respondentâ among its 40 fields, which include new ones such as number of bank accounts, place of Covid vaccination and voter card number.

Enumeration by caste will not delve into whether it falls under the other backward classes (OBC) category. However, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes will be enumerated as earlier.

The questionnaire notified Friday shall also seek name of spouse, parentsâ particulars and nationality â elements captured by the National Population Register (NPR) exercise undertaken alongside Census 2011. NPR updation was, however, delinked from Census 2027.

The new fields in the list of 40 questions â up from 29 asked during Census 2011 â also include respondentâs nationality as declared, permanent address, mobile-phone number, Aadhaar number, passport number and availability of driving licence. While mobile-phone number, Aadhaar number and voter ID may be shared if available, passport number is required only from an Indian passport holder.

Sources told TOI that mother and fatherâs particulars are likely to capture their names, date of birth and place of birth.





While these are key factors that determine citizenship/nationality, their capture will have no impact on individuals since individual census data must remain confidential and cannot be used for âlegal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosureâ, as per the govt.

Sources also said giving a drop-down menu for recording OBC status was not found feasible because states have different castes categorised as OBCs and a mismatch between communities recognised as such by Centre and those at state level.

They also pointed to states expanding their respective OBC lists by adding more castes â something that could have created logistical problems once census was under way.

Officials told TOI that unlike the socio-economic caste census conducted in 2011 â which had returned around 46 lakh castes, making it unusable â the digital mode of Census 2027 and availability of modern, AI-based tools can surmount compilation and segregation challenges.

Also, full confidentiality of an individualâs caste declaration is guaranteed by Census Act.

TOI was the first to report on Aug 4 that the Phase 2 questionnaire shall capture caste âas declared by respondentâ, and, in a first, also capture parentsâ date and place of birth.

Phase 2 is due to start in UT of Ladakh and snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of J&K, Uttarakhand and Himachal on Aug 17. For the rest of India, it will resume in Feb 2027, culminating in the population headcount with March 1, 2027, as the reference date.

World.title: Savarkar remark: Supreme Court quashes case against Rahul Gandhi
World.content:
Noting that there was no sanction to prosecute leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Gandhi for his remarks against V D Savarkar,

Friday quashed proceedings against him initiated by a Lucknow court.

Rahul had allegedly described Savarkar as a "receiver of pension from Britishers" and "a servant of Britishers" at a news conference in 2022.

SC, which had given an earful to Rahul at the last hearing, concluded that criminal proceedings against him were untenable for want of sanction. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu allowed Rahul's appeal on the ground of lack of sanction, even before senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi could argue the case on behalf of the Congress MP.

World.content:
Rahul had claimed Shahâs hand in police excesses against student protesters.

Taking cognisance of two BJP MPsâ complaints against Rahul Gandhi for levelling âdefamatoryâ allegations against home minister Amit Shah, Lok Sabha secretariat has sought the leader of the oppositionâs reply to Speaker Om Birla by Aug 28. The MPs, Sanjay Jaiswal and Anurag Thakur, had filed separate complaints to Birla, accusing Rahul of violating parliamentary rules during his speech in the House on July 30.Rahul had claimed Shahâs hand in police excesses against student protesters. Official sources said Birla would decide whether to ask the Houseâs privilege committee to look into the allegations or close the matter after taking note of Rahulâs response.

World.title: Be mindful of strong India-Italy ties, says MEA after Rahul's jibe at Modi & Meloni
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs Friday urged everyone to be mindful of strong India-Italy ties and the need to be respectful to each other. The remark followed a controversy over Congress member of Parliament Rahul Gandhi as well as party neta Sandeep Dikshit's jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on foreign policy that involved Italian PM Giorgia Meloni.

"We have strong ties with Italy. Our ties with Italy in recent years have expanded and strengthened in every which way, and it's important that, as part of diplomatic practice, we strengthen our ties, keeping in mind being respectful of each other. There's mutual understanding between the two sides," said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.

At an event Thursday, Rahul had ridiculed Modi's handling of foreign policy. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha said it had somehow been ingrained in Modi's mind that foreign policy was all about hugging leaders. He then hugged Dikshit in a bid to demonstrate what govt's foreign policy was about. "Imagine the ignorance... where did he get the idea...?" he said.

Dikshit then said to Rahul, "Ek cheez pooch sakta hoon? Meloni samajh ke toh nahi pakda tha?" Rahul responded, "I have not reached there yet."

World.title: Public exams to become more transparent, secure and trustworthy: President Murmu
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Referring to students as âarchitects of Indiaâs futureâ, President

Friday said govt is undertaking comprehensive steps to reform the public examination system to âcompletely curbâ the use of unfair means, make it more transparent, secure and trustworthy for the youth.

âJust as govt and society must remain united to ensure national security, everyone must contribute through joint and concerted efforts to safeguard the present and future of our students. Public exams become gateways to opportunities for our students,â Murmu said in her address to the nation on Independence Day eve.

Noting that 65% of Indiaâs population is below the age of 35, she said, âThis young population is our most valuable asset.â

In a first, the full version of national song Vande Mataram â recently accorded the same legal status as national anthem â was played ahead of and at the conclusion of Murmuâs address. It was followed by the national anthem. The President recalled the pivotal role played by the national song during Indiaâs freedom struggle.

In her address, the President highlighted that âthe youth of our country are talented, committed, and skilledâ.





âI have seen the innovative and practical solutions that young people are developing to address various challenges at the grassroots level. This reflects the dedication of our youth to society and the nation. A new phase of space exploration has been ushered in through the recent successful rocket launch by a young team with an average age of just 28 years,â the Murmu said.

âOur younger generations strengthen my faith in Indiaâs bright and prosperous future,â she added.

The President also emphasised that physical and mental wellbeing of our youth forms the cornerstone of our countryâs future. âFamilies and society also share the responsibility to motivate our youth to move ahead with enthusiasm,â she said.

World.title: In response to Pak PM Sharif, J&K CM Omar says IWT sucked ‘our blood’, calls for its cancellation
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Pakistan Prime Minister

warned at an event in Islamabad on Friday that Pakistan would take any step to protect its water rights under the

, saying âevery single dropâ of Pakistanâs water is a âred lineâ and âIndia must come to the right pathâ or it would âbe given a direct responseâ. His comments drew a reaction from

chief minister

Omar Abdullah

who said the treaty has been kept in abeyance and should remain so.

âYes, our blood. We have been saying this only, that our blood has been sucked. Thankfully Shehbaz Sharif came to his senses. This (IWT) has sucked the blood out of us. These are our rivers. We have the first right on them,â Omar told reporters here. âFor the sake of saying, Pakistanis say that they are great sympathisers of Kashmiris. But when it comes to water, their sympathy disappears. Where was his sympathy when our permission to use our rivers was taken away from us,â the CM said.

âOut of the six rivers, three which belonged to Punjab were kept by India and our three rivers were handed over to Pakistan. From then till today we are suffering the consequences of this Indus Waters Treaty,â Omar said, adding that under the treaty J&K could neither extract drinking water from the Chenab nor use the Jhelum for irrigation or building a barrage at Tulbul. âOur blood has been sucked and now the IWT has been cancelled.





This should remain cancelled so that we can use this water properly,â Omar added.

The IWT was signed between India and Pakistan in 1960. Under the treaty, India received full rights to use the waters of the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan received rights over the three western rivers, Indus, Chenab and Jhelum.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India placed the treaty in abeyance last year following the Pahalgam terror attack.

In May last year, after the treaty was placed in abeyance, Omar called for restarting the Tulbul Navigation Project on Wular Lake in north Kashmir. The project is located on Wular Lake in the Sopore area of Baramulla district. Pakistan has opposed construction of a 439-foot-long, 40-foot-wide barrage, also known as the Wular barrage or Tulbul Navigation Project, with a navigation lock on the lake.

The Union govt began work on the project in 1984 to regulate water levels and facilitate navigation. However, work was halted a year later after Pakistan objected. Pakistan raised the issue with the Indus Waters Commission in 1986 and work was stopped in 1987.

The governing National Conference in J&K has opposed the IWT all along, calling it detrimental to the interests of the people of Jammu and Kashmir.

World.title: Strong 7.7-magnitude quake strikes off Indonesia: USGS
World.content:
A strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early on Saturday (August 15, 2026), the U.S. Geological Survey said.

The epicentre of the quake was located off the north coast of the island, about 68 km northwest of Ende, USGS said. The quake struck at a relatively shallow depth of just 10 km.

The initial quake was followed by two strong aftershocks in the same area, of magnitude 5.6 and 5.9.

Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) warned of the possibility of tsunami waves being generated by the quake.

Indonesia and neighbouring countries experience frequent earthquakes due to their location in the Pacific “Ring of Fire” -- an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.

World.title: Four arrested in Mumbai in connection with ₹30 crore Ponzi, multi-level marketing scheme
World.content:
The Economic Intelligence Unit (EIU) of the Economic Offences Wing of the Mumbai Police arrested four in connection with a company called AI Origin/Digital Origin on Thursday (August 13, 2026) and Friday (August 14, 2026), allegedly running a Ponzi/Multi-Level Marketing schemes and collecting over ₹30 crore in cash.

A case was filed under the relevant BNS Sections and the BUDS Act. Section 318(4) penalizes cheating (up to 7 years imprisonment), and Section 3(5) enforces joint liability for common intent. Under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes (BUDS) Act, Sections 21 and 23 punish running, soliciting, or accepting unregulated deposits (ranging from 1 to 7 years imprisonment plus heavy fines), while Section 26 fines non-compliance with reporting mandates.

According to the police, the directors of the company, Shrikrishna Pandurang Chavan, Chairman & Executive Director, Ankush Shantaram Parte, Executive Director, and Subhash Yashwant Pandere, Executive Director, along with agents and others, were accepting illegal investments, even in the form of cash, promising continuous, fixed returns of 5-7% monthly, without obtaining any license/registration from the Reserve Bank of India or the Securities and Exchange Board of India.

People were allegedly lured by the illegal investment schemes via their website AIOrigin.in, through various WhatsApp groups, and in-person seminars organised across various districts in Maharashtra. The company, which has been running for a year also allegedly published s promising additional returns through a ‘member joining’ mechanism.

This mechanism allegedly involves asking the investor to give the company ₹1,500 after which they will give the investor an app called ‘UPPI’ from which they can access their returns. However, they can only access their returns from the app after sharing the scheme to other people. For each person inducted to the app, the investor gets ₹3 to ₹5, which means they would need at least 70-80 people. They can then access the app after getting ₹500 on it.

They even allegedly took 60 of their agents on a paid trip to Thailand to recruit other people into their investments scheme. The company had already allegedly been working with over 3,000 investors.

The EIW also found that new offices of the company are allegedly operational in Thane, Palghar, Pimpri-Chinchwad, Sangli, and Kolhapur, and their operations were being run through agents in the states of Karnataka and Goa as well. Satara and Solapur offices were to be started on August 16th.

The police raided the offices of the alleged company in Vasai West in Palghar, Goregaon East and Malad East in Mumbai.

They even seized ₹12.08 lakh in cash, nine bank accounts’ passbooks, one BMW Motor Car, one Verna Car, and seven laptops/desktops.

The EIU investigation is ongoing.

World.title: J&K administration says no work from home order for Pandits in Kashmir; CM Abdullah says ‘a credible threat cannot be taken lightly’
World.content:
Even as the J&K administration on Friday (August 14, 2026) refuted any work-from-home orders for Kashmiri Pandits working in Kashmir, the community has approached the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) to “probe how personal data of Prime Minister Package Employees in Kashmir was leaked” and made it to a purported terror threat letter online. J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said “a credible threat cannot be taken lightly”.

Rakesh Handu, a Pandit social activist, said he was in touch with the six Pandit employees whose names and mobile numbers figured in the threat letter online and “were shifted to Jammu”.

Mr. Handu, on behalf of Kashmiri Pandit PM Package employees, has submitted a representation to the NHRC and NCM. “For the last few days, threat letters and lists are again circulating. These lists contain name, department, place of posting, and personal mobile numbers of PM Package employees. This is not isolated. Similar lists were published by Kashmir Fight / TRF (The Resistance Front) blog in 2022 (56 employees) and 2023 (57 PM Package teachers),” said Mr. Handu, in the letter.

He pointed out that after the targeted killings of Rahul Bhat, Rajni Bala post-2019, “many of Pandit employees had submitted en mass resignations citing threat to life”.

“When a religious minority serving the Government is openly threatened, named, and told not to hoist the national flag, it is a test of human rights and minority rights in a democracy,” reads the letter.

The letter demanded a FIR and probe by the police’s Cyber Cell and the National Investigation Agency. “There should be an immediate security audit of all PM Package employees and transit camps, especially before 15th August celebrations. Till threat assessment is complete, allow work from home or attachment to Jammu,” it added.

Meanwhile, Divisional Commissioner, Kashmir, Anshul Garg on Friday (August 14, 2026) said no order has been issued asking Pandit employees to work from home. “The administration has made necessary security arrangements for employees, residents and the general public ahead of the Independence Day celebrations in Srinagar. We should rely on the authentic information channels that are provided by the government and the administration,” said Mr. Garg.

Reacting to Mr. Garg’s statement, Mr. Handu sought clarification from the J&K administration and said, “Why are these contradictory statements coming from Honourable Divisional Commissioner Kashmir?”

Meanwhile, J&K CM Abdullah said militancy may be declared “finished.” “But a credible threat cannot be taken lightly. Those responsible for security must act decisively, identify those behind it, and ensure foolproof protection,” said Mr. Abdullah.

World.title: Uttar Pradesh aspirants waiting merit list plans protest outside recruitment board, flags prolong delay
World.content:
Candidates of Village Panchayat Officer (VPO) examination who are waiting for the final merit list, announced on Friday (August 14, 2026) of organising an indefinite protest outside Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Service Selection Commission (UPSSSC) from August 17, if the merit list is not released and questioned the commission for the delay.

“Our final merit list/result of Village Panchayat Officer (VPO) is pending since roughly three months, the prolonged delay is adversely impacting our lives, hence we decided again to meet the authorities at UPSSSC, and start our indefinite protest outside the recruitment board office from August 17, the poster has been circulated among shortlisted candidates,” said Ravi Pandey, an aspirant shortlisted in mains examination. He added, candidates are in touch with each other through social media applications. Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, a Prayagraj based outfit of competitive government recruitment examination aspirants, also extended support to the candidates.

“We will hold the Commission accountable, this prolonged delay is a criminal act as precious years of young people are getting wasted, every job aspirant in U.P. Stands with VPO candidates, the Board and government is playing with lives of young people,” added Pankaj Pandey, who is associated with Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch.

Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) is recruitment agency entrusted for direct recruitment to all such group C and D posts as may be specified by the State Government by notification. Village Panchayat Officer (VPO) for 1,468 posts were notified on May 16, 2023 by the UPSSSC. Candidates roughly 40 times the available vacancy are shortlisted for VPO Mains examination based on Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET) score.

World.title: Unmarked proforma being served to West Bengal madrasas by police seeking details of foreign funding, visitors
World.content:
West Bengal started serving an unmarked proforma across the madrasas, mosques, and idgahs across the State seeking details of foreign funding source, foreign visitors, and also the distance of the premises from the international border.

The incident sparked an outrage by the madrasa and mosque authorities while a group of human rights activists also submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Director General of Police Siddh Nath Gupta seeking an immediate inquiry into the matter and clarification for such survey.

The said proforma distributed by police in multiple madrasas across districts such as Barrackpore, Birbhum, Malda, Murshidabad, Haroa, North and South 24 Parganas, the authorities of these religious organisations have been asked at least 26 questions under a title ‘Proforma for survey of Madrasah’ or ‘Proforma for survey of mosque/ idgah/ mazar’.

Apart from their name, address with GPS coordination, categorical affiliation, ownership, registration number, photograph of the premises, number of staff and students, these questions include the source of foreign funding, the details of the foreign visitors in the last three years, any foreign exchange programme of students being run currently, and the distance of the prmeises from border areas.

The information regarding any legal dispute over the premises, FIR or chargesheet filed against any staff, and political affiliation of any staff, faculty, or alumni have also been sought in the questionnaires.

The survey is being run by the police and the Department of Minority Affairs of West Bengal. However, what rose concerns among the people and the activists that the proforma does not bear any reference to any related government notification, name of the issuing authority, official stamp, seal, memo or order number, date, or any specific legal provision under which the survey is being conducted.

The staff from several madrasas and mosques also reported that the police served it late at night and also often engaged in heated exchange with the locals. At around 12 a.m. on August 12, a team of police personnel including the inspector of Nimta Police Station in Barrackpore visited the Masjid Baitul Muazzam and a nearby madrasa to serve the form and asked to submit all the details at the police station by next morning, said a staff Jahangir Ali.

In Birbhum’s Lohapir Jama Masjid, three civic volunteers from Nalhati Police Station served the proforma on August 6 for all the mosques and madrasas to one mosque head, Azizur Rahman. “When we objected, they said it is part of a regular survey. We also asked for the government notification, seals, and issuing authority names. They didn’t respond anything but said we must submit all the details within a day. However, we all have decided not to submit it now until they serve a professional proforma with a government notification attached to it,” said Mr. Rahaman.

The Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR), West Bengal Chapter, has expressed concern over survey forms being handed over to the committees of mosques, madrasas, Idgahs and mazars in different parts of the State.

“Such an exercise, particularly when it involves sensitive information concerning religious institutions, should be carried out only on the basis of a clear and identifiable government order and under a defined legal framework. At present, the copies of the forms available with APCR do not clearly mention any Government Notification, Memo Number, date, issuing authority or specific legal provision under which the information is being sought. The question is therefore simple and legitimate: If these forms have been issued under an official government or police order, why has that order not been made available to the concerned institutions and the public?” said the secretary of APCR, Umar Awais.

The acitivists also expressed their concerns over the purpose of the government to conduct this survey. It stated that hat the statewide survey of madrasas initiated by the Department of Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education is a separate matter. The existence of a government-approved madrasa survey cannot, by itself, establish the authority for every separate police form or for the collection of additional sensitive information.

In their letter to the CM and DG, they also urged to maintain the transparency of such survey in which the government asked a slew of sensitive information. “However, such exercises must be transparent, lawful and non-discriminatory and must not result in profiling or selective targeting of any particular religious community. If this is an official government survey, let the government order be made public. If it is a police initiative, the authorities must clearly state under which law and for what purpose such sensitive information is being collected from religious institutions,” it said.

DG Siddh Nath Gupta did not respond to the calls. However, Birbhum SP Vidit Raj Bhundesh said that he has no knowledge about the survey. The inspector of Nimta Police Station in Barrackpore, Rahul Deb Mondal admitted that he served the proforma to some local madrasas but refused to comment further on the development.

World.title: Nagaland church body opposes Vande Mataram singing
World.content:
GUWAHATI

The Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) has opposed the Centre’s order to play or sing the revised version of Vande Mataram, the National Song, at official events to mark India’s 80th Independence Day.

The church body’s opposition follows the Naga Students’ Federation’s call to ensure that schools and other educational institutions do not send their students to participate in the Independence Day programmes. The students’ body also said students who decline to sing Vande Mataram “on grounds of conscience or religious beliefs” should not face disciplinary action or discrimination.

In a statement on Thursday (August 13, 2026) evening, the NBCC said it was against any directive or practice that seeks to compel citizens, particularly Christians, to sing Vande Mataram. It maintained that patriotism should arise from willing participation and a shared love for the nation rather than compulsion.

At the same time, the church body called upon all stakeholders to express their positions peacefully and constructively, cautioning that disagreement over national symbols or patriotic practices should not become a source of communal tension or social division.

The NBCC said it fully respects national symbols, patriotic sentiments, and the constitutional values of India. However, it insisted that matters concerning faith, conscience, religious conviction, and deeply held identity require “the highest degree of sensitivity, wisdom, and respect.”

“National unity cannot be strengthened by compelling citizens to participate in an expression that, for reasons of faith or conscience, they may not be able to embrace,” the NBCC said, reminding the Centre that India was a plural and diverse nation.

“India’s unity will be strongest when every citizen, irrespective of faith, community, culture, or conviction, can say with confidence that there is a rightful place for them in the nation and that their conscience will be respected,” it added.

World.title: Thousands participate in Tiranga Yatra in Bihar, Jharkhand
World.content:
Thousands of people joined the Tiranga Yatra celebrating national pride and unity. Students and the general public participated in the ‘Tiranga Yatra’ in both Bihar and Jharkhand.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary led the Tiranga Yatra in Haveli Kharagpur as part of the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign-2026 in Munger district. Carrying the Tricolour and chanting “Bharat Mata Ki Jai”, the participants conveyed a message of national unity, integrity, and patriotism. Mr. Choudhary paid tributes by offering flowers and garlanding the statues of the late Nandalal Bose, Baba Saheb Ambedkar and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Ministers of the Bihar Government, MLAs, MLCs, and social and political activists were part of the procession. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Choudhary said that the Tricolour is a symbol of the country’s unity, integrity, and pride.

“The ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign is a significant initiative aimed at fostering respect for the nation, patriotism, and a sense of national unity among citizens,” Mr. Choudhary said.

He called upon the people to transform this initiative into a true mass movement.

Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai also participated in the Tiranga Yatra from the Mohiuddinnagar Assembly constituency to the Morwa Assembly constituency within the Ujiarpur Lok Sabha constituency.

Hundreds of party workers and youths participated in the procession, riding motorcycles and carrying the Tricolour in their hands, while chanting slogans of “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and “Vande Mataram.”

Mr. Rai said that, following the call of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ initiative has evolved into a powerful campaign driven by public participation.

Also after the meeting of Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLD) district presidents, party supremo Upendra Kushwaha, Bihar Government’s Panchayati Raj Minister Deepak Prakash, MLAs Alok Kumar Singh and Snehlata Kushwaha, and other state office-bearers participated in the Tiranga Yatra in Patna.

Jharkhand Leader of Opposition and former Chief Minister Babulal Marandi also participated in the Tiranga Yatra organised by the BJP in Medininagar (Daltonganj). Palamu MP B.D. Ram, Chatra MP Kalicharan Singh, MLA Shashi Bhushan Mehta were also present along with the district president and party workers.

Similarly, the 209 CoBRA Battalion (CRPF) organised a motorcycle Tiranga Yatra to foster patriotism, national integration, and respect for the Tricolour. Led by Commandant Sorabh Bhatnagar, the rally showcased the force’s unwavering commitment to national pride.

​Starting from the Battalion Headquarters (Khunti district), the motorcycle convoy carrying the National Flag travelled through Tupudana Chowk (Ranchi) to Bridgeford School, ODM Sapphire School, Kalamati High School, and PM Shri Kasturba Gandhi Vidyalaya (Kalamati). At each stop, the rally received a warm and enthusiastic welcome from students, educators, and the public.

CoBRA personnel interacted directly with students, distributed National Flags and chocolates. The troops also spoke regarding civic responsibilities, the paramount importance of national unity, and proper respect for the National Flag.

​On the other hand, nine police officers from Jharkhand have been selected for the President’s Police Medal on the occasion of Independence Day 2026, including the President’s Medal for Distinguished Service (PSM) to Shailendra Kumar Sinha, IPS, Inspector General of Police, Bokaro.

The Bihar Police has also been awarded the prestigious President’s Colour Award this year. Bihar DGP Vinay Kumar said that 18 police personnel from Bihar will be awarded by the President.

They will be awarded in three different categories of gallantry medal, meritorious medal and distinguished service medal, while seven police personnel will be awarded by ₹51,000 by the State government on the occasion.

World.title: Former Trinamool MLA Nirmal Ghosh mobbed outside police station
World.content:
KOLKATA

Former Trinamool Congress MLA Nirmal Ghosh was mobbed outside a police station on Friday (August 14, 2026). A day back, he was arrested from Odisha for his alleged involvement in the ‘hurried’ cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim’s dead body.

Mr. Ghosh was attacked right outside the Khardah Police Station as he was being escorted by the police to produce him at the Barrackpore Court in North 24 Parganas. He was wearing a helmet, but he was still subjected to physical attack, some threw eggs and muck, sticks, bricks, some also threw kicks and slaps. Many protestors carried garlands made of shoes.

The police tried to cover his head with a helmet to avoid any injuries during the transit. Mr. Ghosh was mobbed with “chor, chor“ (thief, thief) slogans outside the Barrackpore Court.

He was sent to 8 days police custody. He has also been accused in another case for allegedly stealing lottery prize money.

“Police promptly arrested the accused from another State. I appreciate the CP Barrackpore for their work,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Friday (August 14, 2026).

Commenting on the attack, Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned the incident. “This cannot happen. How can the police allow this? The arrested person has not been convicted,“ Mr. Kunal Ghosh said. He also accused the police of being complacent in the attacks.

Nirmal Ghosh aide attacked

A former Trinamool councillor, Sanjib Mukherjee, a neighbour of the RG Kar victim in Panihati area, was also subjected to similar treatment. He was also being taken to court because he was allegedly present during the cremation of the victim’s body and was also known to be a close aide of Mr Ghosh. Mr. Mukherjee was also arrested on Thursday (August 14, 2026).

Mr. Ghosh, a former MLA from Panihati, also served as the chief whip of the Mamata Banerjee government. His son, Tirthankar Ghosh had fought the Assembly polls from Panihati and lost to the mother of the RG Kar victim Ratna Debnath.

Series of attacks on leaders

The attack on Mr. Ghosh is among the series of attacks that many Trinamool leaders have been subjected to in the past three months. After the Trinamool’s loss in the 2026 Assembly elections to the BJP, many of their current and former leaders, MLAs, former Ministers, and Councillors have been mobbed. Angry masses have raised slogans against them, hurled eggs, bricks, many were heckled, and some were also thrashed in public since May 4.

Among the top leaders, Trinamool chairperson and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, MLA Kunal Ghosh, and many others have come under attack. Mr. Abhishek Banerjee was one of the first leaders, who was showered with eggs and physically abused by the mob, after which the attacks have been consistent on the others.

Trinamool Congress leaders have repeatedly blamed the BJP for these attacks. However, BJP leadership has denied all such allegations.

The Calcutta High Court had also raised questions about the role of the State’s administration and the police for not being able to ensure the safety of the leaders.

World.title: PM Shehbaz briefs President Zardari on Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called on President Asif Ali Zardari in Islamabad on Friday and briefed him on a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.

For his part, President Zardari “expressed his best wishes for the effective implementation of the tripartite agreement with regard to defence cooperation, regional peace and stability and promotion of the security of the Muslim ummah”, the Presidency’s statement on its X account said.

He also appreciated PM Shehbaz’s and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts for “further strengthening the longstanding fraternal relations between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan into a robust strategic partnership”, the statement added.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 in Makkah, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia will form political and military mechanisms under the defence pact , Turkiye’s defence ministry said on Thursday, adding the alliance would also deepen defence industry cooperation.

Both Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Dar have said the pact is defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it is also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan.

Meanwhile, Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

Counter-terrorism also discussed

Apart from discussions on the Makkah pact, “the professional capabilities of the security forces and law enforcement agencies in operations against Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were appreciated” during Friday’s meeting, the statement by the Presidency said.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan, and Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

The meeting’s participants reiterated the “resolve to eradicate the scourge of terrorism” from the country, the statement said, adding that foreign and interior affairs were also discussed.

President Zardari also emphasised “the need for effective measures to provide relief to the people” in light of the current regional situation. He also stressed the need for “uninterrupted supply of essential commodities and their availability at reasonable prices”.

He “expressed the hope that Pakistan’s effective diplomatic efforts for the promotion of regional and global peace would further strengthen the country’s international standing, and that its positive impacts would be reflected in the national economy and the lives of the people”, the Presidency’s statement said.

The meeting was also attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan and Senator Sherry Rehman.

World.title: Petroleum dealers postpone planned strike as govt approves margin revision
World.content:
The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers’ Association (PPDA) on Friday called off its plans to begin a strike on Saturday after the government approved a proposed revision in the dealers’ margins.

The nod for the revision was also confirmed by the finance ministry in a statement.

The Economic Coordination Committee had “deliberated on the matter regarding revision of dealers’ margins on motor spirit and high-speed diesel” during a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on a public holiday, the statement said, adding that a revision of the margin had been approved.

The statement did not specify the increase in the margin but a senior official told Dawn that the margin had been increased by Rs1.34.
